Back at the shrine, Kokomi took Tsumi to be the last Vassal of Watatsumi (Orobashi's half-serpent familiars), rejected Enjou's theory that she was one of the "vishap-people" (Reptilians: vishaps that imitate humans and differ only in their vertical pupils) as pure fiction, since Watatsumi's ancient documents say nothing of them, and resolved to find a way to stop the soil bleaching that would not keep disturbing the vishaps.

49.content:
Evernight Temple (also: Tokoyo Reibyou): The Evernight Temple is a subarea of Enkanomiya, the sunken ancient land reached from beneath Watatsumi Island. It is a ruined sacred site where a faintly glowing stream, the Tokoyo Reisen (once called the River Lethe), runs close by. Offerings, hidden rooms and spectral figures from old Byakuyakoku are scattered through it, among them a fragment of the dead inventor Aberaku.

Enkanomiya shifts between "Whitenight" and "Evernight" with the Dainichi Mikoshi, and some barriers, rooms and spirits at the temple exist only in one phase. Its Japanese name is written 常夜霊廟; the wiki glosses it as "Evernight Mausoleum".

Geography: Enkanomiya lies under Watatsumi Island and is entered through a deep pool east of Sangonomiya Shrine once the seals on the five Goshou Rocks are broken. The Evernight Temple is one of its subareas, a glide down from the eastern teleport waypoint of the Dainichi Mikoshi. It holds an Elemental Monument, Triangular Mechanisms, Places of Essence Worship and Seelie, and its local specialty is Sea Ganoderma. A quiet coral-ringed open space near the temple is one of the sitting spots in a hidden objective.

Doors, lanterns and barriers are tied to Enkanomiya's day-night mechanisms: the Daises of Day and Night, Triangular Mechanisms that are struck to move things, and essence-worship sites that carry one phase's power into the other. Secret rooms are opened by switching between Whitenight and Evernight and working these in order.

Places: The Tokoyo Reisen, the stream beside the temple, marked as its own point of interest. A secret room, reached by following the traces of Bathysmal Vishaps, which holds one fragment of the Reins of Revival. The precinct where part of Aberaku's remains (his "sacred crown") was enshrined.

People: There are no living residents. Spectral figures appear in Evernight: the spirit of Aberaku, who calls himself Helios-Forger, and seven Sunchildren (Ion, Isumenasu, Orupeusu, Piramumon, Rikoru, Risutaiosu and Surepio), who can be spoken to only in Evernight and vanish afterwards. The Sunchildren were child figureheads of old Byakuyakoku, ruled through by a cabal of nobles.

The Sunchildren talk about ordinary things. Ion reads fortunes and admits that he softens bad readings; Isumenasu dismisses the Traveler's map as a fraud because Byakuyakoku could not be that small; Orupeusu has sworn not to sing until he hears Clymene's voice; and Piramumon, delighted that other lands exist, mentions the Rite of Solar Return he must attend. Treat them as wistful afterimages, not as living children.

History: Enkanomiya (earlier Byakuyakoku, Tokoyokoku, and originally Delphi Pytho) sank into the sea in the war of funerary flame and was cut off from the surface. Its people held off the Dragonheirs of the Depths, now called Bathysmal Vishaps, with the Dainichi Mikoshi, the artificial sun Aberaku built. Corrupt nobles later set up child Sunchildren as puppet rulers; Aberaku, who opposed them, was imprisoned on the first Sunchild's accusation and died in captivity, and his clothes and body were enshrined in several places. The crown was kept at the Evernight Temple. Orobashi later overthrew the Sunchildren and led the survivors up to the surface.

Aberaku's spirit, scattered by these separate enshrinements, cannot rest. At the temple he recalls being held somewhere very high, dark and cold, and cannot say why a high place should feel wrong to him. The offerings left here carry a trace of his thoughts.

Dangers: Hilichurls, samachurls, slimes and Anemo Specters; Electro, Hydro and Pyro Abyss Mages; Primordial Bathysmal Vishaps and hatchlings; Thundercraven and Rockfond Rifthound whelps; Ruin Guards, Ruin Graders and Ruin Destroyers. Damaged mechanisms can be repaired by switching phase.

Atmosphere: Dark stone beneath a lightless sky, lantern and sigil glow, a stream that shines faintly in the dim, and ghostly figures who speak briefly and are gone. It is a place of memory more than of life.

Quests: Temple Inquiry (Hyperion's Dirge): Aberaku's spirit-trial is passed here and the Offerings of the Temple are collected. The Trail of Drake and Serpent (From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku): Vishap traces lead to a secret room and a fragment of the Reins of Revival. Sunchildren Hide and Seek: a hidden objective unlocked after The Phaethons' Syrtos. Lotus Eater: the Waters of Lethe are drawn from the Tokoyo Reisen.

Another hidden objective, Reading Kabayama's Lanterns, uses a sitting rock in the coral-ringed space near the temple as one of its three viewpoints.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple stands unchanged in Enkanomiya, explorable and empty of living people. Nothing newer than its 2.4 content was found.

Enkanomiya itself is little known outside Inazuma; when the Traveler mentioned it to Wriothesley in Fontaine, he had to ask what it was.

50.comment: Evernight Temple: Tokoyo Reisen and the Waters of Lethe
50.content:
The Tokoyo Reisen is a stream at the temple, once called the River Lethe. Its water shines faintly and does not by itself make a drinker forget, but the Dragonbone Orb, a rare fruit that a Dragonbone Flower bears when watered with it, calms the mind and sweeps worries away. In the Lotus Eater quest Adonis, a student of the resistance leader Supada no Hiko (called Spartacus), says remnants of the resistance sold the orbs to fund their cause; many fighters then lost their will to resist, and he wonders if the formula was planted by the nobles who ruled through the Sunchildren.

The orbs are made by watering the flower with the stream's water and waiting for it to condense. Supada no Hiko is himself only an afterimage held in the altar at the Serpent's Heart; Adonis learns from the Traveler that his master is trapped there.

51.comment: Evernight Temple: Aberaku at the Evernight Temple
51.content: In the Temple Inquiry, Aberaku's spirit calls himself "Helios-Forger" and does not remember how he died, only that a child ordered his imprisonment and that he feels no hatred for that child, who was a puppet. He asks the Traveler to defeat the monsters that act as warders of his spirit, and hands over the Offerings of the Temple, which hold part of his thoughts. His speech keeps breaking off mid-thought.

52.comment: Evernight Temple: The Sunchildren of the Temple
52.content: The Sunchildren (Phaethons) were child figureheads of Byakuyakoku after the Dainichi Mikoshi was built; a cabal of corrupt nobles used them as puppets and let them take the blame for harm done in their name. When a Sunchild reached a certain age the Rite of Solar Return ended that Sunchild's life, so they could not realise they were being manipulated. Rikoru was the first Sunchild. In the Sunchildren Hide and Seek objective seven of them are found as afterimages at the temple. Describe them factually and gently: lonely children of an unjust system.

53.comment: Evernight Temple: Reins of Revival at the Temple
53.content: In The Trail of Drake and Serpent the Traveler follows Bathysmal Vishap traces at the temple, defeats whelps guarding a mechanism, opens the secret room by switching phases, and collects one of three fragments of the Reins of Revival. The other two come from Dreams in the Gaps and The Heart of Ouroboros; together they continue The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent, which leads to the Golden Bridle used elsewhere in Enkanomiya.

54.content:
Fort Fujitou (also: Fujitou-toride, Wisteria Helmet Fort): Fort Fujitou is a Watatsumi Army camp on Yashiori Island, where soldiers of the Sangonomiya resistance, led by Sangonomiya Kokomi, held ground against the Shogunate's forces. It sits among thunderstorms and the Tatarigami-stricken land of the island. The Traveler meets the officer Kaida Ryouma and the blacksmith Miyazaki Saburou there, and a man named Kaji who starts the Orobashi's Legacy quests.

The Japanese name means "Wisteria Helmet Fort". After Kokomi's story quest the background soldiers leave the camp, and by then the resistance has become a peace-keeping and rebuilding body.

Geography: On Yashiori Island, beside the electric weather of the island, with an Electro Cube, Electro Rock Pile, Electro Seelie, Narukami Pillar, Thunder Barrier and Thunder Sakura Bough around it. Local specialty: Crystal Marrow.

The island's storms come from the Tatarigami released when the wards of the Electro Archon were destroyed; fixing the wards in Orobashi's Legacy calms them.

People: Kaida Ryouma is a Sangonomiya officer who used to work for the Kujou Clan and fought against them. Miyazaki Saburou is a swordsmith from Tatarasuna, a successor of the Miyazaki Art, who joined the Army for protection and forges its arms. Others include the samurai Moriguchi, Nathan and Takahashi, and the workers Sumi and Yuuzou. Kaji moves to the Kujou Encampment after Orobashi's Legacy.

Ryouma says the Army trails the Shogunate's elite troops but must believe it can win; after the war he is grateful for Kokomi and Gorou and wonders what became of his old Tenryou Commission. Saburou says Kannazuka is disputed ground, "the hill where no gods reside", and tells the Traveler about Orobashi.

Governance: Military camp run under Kokomi and General Gorou. Kokomi is the leader; Gorou is the general; Ryouma is an officer. The Army is called "rebels" by the Shogunate.

History: During the Vision Hunt Decree war, the camp was a staging post for the resistance. Kaji arrives there to look into the Yashiori storms, which he ties to the destroyed wards and the remains of Orobashi. After the Traveler persuades the Raiden Shogun to change course, the Decree ends, and peace talks begin; Ryouma says soldiers there are glad, and the Army keeps order and helps rebuild.

Miyazaki Saburou's account of Orobashi and the Electro Archon's battle explains why Yashiori Island lies in ruin and how Fort Mumei came to be. See Orobashi's Legacy and the entry on Fort Mumei.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Nobushi and Kairagi, Treasure Hoarders, slimes, Mirror Maidens and Crackling Axe Mitachurls; the Tatarigami weather of the island.

Atmosphere: Rain, thunder, tents and forge-smoke; soldiers worn down by war, with a note of relief once it is over.

Quests: Orobashi's Legacy (Kaji's quests, Parts I to V) begins here; Kokomi's story quest Warriors' Dreams Like Spring Grass Renewing ends the war's aftermath.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the camp is still a Watatsumi Army site, though quieter, since the Vision Hunt Decree ended and soldiers moved on to peace work.

55.comment: Fort Fujitou: Kaji and Orobashi's Legacy
55.content: Kaji, a man at Fort Fujitou, investigates the island's endless rain and lightning, which he believes comes from destroyed ancient wards linked to the slain Orobashi. The Traveler repairs wards at Musoujin Gorge, Serpent's Head and Jakotsu Mine; Fort Mumei then rises from the sea and the final ward is restored.

56.content:
Fort Hiraumi (also: Hiraumi Fort, Hiraumi-toride, Flat Sea Fort): Fort Hiraumi is a subarea at the eastern tip of Seirai Island, the Inazuman island scarred by a long-ago calamity and a perpetual thunderstorm. It is a fort-like site on the island, roamed by Nobushi, Kairagi and Treasure Hoarders and home to the Slumbering Court, a domain. The in-game map calls it Hiraumi-toride.

Nothing in the game text says who built the fort or what it once guarded. What canon shows is its present state: a stormy, lightning-charged place with Electro puzzles, Thunder Sakura Boughs and Phase Gates, with an abandoned mansion on its grounds that the domain description calls the haunt of monsters from the rift.

Geography: The fort lies on Seirai Island, the island whose centre was once wrapped in constant storm and Balethunder until the Seirai Stormchasers quests were completed. Electro runs through the whole area. Features listed for the subarea include Electro Cubes, Electro Seelie, Lightning Strike Probes, light-up tile puzzles, Thunder Barriers, Thunder Sakura Boughs, Phase Gates, a Waverider Waypoint and bake-danuki. Local specialties include Amakumo Fruit, Naku Weed and Sea Ganoderma.

One of the Seirai Stormchasers' Warding Stones is reached from Fort Hiraumi: the Traveler enters a Phase Gate south of the fort's southern Teleport Waypoint and climbs floating stones to a waypoint where the stone waits. This is a quest-time route: the floating rocks that carry the player up are despawned during Part IV, which finishes the series.

Places: The main landmark is the Slumbering Court, the domain on the fort's grounds. Its official description calls it a masterless mansion that has become the haunting ground of rift monsters, and it rewards those who master its Electro trial with artifacts. A cat-shaped hidden objective, "The Cat's Affection" (an unofficial name), is located to the right of the domain and needs the recipe from the quest Neko Is a Cat: Shrine Recipe.

In "The Cat's Affection" the player feeds the Delicious Invigorating Kitty Meal to a cat on a paw-shaped rock once a day. After each daily reset the kitten shifts to the next toe, and on the last day it produces a chest. The recipe for the meal comes from Kiminami Anna through Neko's tasks to revive the Asase Shrine.

People: There are no named residents. The area is held by Nobushi (Hitsukeban, Jintouban and Kikouban), Kairagi, Treasure Hoarders, Hilichurl Shooters and Mirror Maidens among the elite enemies.

Dangers: Electro Slimes and Whopperflowers, Nobushi and Kairagi patrols, Treasure Hoarder gangs, specters, Crackling and Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Mirror Maidens and Ruin Machines (Ruin Cruisers and Scouts). Lightning-charged terrain and Thunder Barriers shape how safely anyone can move.

The Daily Commission "A Gentleman Strikes in Broad Daylight" has a Fort Hiraumi version in which the Traveler must filch supplies from a Treasure Hoarder camp west of the waypoint; the commission "Operation Thunderous Ignition" starts at the island's eastmost tip, where Kairagi appear and the Thunder Dwellings can be used to charge Electro attacks.

History: No history of the fort itself is given. The island around it is said to have suffered a calamity that left its centre in a perpetual thunderstorm.

Before the Seirai Stormchasers quests, the centre of the island was constantly afflicted with Balethunder and targeted lightning, and exploration at the edge was hampered by storms.

Travel: Fort Hiraumi has a Teleport Waypoint and a Waverider Waypoint. Fort Hiraumi and Seirai Island were added in version 2.1.

Quests: The fort appears in the Seirai Stormchasers world quest series (Part III's Warding Stone route), the Neko Is a Cat shrine recipe chain, the commissions mentioned above, and a Torn Page, "Toki Alley Tales (III)", whose location is listed as east of the fort.

Atmosphere: Electro everywhere: lightning probes, Thunder Barriers and Thunder Sakura Boughs, with hostile patrols and the shadow of the haunted mansion nearby. It is an island that bears the marks of a calamity and a storm that raged for a long time.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Fort Hiraumi is an open, hostile exploration area on Seirai Island; the wiki records no change since 2.1.

57.content: The Slumbering Court is an Electro-themed domain on Seirai Island. Its in-game description calls it a masterless mansion that has become the haunting ground of monsters from the rift, and says those who can wield the eternal lightning to conquer its trial will win artifacts. Thundercraven Rifthounds are among its enemies, and Electro-Charged is the effective way to fight them. The domain's own page is the place for its gameplay detail; the lore tie to the fort is not explained.

58.content:
Fort Mumei (also: Mumyou-toride, Fort of Ignorance): Fort Mumei is a group of ruins on Yashiori Island, remains of an ancient, majestic city that fell in the Archon War when the serpent god Orobashi invaded the island and clashed with the Raiden Shogun's forces. It lay under the sea until the Traveler finished the Orobashi's Legacy quests, when the fort rose out of the water near Watatsumi Island.

Its name means "ignorance" (the Buddhist avidya) in Japanese and sounds like "nameless". The small islets nearby were often used as transit points for supplies going to Watatsumi Island.

Geography: A cluster of ruined structures on Yashiori Island near Watatsumi Island, ringed by islets. Features: Electro Seelie, a Light-Up Tile Puzzle, a Narukami Pillar, a Thunder Sakura Bough, a Waverider Waypoint, a sword hilt (from the quest Put Them To Rest), a Handy Notepad, and Sea Ganoderma. Enemies are Hilichurl Fighters, Pyro Hilichurl Shooters, Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Ruin Destroyers and Ruin Scouts.

After Orobashi's Legacy is completed, the fort stands raised out of the sea. A Maguu Kenki guards the last, largest ward there.

History: Late in the Archon War, Orobashi invaded Yashiori Island and came into conflict with the Electro Archon (Beelzebul, the Raiden Shogun), which destroyed the ancient city. The Archon slew Orobashi, splitting the island and leaving the Musoujin Gorge, and set wards to hold down the Tatarigami, the slain god's lingering hatred.

When the Watatsumi Army rebelled against the Shogunate, rebel soldiers attacked Fort Mumei and destroyed the Electro Archon's wards on Yashiori Island, unleashing the Tatarigami. Another account says a radical faction acting without Kokomi's knowledge did this in disguise, hoping to restore Orobashi's dignity.

Dangers: Tatarigami-driven storms; Ruin Machines; Mitachurls; and, in the quest, a Maguu Kenki guarding the final ward.

Atmosphere: Wet grey stone and drowned halls, heavy with the sense of an ended age; thunder over a battle site.

Quests: Orobashi's Legacy, Parts IV and V (with Kaji): the fort rises from the sea, and the last ward is restored. The Kokomi quest Sword, Fish, Resistance mentions the ruins as a supply route near Watatsumi.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruin stands above water and the island's Tatarigami weather has calmed with its wards repaired.

59.comment: Fort Mumei: Orobashi and the Battle of Yashiori
59.content: Orobashi no Mikoto, the Watatsumi Omikami, led its forces to Yashiori Island near the end of the Archon War and fought the Electro Archon. The Archon killed it with the Musou no Hitotachi, splitting the island and creating the Musoujin Gorge. Its lingering hatred became the Tatarigami, held back by the Archon's wards. Watatsumi's people kept worshipping Orobashi.

60.content:
Hanamizaka (also: Flower-Viewing Slope, Hanamizaka district): Hanamizaka is the suburb of Inazuma City on the north side of the river that cuts through the city's northern part, one of the city's three parts alongside Tenryou and Tenshukaku. It is a district of family workshops and shops: the Naganohara fireworks shop, Amenoma Smithy, Kiminami Restaurant, Yae Publishing House and the Bantan Sango detective agency. Its name means "Flower-Viewing Slope".

Compared with the commercial street of Tenryou it feels more residential and artisan. It is where a firework-maker, a master bladesmith, a restaurant owner, a pair of detectives and a famous publisher are neighbours, and where the Shogunate's bulletin board carried everything from official notices to graffiti and complaints.

Geography: Hanamizaka lies north of the river through the north of Inazuma City, on Narukami Island. Amenoma Smithy stands at the city's eastern end, in the eastern suburb; the western outskirts hold quieter homes and a few city watchmen. The Hanamizaka bulletin board stands north-east of the city's northern Teleport Waypoint.

Canon describes the three parts of the city only briefly. Hanamizaka is the suburb, Tenryou the commercial heart below Tenshukaku, and Tenshukaku the Raiden Shogun's castle at the top. The Naganohara Fireworks Show is watched from Amakane Island, from which the whole of Inazuma City can be seen.

Places: Naganohara Fireworks: the Naganohara family's shop, run by Yoimiya's family, called by an Inazuman named Takami the oldest and one of the best in Inazuma. It also sells small toys and trinkets, some imported by the Crux fleet and some made by Yoimiya.
Amenoma Smithy: the workshop of the Amenoma Art, one of the five bladesmithing schools of the Raiden Gokaden. Amenoma Tougo owns it; his disciple Hajime handles ordinary ironware and weapons.
Kiminami Restaurant: owned by Kiminami Anna, with a menu notice advertising a new dish from abroad.
Yae Publishing House: the great publisher founded by Yae Miko, with editors in the suburb.
Bantan Sango Detective Agency: Ryuuji and Sango's agency, taking missing persons, lost pets, deliveries and procurement.

The Bantan Sango Agency advertises its readiness to catch even bandit leaders if the price is right. Yae Publishing House runs the "This Novel Is Amazing!" competition and lists Yae Miko herself as editor-in-chief. The fireworks shop's own board carries a fire-brigade notice scolding Yoimiya's risky behaviour and threatening to report her to the Yashiro Commissioner. Its by-products can be mixed with plant extract to make scentless candles.

People: Notable residents of the eastern suburb: the firework-maker Naganohara Ryuunosuke, the bladesmith Amenoma Tougo, the detectives Ryuuji and Sango, and the editors Shigeru and Kuroda of Yae Publishing House. City watchmen (doushin) such as Andou and Amano and the yoriki Kurosawa Kyounosuke patrol the suburb on behalf of the Tenryou Commission.

Yoimiya, who runs the shop's festival work, is the best-known figure here, and the Naganohara Fireworks Show is her family's craft. The vendor Hajime and the restaurateur Kiminami Anna also trade here.

Governance: Hanamizaka falls under the Shogunate's city administration. Order is kept by the Tenryou Commission's watchmen; festivals and ceremony fall under the Yashiro Commission, which created the first fireworks show.

During the war of the Vision Hunt Decree, the Shogunate's bulletin board in Hanamizaka carried agent notices praising the Decree, Tenryou Commission notices enforcing the Sakoku Decree, and rental or sale notices for the property of fugitives. Vandals and critics posted replies that the Commission answered in turn.

Culture: Hanamizaka is where Inazuma's festival craft lives: fireworks launched for the Naganohara show, forged blades and the novels on sale. People associate fireworks with what matters to them (friendship, marriage, belief), and families pick their own fireworks through paper slips supplied by the Naganohara family.

The fireworks show began over a century ago as a commemorative display by the Yashiro Commission with expert pyrotechnicians; as fireworks spread, families took part and it became a tradition. One year Kamisato Ayaka asked Yoimiya to shape the display so that, from Tenshukaku, it formed the Electro Mitsudomoe, the Shogun's emblem. Yoimiya has said that fireworks, which vanish in a flash, are the opposite of the Shogun's ideal of eternity, but that the feelings people attach to them last.

History: Canon gives Hanamizaka no founding story. Its notable history comes from the Archon Quest era: during the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees the suburb's bulletin board and smithy notices show the war's effects, such as the stalled supply of Jade Steel, and Arataki Itto's public quarrel with the Kujou tengu.

The notices from that time included a complaint that crime, smuggling and forged papers were rising, which officials answered as lies. After the war ends, those first sets of messages are replaced, and the Decrees are gone.

Atmosphere: Narrow, busy streets of wooden shopfronts and noren curtains, the clang of hammers from the smithy, the smell of the restaurant, children buying marbles and tops, and paper notices on boards. Evenings are alive with festival preparations.

Quests: Yoimiya's story quest "Together Under the Fireworks" and the Naganohara Fireworks Show; the Tatara Tales world quest, which interrupts the Jade Steel supply at Amenoma Smithy; "This Novel Is Amazing!" at Yae Publishing House.

Travel: The Hanamizaka bulletin board stands near the city's northern Teleport Waypoint. Amakane Island is the place to watch the fireworks.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Hanamizaka is an ordinary peaceful suburb; the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees are over and the shops are open.

Yoimiya's family runs the fireworks shop and show as before. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 plot touches the suburb.

61.comment: Hanamizaka: Naganohara Fireworks and the Fireworks Show
61.content:
Naganohara Fireworks is the shop of the Naganohara family in Hanamizaka, said to be the oldest and one of the best in Inazuma. Yoimiya, the family's firework-maker, even had the Crux fleet fire fireworks overseas to spread its name. The shop also sells knickknacks beloved by children and adults: Scatterbloom Marbles that bloom when they strike each other, Leaping Tops that chirp like birds, Neon Dragonflies that change colour in flight, and Katydid Coils that repel mosquitos.

The Naganohara Fireworks Show is held at festivals through the year. The Naganohara family prepares fireworks for each family that takes part, with paper slips containing the recipes. Over a century ago the Yashiro Commission began the show as a commemoration. Imatani Saburou proposed to his wife at the show fifty years ago, and Takami of the Yashiro Commission helps run it from Amakane Island.

62.content:
Amenoma Smithy is a smithy on the eastern end of Inazuma City, in Hanamizaka. Its master, Amenoma Tougo, practises the Amenoma Art, one of the five bladesmithing schools of the Raiden Gokaden, and in his old age accepts only orders for exquisite Jade Steel swords and knives. Everyday ironware and ordinary weapons are handled by his disciple Hajime.

Tougo says there is nothing mystical in the craft, only practice day after day until body and mind absorb every motion. The Art tries to imitate the patience of water turning stone to sand. During the war, a notice at the smithy apologised that the Jade Steel supply had stalled and asked customers for their understanding.

63.content:
Yae Publishing House is a giant of Inazuma's publishing industry, founded by Yae Miko, chief priestess of the Grand Narukami Shrine, who is also its editor-in-chief. It runs a contest named "This Novel Is Amazing!" and is famous across Teyvat. It publishes light literature, and the best-selling Liyue novel "A Legend of Sword" is serialised there.

The publisher has tried to hire Albedo for his art. Its staff includes editors Kuroda and Shigeru, event manager Aratani, and columnist "Ms. Hina". During the war, the Grand Narukami Shrine announced that its reader forum would welcome readers from both Shogunate and rebel territory, because Yae Miko treated a common hobby as a reason for equal treatment.

64.content: A small detective agency in Hanamizaka, staffed by the detectives Ryuuji and Sango. Its board advertises investigation of missing persons, missing pets, marital questions, commercial commissions, procurement and delivery.

65.content: The Shogunate's Hanamizaka bulletin board carried a first set of notices that is replaced once Sangonomiya Kokomi's first story quest is completed. Those notices include a praise of Kujou Takayuki for implementing the Vision Hunt Decree quickly, sales of fugitives' property, arrest warrants, and Arataki Itto's challenges to the Kujou tengu, which he blames for taking his Vision. The messages were put up before the war's end and describe a city under strain.

66.content:
Higi Village (also: Scarlet Tree Village): Higi Village is a small village on Yashiori Island in Inazuma, whose main export was Crystal Marrow. The war between the Watatsumi Army and the Shogun's Army, and then the Tatarigami curse of the serpent god Orobashi, emptied it. Most residents fled, died or were sacrificed; the chief Washizu, once a kind man, went mad, while a boy named Chouji tries to sell Crystal Marrow to leave.

The village's secret is grim: Washizu drew passing travellers into praying at his shrine, then tried to kill them as sacrifices to the voice in his head. The Traveler kills him in self-defence after several days of prayer. The pharmacist Yasumoto and the samurai Inaba Kyuuzou disappear along the way.

Geography: Higi lies on Yashiori Island in Inazuma. A Statue of the Seven stands on the northeastern side of the village, and the viewpoint for Serpent's Head, which lies southeast of the village, can be found inside it. The shrine at which Washizu keeps watch stands in the village, and Jakotsu Mine lies nearby.

Local plants include the Naku Weed, which is steeped in Tatarigami energy. Thunder Sakura Boughs and Electro Seelie are found here, as are Kairagi and Nobushi (rogue samurai) who prowl the village. A Bake-Danuki can be found too.

Places: The village shrine, the chief's house, the pharmacist's house, Jakotsu Mine (where Chouji lives) and the central tree.

Items found around the village include the Incomplete Register, Washizu's list of the dead and sacrificed; the Incomplete Notes; Yasumoto's Pharmacist's Notebook; and the Sword Hilt tied to the quest Put Them To Rest.

People: Washizu: village chief, now deranged. Yasumoto: pharmacist, student of the late Naoko. Chouji: a boy selling Crystal Marrow near Jakotsu Mine. Chouji's mother and father: both gone from the village.

Before the Tatarigami, Washizu is described as a kind man who set up shrines to pacify Orobashi's soul and welcomed outsiders; he is mentioned in the Teyvat Travel Guide as having greeted the traveller Alice with a feast. Naoko, the village pharmacist, went mad and died after being locked up. "Uncle" Onitaka's pirates have a symbiotic relationship with the village.

Governance: Washizu governed as village chief with help from the village's pharmacists. Under the Shogunate, officers regularly visited to prevent the village from siding with the resistance and to take its Crystal Marrow, the main export, for the war.

Early in the war Washizu pooled the villagers' wealth and shared it equally, setting a part aside for the local pirates, and decided to guard the shrine as his duty. His notes complain that neither the Shogunate nor the Watatsumi Army cared about the village beyond propaganda.

Culture: Higi's way of life revolved around Crystal Marrow, a crystal containing a sliver of Tatarigami power that makes smelted metal stronger and tougher, and around shrines to quiet Orobashi's soul.

Some of the sick fled to the local pirates for help. The "medicine" of lavender melon and sugar soup that Yasumoto made was a comfort rather than a cure.

History: The village was one of the places worst hit by the Watatsumi Army-Shogun's Army war: constant losses, officers commandeering Crystal Marrow, refugees from Jakotsu Mine and a shortage of food. According to the wiki, when Orobashi fanatics in the Watatsumi Army broke the wards over Yashiori, the Tatarigami returned and the villagers fell sick or went mad. Many fled; some joined the pirates.

Washizu began recording the dead in a register, then became unstable and began sacrificing villagers and outsiders to the voice he called "Him". Chouji's mother, whom he named as special to this god, escaped with the pirates to Sumeru, hoping that the Akademiya could cure her fever and bleeding. The villagers told Chouji his father had died; the pirates' diaries imply he left after recovering and chose to vanish.

Atmosphere: A hush hangs over empty houses under a persistent storm. Crystal Marrow is found near the mine, pages of notebooks are scattered about, and the chief sits muttering at the shrine.

Dangers: The Tatarigami: illness, hallucinations and madness; the enemies who roam the village; the chief Washizu, who attacks those who pray too long; and pirates around Nazuchi Beach. Anyone without a Vision is at greater risk of the curse.

Quests: Washizu's Prayers, Sinister Instruction, Gazing Three Thousand Miles Away (Chouji), Put Them To Rest, Pay Your Respects, and the Hidden Exploration Objective Tatarigami Investigation Expedition.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Higi Village remains largely abandoned; Washizu is dead and the curse has not been lifted.

Chouji has set out to find his parents, Yasumoto is missing and the chief is dead. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content revisits it.

67.comment: Higi Village: Washizu and the Outsider Shrine
67.content:
Washizu was Higi Village's chief and a kind, welcoming man until the Tatarigami drove him mad. He took to praying at a shrine and urged strangers to join him, leaving rewards at their doorsteps. Over several days the Traveler prays with him, and on the last he tries to stab them, defeated in combat. His notes show he had been sacrificing villagers and passersby to a voice he calls "Him", using their belongings to lure others.

He accused Yasumoto of being a fraud, locked up the pharmacist Naoko and another man when they went mad, and listed the sacrificed in the Incomplete Register. After failing to recapture Chouji's mother, he turned to the Traveler, whom he recorded as a "Nameless Outlander".

68.content:
Chouji is a boy who lives near Jakotsu Mine. After the village emptied and his mother left, he began selling Crystal Marrow to travellers at inflated prices to earn the Mora to leave Yashiori and search for his parents. He is serious beyond his years, bargains sharply, and is wary of both Washizu and Yasumoto. The Traveler helps him mine; in return he teaches how to cook Imported Poultry and asks them to learn about his mother at the local shrines.

He believes his mother left without him and thinks his father is dead; neither is true: the Tatarigami flowed freely in his mother, who left for Sumeru with the pirate Onitaka in search of a cure, and the pirates' diaries imply his father left under the curse's influence.

69.comment: Higi Village: Chouji in the Puppy Union Roster
69.content: During the limited-time event Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness, Shikanoin Heizou's Puppy Union admission details list Chouji among the children rescued from the warzone, under the codename Weasel Thief No. 12, and give his age during the war as eight. This is a wiki summary of event text. He is a child; treat him factually and never romantically.

70.comment: Higi Village: The Tatarigami on Yashiori
70.content:
The Tatarigami is the curse formed from the will and power of the serpent god Orobashi after Ei slew him on Yashiori Island, kept in check by wards. When the wards fail it causes thunderstorms, withering plants and untreatable illness. Victims suffer bleeding, fever, rashes, migraines, dizziness, hallucinated voices and madness, and Vision-holders are less affected.

Some people resist it: Chouji and Yasumoto show no symptoms, and Chouji's mother stayed clear-headed while ill. Crystal Marrow, found on Orobashi's bones, carries a sliver of the power.

71.content:
Inazuma (also: Nation of Eternity, Inazuma Archipelago, Land of Eternity): Inazuma is the island nation of Eternity off the far east of Teyvat, near the Dark Sea. Its god is the Electro Archon Raiden Ei, the Raiden Shogun. For centuries a deathless puppet (the Shogun) ruled in her place while her mind meditated in the Plane of Euthymia. The Shogunate governs from Inazuma City and the castle Tenshukaku on Narukami Island, with daily affairs run by the Tri-Commission. Inazuma is a land of cherry blossoms, red maples, thunderstorms, shrines, swordsmanship, and youkai living alongside humans. It was recently closed off by the Sakoku Decree, while the Vision Hunt Decree seized its people's Visions. Both decrees are now repealed.

Inazumans revere the Shogun as an unchanging god and have only recently begun to know Ei as a person. Watatsumi Island still worships its own slain god, Orobashi.

Geography: Inazuma has six main islands. Narukami holds the capital, the foreigners' port of Ritou and Mt. Yougou. Kannazuka has the Mikage Furnace. Yashiori is split by Musoujin Gorge. Watatsumi, with Sangonomiya Shrine, lies farthest from the capital. Seirai is storm-wracked and Tsurumi fog-bound. Enkanomiya lies under the sea beneath Watatsumi.

The islands are what survived a great flood after the war of funerary flame. Orobashi raised most of Watatsumi from his own coral near the end of the Archon War. Kannazuka is "the hill where no gods reside," claimed by neither faith. Thunder Sakura trees, grafted from the Sacred Sakura, draw filth from the land, and Electro barriers and storms mark old seals and wounds.

Government: The Raiden Shogun rules from Tenshukaku through the Tri-Commission. The Tenryou Commission (Kujou Clan) handles the military and security. The Kanjou Commission (Hiiragi Clan) handles finance and the borders. The Yashiro Commission (Kamisato Clan, under Kamisato Ayato) oversees shrines and festivals. The Grand Narukami Shrine under Guuji Yae Miko answers to the Archon, not to the Shogunate. Watatsumi is largely governed by its Divine Priestess, Sangonomiya Kokomi.

The Tenryou and Kanjou commissioners, Kujou Takayuki and Hiiragi Shinsuke, collaborated with the Fatui. Both were removed and arrested, and neither has an official successor. Kujou Kamaji and Hiiragi Chisato serve as acting clan heads, and the tengu Kujou Sara commands the Shogunate's forces.

Religion: Devotion to the Electro Archon is far more visible in daily life than in Mondstadt or Liyue. The Grand Narukami Shrine guards the Sacred Sakura and performs its Cleansing Ritual. Watatsumi reveres Orobashi as the Watatsumi Omikami, which the Shogun permitted after his defeat. Few people know that "Baal" was originally two gods: Makoto, the first Archon, and Ei, her kagemusha (body double), who took her titles.

History: The twin gods Makoto and Ei won the archipelago in the Archon War. Their conquered youkai helped humans found a city by the sea, and Ei slew rival gods such as Orobashi more than 2,000 years ago. In the cataclysm 500 years ago Makoto died in Khaenri'ah. Fearing "erosion," Ei pursued Eternity: about 400 years ago she left the Shogun puppet to rule, sealed her mind in the Plane of Euthymia, and gave the Electro Gnosis to Yae Miko. A year before the Traveler came, the Fatui manipulated two commissions into the Sakoku and Vision Hunt decrees, which provoked a civil war with Watatsumi.

The Traveler, Yae Miko and the Watatsumi resistance confronted Ei and ended the Vision Hunt. Ei then redefined Eternity and lifted Sakoku (2.5). Older layers of history include sunken Byakuyakoku (Enkanomiya), Tsurumi's Thunderbird tribe, and Ei's killing of the Thunderbird about 1,500 years ago.

Culture: Youkai such as kitsune, tengu, oni and bake-danuki live among humans, though few remain and most keep to themselves. Swordsmanship and honour are central, and a Duel Before the Throne before the Shogun is fought to the death. Light novels flourish, and the main festivals are the Summer Festival, the Irodori Festival and the Mikawa Flower Festival.

Economy: Sakoku crippled trade, and the economy has been recovering since the reopening. Exports include printed books (Yae Publishing House), kimonos, toys and Naganohara fireworks. Swords forged from Jade Steel made at the Mikage Furnace were long famous.

Foreign relations: The Fatui of Snezhnaya engineered the decrees to obtain the Electro Gnosis; Signora was executed after losing a duel to the Traveler, yet diplomatic ties continue. Liyue's Crux Fleet ran the blockade. Inazuma lies close to the Dark Sea and has fought many wars against what comes from it.

Dangers: Ronin (Nobushi, Kairagi), Treasure Hoarders, the Tatarigami on Yashiori, lingering Electro storms, Fatui agents, Abyss Order activity around Enkanomiya, and Abyssal filth that gathers under the Thunder Sakura.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Inazuma is at peace and open. The Vision Hunt is over and the Visions have been returned, Sakoku is lifted, a ceasefire with Watatsumi holds, and Ei takes a more direct part in governing.

The Electro Gnosis is now in Fatui hands. The Archon Quest has since moved on to other nations, up to Snezhnaya (Chapter VII, 7.0-7.1). At the close of 7.1, after Ronova destroyed a Celestial Nail in Snezhnaya with Eitr, the other Nails across Teyvat began emitting pillars of light, and unusual activity was reported on Tsurumi Island, where a Nail is believed to have fallen. Yae Miko went to see for herself after drawing a "Great Misfortune" fortune slip; she senses a faint power there and means to bring Kokomi to look at it. What the phenomenon means is not yet known.

Watatsumi keeps its army as peacekeepers while talks on its status are paused.

72.comment: Inazuma: The Tri-Commission and the Shogun's Army
72.content:
The three commissions meet at Tenshukaku, and any one of them can block the others' proposals: during the Vision Hunt the Tenryou and Kanjou repeatedly vetoed the Yashiro's motions to repeal it. The Tenryou Commission is the Shogun's executive arm for security, war and policing, and enforced both decrees. The Kanjou Commission, based at Ritou, manages finance, customs and borders, and was known for harsh treatment of foreigners. The Yashiro Commission, headquartered at the Kamisato Estate, runs shrines, festivals and cultural affairs. It is considered closest to the Shogun and was the only commission that refused the Fatui. The Shogun's Army is the national army, with units serving each commission. The Watatsumi Army, led by Kokomi with Gorou as general, is a separate force. The Shuumatsuban are a covert ninja corps answering to the Yashiro Commissioner.

After the decrees fell, Takayuki was placed under house arrest and Shinsuke imprisoned for their part in the Fatui plot. Takayuki had fed the Shogun false reports, and Shinsuke had supplied Crystal Marrow for Delusions. When a commissioner falls, lesser clans such as the Takatsukasa may move against the leading clan. In Reflections of Mortality (2.1), Ei offered the Tenryou post through a duel. Takatsukasa Susumu refused out of fear, but Kujou Kamaji accepted although he knew he was outmatched, to let his clan's prestige end with honour. Ei judged him honourable and gave the Kujou more time. The Yashiro's clean record has earned it more sympathy and influence.

73.content:
Humans are the majority, but youkai also live in Inazuma, many descended from races Ei conquered and then took into her service. Yae Miko is a kitsune, Kujou Sara a tengu and Arataki Itto an oni. Samurai families are proud and honour-bound: they send children into the Shogun's service and count defeat, or help from an outsider, as shameful. Anyone with a grievance may call a Duel Before the Throne at Tenshukaku. It always ends in death, and a loser who survives is executed with the Musou no Hitotachi, the peak of Ei's swordsmanship. Inazumans who leave the country to train call themselves shugenja. The national cry is "Glory to the Shogun and her everlasting reign!"

The Summer Festival on Narukami is lit by Naganohara Fireworks, and its owner Yoimiya is called the festival's "Queen." The Irodori Festival honours the ancient poets known as the Five Kasen; Yae Miko revived it as an international light-novel convention after Sakoku. The Mikawa Flower Festival is a youkai revel more than five centuries old that Ei, Makoto, the Kitsune Saiguu and Yae Miko once attended. At the Goshintou Ceremony, master swordsmiths offer their finest blades to the Grand Narukami Shrine. The Warrior's Spirit Swordfighting Exhibition once pitted champions against the Shogun herself and now uses an emissary, most recently Kamisato Ayaka.

74.content: Before the decrees Inazuma's economy was healthy. Under Sakoku few ships braved the storms, imports and exports collapsed, and fishing shrank because the Kanjou Commission treated every boat as a possible escape. Snezhnayan merchants and the Fatui were at first exempt. Publishing is a major trade: the Yae Publishing House is an industry giant and runs the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest. Kimonos, toys and fireworks, mostly Naganohara's, are exported. Crystal Marrow from Orobashi's remains fed the Jakotsu Mine and the Mikage Furnace's Jade Steel. Inazuman blades sold steadily to Fontaine, but the mine closed after a "sickness," and Jade Steel production stopped after the peace with Watatsumi.

75.comment: Inazuma: Fatui Operations and the Electro Gnosis
75.content: Under the Harbinger Signora, with Scaramouche also active, the Fatui corrupted the Tenryou and Kanjou commissions. They pushed the decrees to destabilise Inazuma and create a market for Delusions, and supplied Delusions to the Watatsumi resistance, whose toll killed soldiers who relied on them. Their agent Nathan helped Orobashi fanatics destroy Yashiori's wards. Their goal was the Electro Gnosis. Signora lost a Duel Before the Throne to the Traveler and was executed by the Shogun. Yae Miko had kept the Gnosis since Ei withdrew, and she traded it to Scaramouche in exchange for the Traveler's safety.

76.comment: Inazuma: Narukami Island and Inazuma City
76.content:
Narukami is the political heart of Inazuma and where public festivals are held. Inazuma City was built during the Archon War on cliffs at the island's southern tip. It is the nation's most populous and prosperous city, known for family businesses and low crime, and it climbs from the harbour and Hanamizaka's shops past the Tenryou Commission to Tenshukaku. Mt. Yougou above holds the Grand Narukami Shrine and the Sacred Sakura. The shrine maidens sell omamori and fortune slips, and armed force is forbidden on the grounds. The Kamisato Estate and Chinju Forest, home to bake-danuki pranksters, are also on the island.

The Kitsune Saiguu, the great kitsune who once led the shrine, persuaded Baal to spare the tanuki Ioroi and make him Hidden Protector of Chinju Forest. Centuries of care by kitsune have given the Sacred Sakura its foxlike shape. Abyssal filth absorbed by the Thunder Sakura collects in its roots and must be purged in the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual.

77.comment: Inazuma: Ritou and Entry to Inazuma
77.content: Ritou, the "outlying island" attached to Narukami, has long been the only gateway for outsiders. Hiiragi Hiroshi of the Kanjou Commission built it from a deserted island after the cataclysm, and it is still the Hiiragi Clan's base. Under Sakoku, thunderstorms ringed the archipelago. Outlanders stuck at Ritou needed a hard-won travel permit to go further inland, and Kanjou ashigaru blocked the road. Since the decree was lifted the storms no longer bar the way, and international shops and the International Trade Association fill its maple-shaded plaza.

78.content: Kannazuka was the civil war's disputed front line. The Kujou Encampment, a fortress Kujou Shigeyori built on the cataclysm-era battlefield, faced the Watatsumi forces. Tatarasuna's Mikage Furnace, the nation's largest smelter, made Jade Steel from Crystal Marrow until it malfunctioned during the war. Xavier contained it under a dome, and the Traveler later helped restore it.

79.comment: Inazuma: Yashiori Island and the Tatarigami
79.content:
Yashiori Island holds the skeleton of Orobashi, the serpent god of Watatsumi. More than two thousand years ago he invaded the island. His vassal Akuou killed Ei's friend the great tengu Sasayuri, and in her fury Ei's Musou no Hitotachi killed Orobashi and Akuou together and split the island, forming Musoujin Gorge. Orobashi's resentment became the Tatarigami. Ei sealed it with wards (Narukami Pillars), and the Kitain Clan served as Yashiori Guardians until their line ended in the cataclysm. During the civil war, Orobashi fanatics aided by a Fatui agent destroyed the wards without Kokomi's knowledge. Storms, sickness and madness emptied Higi Village until the Traveler restored the wards.

Kujou Masahito, the general on Yashiori, reported the Tatarigami honestly. His father Takayuki thought he was exaggerating and sent investigators, who confirmed the reports and then went missing themselves. The ancient city of Mumei, which Watatsumi seized in the invasion, was destroyed in the battle.

80.content:
Watatsumi Island lies opposite Narukami, lush with brightly coloured coral and plants. It is home to the Sangonomiya Clan and its Divine Priestess, currently Sangonomiya Kokomi, who rules from Sangonomiya Shrine. Its people descend from Enkanomiya and still worship Orobashi. Relations with the Shogunate stayed cool for centuries and became open war under the Vision Hunt. After the ceasefire, talks on returning the island to Shogunate rule were paused, and the Watatsumi Army now keeps the peace, helps rebuild and is clearing out the Fatui. The island's poor soil is threatened by bleaching "Holy Soil," held back by rituals that need Bloodbranch Coral from Enkanomiya.

Enkanomiya (opened in 2.4), reached through a pool near Sangonomiya Shrine, was once Byakuyakoku and sank into the depths after the war of funerary flame. Istaroth's wind still reached it, and the sage Abrax (Aberaku) built the artificial sun Dainichi Mikoshi to drive off the vishaps. Corrupt nobles then ruled through puppet "Sunchildren" until the fugitive god Orobashi overthrew them, and his coral became his people's ladder to the surface. The Heavenly Principles later sentenced him for reading a forbidden text, and his invasion of Yashiori was partly a way to meet that sentence. When the Traveler recently retrieved coral for Watatsumi, the Abyss Order and Bathysmal Vishaps interfered, and future harvests may fail. Kokomi is now looking for another remedy. The shrine maiden Tsuyuko, trained at the Akademiya, blames seawater salinity for the Holy Soil.

81.content:
About 1,500 years ago the Thunderbird, Kanna Kapatcir, ravaged Seirai Island and ruined the city of Hiraumi. Ei killed her atop Amakumo Peak, and Asase Shrine was built to contain the hatred that lingered as the Thunder Manifestation. Later the shrine maiden Asase Hibiki broke the seals to aid the pirate Ako Domeki's rebellion. The storm that followed shattered the island and forced the Shogunate to evacuate it. Tsurumi Island to the south was the Thunderbird's earlier home. Its tribe revered her; after the boy Ruu was sacrificed to her, she destroyed them and trapped the island in a looping, fog-shrouded day. The Traveler resealed Seirai's storm and helped Ruu's spirit keep his promise to sing for her, which lifted the curse.

Long before the tribe, an older civilisation left vast ruins under Tsurumi, with murals of Celestia on their walls; the researcher Sumida theorises that something, implied to be a Celestial Nail, fell there from Celestia. Ruins and Ruin Sentinels lie under both islands. Seirai has no permanent residents today, and Tsurumi holds only hilichurls, riftwolves and automatons.

82.content: Inazuma's Archon was originally two people. Makoto, the gentler twin, became the first Electro Archon. Ei, the stronger warrior, thought her sister the better ruler and gave up her own body so Makoto could ascend. Makoto remade Ei's body, and Ei served as her kagemusha, so the world knew only one god, Baal. In peaceful times Ei, Makoto, the Kitsune Saiguu, the oni Mikoshi Chiyo and the great tengu Sasayuri gathered for picnics and celebrations before the throne.

83.comment: Inazuma: The Cataclysm and Ei's Pursuit of Eternity
83.content: In the cataclysm Makoto went alone to Khaenri'ah and died there; Ei saved a fragment of her consciousness. At home the swordsman Takamine the Mistsplitter vanished into the darkness. Mikoshi Chiyo, tainted by a "beast of sin" that had swallowed her, turned her blade on Ei and was driven off. The Kitsune Saiguu was consumed, and only fragments of her memory survived as Hanachirusato. On her return Ei found the Sacred Sakura standing on Mt. Yougou, a tree everyone else remembered as ancient, and its power helped her end the disaster. Grief and disillusion with Celestia drove her to seek Eternity, and she founded the Tri-Commission. Her first puppet wept on waking, so she sealed his powers and let him go. After further failures she created the Shogun about 400 years ago, set it to rule by fixed directives, and withdrew into the Plane of Euthymia, a technique Yae Miko had taught her. She largely ignored daily affairs, the Vision Hunt included, which she tacitly approved.

84.comment: Inazuma: The Sakoku and Vision Hunt Decrees
84.content:
One year before the Traveler's arrival, the Shogun sealed Inazuma's borders and ordered every Vision seized and set into the Statue of the Omnipresent God. The plan was the Fatui's. Ei knew they were involved but judged them irrelevant to Eternity. Ninety-nine Visions were taken, and their owners lost their drive and ambition; Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu seemed unaffected. Kazuha's friend challenged the decree in a Duel Before the Throne, lost to Kujou Sara and was executed, and Kazuha fled with the friend's Vision. The Watatsumi Army rose in revolt. The Traveler interrupted a Vision Hunt Ceremony and was defeated by Ei in the Plane of Euthymia. With Yae Miko's help they later showed Ei the wishes held in the seized Visions and defeated her. The Vision Hunt ended, the Visions were returned, and Kujou Sara and Kokomi signed a ceasefire with the Traveler as witness.

The Sakoku Decree outlasted the Vision Hunt for a while, with its restrictions on foreigners eased, until Ei lifted it after Transient Dreams. Since the Vision Hunt began, no new Electro Visions are known to have appeared.

85.content: After the decrees fell, Ei began changing the Shogun's protocols. The puppet had been built never to change and came to see her as an enemy of Eternity. When rifthounds attacked the Sacred Sakura's roots, Ei relived the cataclysm. She fought the Shogun inside Makoto's realm of consciousness, where Makoto's remnant said farewell and left her a Sacred Sakura seed, which took root in Inazuma's past. Under their new agreement Inazuma will not be ruled out of fear of the Heavenly Principles, and Ei honours past sacrifices instead of over-protecting the nation from progress. She treats the Shogun as a partner, not a tool. She lifted Sakoku, and she now walks among her people, who are slowly learning who she is. The Traveler has also performed the latest Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual with Hanachirusato.

86.content:
Inazuma City: Inazuma City is the capital of Inazuma, built on cliffs at the southern tip of Narukami Island. Most of the nation's people live here, and it is Inazuma's liveliest and most prosperous place, known for low crime and a great many family businesses. The city rises in three parts: the suburb of Hanamizaka, the commercial streets of Tenryou, and at the top Tenshukaku, the castle where the Raiden Shogun resides and rules.

The Tenryou Commission, which handles public order, security and the Shogunate's military affairs, has its headquarters inside the Tenshukaku complex. In front of the castle stands the Statue of the Omnipresent God, built as a symbol of Eternity during the Vision Hunt Decree.

Geography: The city climbs from the harbour up the cliffs. Hanamizaka ("Flower-Viewing Slope") is a suburb north of the river that cuts through the northern part of the city. Tenryou lies just below Tenshukaku, a tangle of streets and lanes that all converge before the castle, which stands on the highest point and looks out over the whole of the Shogun's domain. Mt. Yougou and the Grand Narukami Shrine rise inland on the same island; Ritou, the foreigners' port of entry, is also on Narukami Island.

The population keeps growing, so the city expands outward. Simple, easily built houses have spread through the newer districts; families are meant to enlarge them once they have saved enough, though few have managed it in recent years. The outskirts keep an older, unhurried feel along old paths that the city's prosperity has barely touched.

Places: Hanamizaka: Amenoma Smithy (a Raiden Gokaden bladesmithing school), Naganohara Fireworks (Yoimiya's family shop), Yae Publishing House, Kiminami Restaurant and the Bantan Sango Detective Agency. Tenryou: the commercial street with the Adventurers' Guild desk (Katheryne), shops for kimonos, lacquerware, netsuke and groceries, street-food stalls, Uyuu Restaurant, the Police Station, Komore Teahouse and the Aisa Bathhouse. Tenshukaku: the Shogun's residence, the Tenryou Commission Headquarters, the castle's hot springs and the Statue of the Omnipresent God.

Shops named on the street include Ogura Textiles & Kimonos, Yayoi Lacquerware, Netsuke no Gen Crafts, Shimura's and Tsukumomono Groceries. Tomoki's stall sells Dango Milk. The Police Station (Bugyou-sho, "Commissioner's Office") keeps law and order and held prisoners such as the Vision forger Masakatsu. A Meikyou Shisui Art dojo, Domon's, is also in the city.

People: Merchants, craftsfolk, artisans and family-run businesses make up much of the city; doushin and yoriki of the Tenryou Commission patrol the streets, and Hatamoto and Okuzumeshuu guard Tenshukaku. Notable residents or regulars include Yoimiya of Naganohara Fireworks, Yae Miko's editors at Yae Publishing House, the smith Amenoma Tougo, and Katheryne at the guild desk.

The Shogun herself does not patrol: in Ei's words that is the Tenryou Commission's job, and the Shogun has no need of recreation. When Ei walked the market in person (2.1), shopkeepers were startled to see the "Almighty Shogun" in the street. Komore Teahouse's famous "boss" is Taroumaru, a Shiba Inu said to be a former Shuumatsuban ninja dog.

Governance: The city is the seat of the Inazuma Shogunate. The Raiden Shogun governs from Tenshukaku, and the three commissions of the Tri-Commission meet there. The Tenryou Commission keeps order in the city, runs the Police Station and enforced both the Vision Hunt and the Sakoku decrees.

A duel before the throne can be fought at Tenshukaku with the Shogun's approval; its victor is granted a second chance, which is how the Traveler survived their confrontation with Signora. In the days when Inazuman houses were mostly wooden, the Shogun charged the Tenryou Commission with setting up fire brigades; today a Fire Brigade notice outside Naganohara Fireworks warns Yoimiya against further "risky behaviour".

Culture: The city is the centre of Inazuman commerce and popular culture: fireworks, light novels (Yae Publishing House runs the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest), traditional crafts and street food. Komore Teahouse is a members-only teahouse owned by the Yashiro Commission and used by the Kamisato Clan as a private meeting place; guests leave payment in a box. The old Fire-Soothing Festival Committee, once chaired by the Tenryou Commission and managed by the Grand Narukami Shrine, prayed for a year without fires; Yae Miko later turned its festival into a light novel contest and "borrowed" its budget for the Yae Publishing House.

History: During the Archon War, youkai under the banner of Narukami used their powers to help humans who had sought refuge in the mountains build a city by the sea; Yae Miko's story calls this the beginning of Inazuma. Tenshukaku dates from the same war. The Shogun closed the nation with the Sakoku Decree, and about a year before the Traveler arrived she issued the Vision Hunt Decree; the Statue of the Omnipresent God was raised before Tenshukaku to hold the confiscated Visions. In the Archon Quest (2.0-2.1) the Traveler confronted the Shogun at the Vision Hunt ceremony, Signora was executed after a duel before the throne, and the Traveler defeated Ei, after which the Visions were returned.

A tale of the Kitsune Saiguu's era has her goading the bake-danuki Ioroi into plucking a Naku Weed from the Tenshukaku garden, where Ei caught him. About five hundred years ago Lord Hiiragi Hiroshi of the Kanjou Commission gave the Shogun a Snezhnayan blast furnace that heats Tenshukaku's hot springs. The Yae Publishing House is no more than about five hundred years old. After the Sakoku Decree ended (2.5) the city opened to foreign visitors again. By 5.4 the Natlan-inspired Aisa Bathhouse in Tenryou had been renovated with Yumemizuki Mizuki as its core investor.

Atmosphere: The bustle of family shops and street stalls below, the castle looming above. The official viewpoint text describes Tenryou's lanes all gathering beneath the "eternal and silent gaze" of the Shogun. Since the decrees ended the mood is open and busy; under them, Vision bearers were stopped in the street and the Tenryou Commission's patrols set the tone.

Dangers: Inside the city, danger is mostly political or criminal: the Tenryou Commission's enforcement under the old decrees, Fatui intrigue, Treasure Hoarders and petty fraud of the kind the Bantan Sango detectives take on. The countryside beyond has the usual monsters; within the city itself, crime is famously low.

Quests: Chapter II Act I (2.0) brings the Traveler to the city to visit people who lost their Visions; Act II opens with the Vision Hunt ceremony; Act III (2.1) ends with the duel before the throne and the battle with Ei. Many Inazuma story quests are set here, including those of the Raiden Shogun, Yoimiya, Yae Miko, Kamisato Ayaka, Kamisato Ayato, Kaedehara Kazuha, Arataki Itto and Yumemizuki Mizuki.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Inazuma City is peaceful and open. The Vision Hunt Decree was abolished in 2.1 and the Sakoku Decree in 2.5; the Shogun still rules from Tenshukaku.

Ei now takes a more direct interest in her people. The confiscated Visions were removed from the statue and returned to their owners. No new crisis in the city appears in the Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) storylines.

87.content:
Tenshukaku ("heavenly protector tower", the keep of a Japanese-style castle) is the Raiden Shogun's residence and the seat of Inazuma's government, built during the Archon War on the highest point of Inazuma City. The Tenryou Commission Headquarters lie within the complex, guarded by Hatamoto, doushin and yoriki; Okuzumeshuu of the Shogun's personal guard are posted there too. Officials such as a tax secretary and a member of the Royal Bath Commission work in the central courtyard. Duels before the throne are fought here.

Its hot springs are heated by a Snezhnayan blast furnace that Lord Hiiragi Hiroshi of the Kanjou Commission imported as a gift for the Shogun about five hundred years ago. The Shogun's private interior was seen in the Raiden Shogun's story quest (2.1), when the Shogun was indisposed and the Traveler drew Ei out of the Plane of Euthymia.

88.content: Hanamizaka is the suburb north of the river in the city's north, home to Naganohara Fireworks, Amenoma Smithy, Yae Publishing House, Kiminami Restaurant (owner Kiminami Anna) and the Bantan Sango Detective Agency (detectives Sango and Ryuuji). Tenryou is the commercial district below Tenshukaku: the Adventurers' Guild desk, Uyuu Restaurant (owner Okazaki Rikuto), clothing, lacquer and craft shops, food stalls, the Police Station, Komore Teahouse and the Aisa Bathhouse.

89.comment: Inazuma City: Statue of the Omnipresent God
89.content: A huge statue raised in front of Tenshukaku after the Vision Hunt Decree, into which every confiscated Vision was set as the "symbol of Eternity". Thoma told the Traveler it was still under construction when they arrived, and calls it the symbol of Eternity. The public Vision Hunt ceremony for Thoma was held before it. After the Traveler defeated Ei (2.1), the Visions were removed and returned to their owners. Who the statue depicts is disputed (see uncertainties).

90.content: A members-only teahouse in a prime spot on Inazuma City's streets, owned by the Yashiro Commission and used by the Kamisato Clan as a local base and private meeting place; only those the Kamisato approve may enter. Its nominal boss is Taroumaru, a Shiba Inu much admired by dog lovers and said to be a former Shuumatsuban ninja dog. During the 2.0-2.1 Archon Quest Ayaka and Thoma planned their covert operations against the Vision Hunt Decree here with the Traveler, and Thoma took refuge here after the Vision Hunt ceremony.

91.content: Yoimiya's family business in Hanamizaka, described as the oldest and one of the best fireworks shops in Inazuma. It also sells toys and knickknacks, some imported through the Crux Fleet and some made by Yoimiya, and Yoimiya has had fireworks shipped overseas to spread the shop's name. The fire brigade's warning notice outside asks her to stop risky behaviour.

92.content: A giant of Inazuma's publishing industry in Hanamizaka, founded and owned by Yae Miko, chief priestess of the Grand Narukami Shrine. It publishes light novels, holds the "This Novel Is Amazing!" competition, and serialises foreign works such as Xingqiu's A Legend of Sword (under the pen name Zhenyu). It has existed for no more than about five hundred years. Ei visited it during her walk through the city (2.1) to sample modern novels.

93.content:
The smithy of the Amenoma Art, one of the five schools of the Raiden Gokaden, on the eastern end of the city in Hanamizaka. Its owner, Amenoma Tougo, teaches that the Art has no secret tricks, only endless practice and willpower, like water wearing stone to sand. His disciple Hajime takes everyday orders.

The Amenoma Art is the only Gokaden school that came through the Wanderer's old revenge against the bladesmiths unscathed. In the 3.3 Interlude, after the Wanderer erased himself from Irminsul, Tougo told the Traveler the revised history: disaster at Tatarasuna four hundred years ago, and about a hundred years ago a vengeful smith's descendant who murdered Gokaden smiths until the Kamisato and Kaedehara clans stopped him.

94.comment: Inazuma City: The Vision Hunt Ceremony and the Duel Before the Throne
94.content: At a public ceremony before the Statue of the Omnipresent God, Thoma was to be the hundredth person stripped of a Vision. The Traveler intervened and used Electro without a Vision; the Shogun named them "an exception", an enemy of eternity, and defeated them, but Thoma helped them escape (2.0). Later (2.1) Sara learned that Kujou Takayuki had betrayed the Shogunate, the Traveler fought through the Tenryou Commission Headquarters with her, and at Tenshukaku the Traveler won a duel before the throne against the Harbinger Signora, whom the Shogun then executed with the Musou no Hitotachi. Outside, Kaedehara Kazuha blocked the Shogun's strike with his late friend's Vision, the Traveler was drawn into the Plane of Euthymia and defeated Ei, and the Vision Hunt Decree ended.

95.comment: Inazuma City: Ei's Walk Through the City
95.content: In her story quest, with the Shogun puppet indisposed, Ei came out of the Plane of Euthymia and toured the market with the Traveler. She found the shops and vendors much changed from her memory, startled the townsfolk, tried Dango Milk at Tomoki's stall and visited the Yae Publishing House to learn about light novels.

96.content: An indoor bathhouse in Tenryou inspired by Natlan's hot springs, offering baths, fine dining and therapy from yumekui-baku psychologists. It is run by Aikawa Susumu, a returnee from Natlan. After a major renovation, the yumekui-baku psychologist Yumemizuki Mizuki became its core founding investor and decision-maker. Its official description says everyone from high officials to commoners comes to unwind. Its troubles are the subject of Mizuki's story quest (5.4).

97.content:
Jakotsu Mine (also: Jakotsu Koukou, Snake Bone Mine): Jakotsu Mine is a mining area on Yashiori Island, a stormy island of Inazuma where the remains of the slain serpent god Orobashi lie. Once home to miners and their families, it was abandoned after the Tatarigami began sickening the island's people. Today it is a rain-lashed, lightning-struck site containing a broken ward, the bandit-held Formation Estate and the empty house of a boy named Chouji.

The island's constant thunderstorms continue over the mine until the quest Orobashi's Legacy: Part III repairs its ward. Chouji's house is the place where leaflets from both the Shogunate and the Watatsumi resistance still hang on a fence.

Geography: Jakotsu Mine lies on Yashiori Island next to the Serpent's Head. A Narukami Pillar and a Sacred Stone Mound stand on its southern cliff, near where Chouji first appears. A cave to one side of the ward contains a Thunder Barrier and a Thunder Sakura Bough; a path on the other side leads through slimes and Abyss mages. Chouji's House and the Formation Estate domain entrance are here. Local specialties are Crystal Marrow, Naku Weed and Onikabuto.

The area has Electro Elemental Monument, Lightning Strike Probe, Narukami Pillars and Seelies. Common enemies are Kairagi: Dancing Thunder, Nobushi: Hitsukeban and Hydro Slimes. One spot is a location for Kid Kujirai's Temari challenge.

History: Orobashi's remains and its lingering hatred, the Tatarigami, made Yashiori Island unlivable. The Raiden Shogun's wards held the Tatarigami back until a radical faction of the Watatsumi Army destroyed them, after which the miners and villagers fell ill or were driven mad. A notice found at Chouji's house orders miners and families to evacuate in an orderly way because the Tatarigami and the Sangonomiya rebels had both reached the island, and promises that the Tenryou Commission under Kujou Takayuki will escort them away.

Leaflets near the house show both sides of the war: the Shogunate offers help at the Kujou troops' forward base, while a resistance leaflet addresses the island's people as fellow victims of the Vision Hunt Decree and asks why the "Ogosho" never answers questions in person. A co-worker's letter to an "Elder Sister" says the writer found no one, only a broken pick, and urges her to rest since Chouji is still a kid and she has taken a job in the mine.

Quests: Orobashi's Legacy: Part III has the Traveler find the Jakotsu Mine ward, solve its Sacred Stone Puzzle, and retrieve a Rock Pillar Warding Stone and a Rock Pillar Pearl from either side of it before returning them. The quest clears the Tatarigami over the mine and unlocks the Formation Estate domain, whose trial is called Tutelage: King of Thieves.

Chouji's story quest Gazing Three Thousand Miles Away starts nearby. He is a quest NPC who lives alone and saves Mora from selling Crystal Marrow to leave the island and search for his parents.

Dangers: Permanent rain and lightning until the ward is repaired, which makes everything Wet and can trigger Electro-Charged; Tatarigami influence; Nobushi, Kairagi and Abyss mages; the bandits of the Formation Estate.

Atmosphere: Empty mine shafts and miners' houses in the storm, notices tacked to fences still telling people to evacuate, and a sense of a community that left in a hurry.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Jakotsu Mine is deserted. The storms stop once its ward is repaired in Orobashi's Legacy: Part III.

No 6.x or 7.x content on the wiki involves the mine.

98.content: The Formation Estate is a one-time domain entrance in Jakotsu Mine. The description says it once belonged to a lieutenant of Orobashi, until he, the god's body and the sky were rent open by a flash of lightning; later it became a hideout of bandits. It unlocks after Orobashi's Legacy: Part III and clearing the Seelie puzzle; it holds enemies such as Kairagi, Nobushi and Treasure Hoarders.

99.content: Chouji is a quest NPC found near Jakotsu Mine. He and his parents lived in Higi Village until the Tatarigami made villagers ill. He lives alone and is trying to save enough Mora from selling Crystal Marrow to leave Yashiori Island and look for his parents. His house has the evacuation notice and the leaflets from both sides.

100.content:
Jinren Island (also: Jinren-jima, Blade Gang Island): Jinren Island is a cluster of broken isles at the northernmost tip of Inazuma, lying in the shadow of Mt. Yougou. The expedition description says that in a less peaceful time it crawled with deserters who fell into banditry. Kairagi and Nobushi ronin hold it in its main story.

Its name is rendered "Blade Gang Island" in translation. It is best known for the world quest The Farmer's Treasure, in which the Traveler helps a caged young man, Saimon Jirou, and goes hunting for a treasure that turns out to be anything but.

Geography: The isles are separated by water and sand, with a main island where the ronin camp and a small hill with a cage on top. A Time Tunnel here leads to the arena of the Perpetual Mechanical Array, reached by drawing an Electrogranum from a Thunder Sakura Bough and flying up on the Thunder Spheres.

Several cages scattered across the island hold chests, a Seelie, a torn page of the Toki Alley Tales series, a dog named Toratarou, and Saimon Jirou. Metal Keys and a Cage Key are hidden around the island.

People: Two NPCs are tied to the island: Saimon Jirou, the son of a farming family in Konda Village, and Toratarou, a Shiba owned by the Kairagi and Nobushi band whom Jirou calls friendly and not a biter.

The ronin are Kairagi and Nobushi (Kikouban, Jintouban and Hitsukeban types). A Nobushi named Saiya Tadayoshi guards Toratarou's cage and respawns even after the dog is freed.

History: Jirou had belonged to a group of young troublemakers in Konda Village and was pushed by his parents into the army. He eventually deserted, heard of a treasure and went to Jinren Island, where the ronin caged him.

In The Farmer's Treasure the Traveler finds Old Stone Slates for him and defeats the ronin, then a Treasure Hoarders group and some Fatui who also turn up. The "treasury" proves to hold only wheat and vegetables, and Jirou goes home to his parents in Konda Village, who had posted missing-person notices. His father obtains a forged document certifying him unfit for service.

Dangers: Ronin of the Kairagi and Nobushi orders are the main enemies, plus a miniboss guarding Toratarou's cage.

Atmosphere: Salt wind, sand, ruined lean-tos and cages, with Mt. Yougou looming in the north. Mostly bleak, with a streak of slapstick in the farmer's tale.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Jinren Island is unchanged in lore; Jirou has returned home.

101.content:
Kamisato Estate (also: Kamisato Yashiki, Kamisato Residence): The Kamisato Estate is the large residence of the Kamisato Clan on Narukami Island in Inazuma, and a point of interest in the Inazuman Archon Quests. The clan head Kamisato Ayato and his younger sister Kamisato Ayaka live and work here. The Yashiro Commission, one of Inazuma's three Commissions, has its headquarters inside the main building.

The map text describes the Yashiro Commission as ostensibly handling the ceremonial and cultural life of the people, though its duties are so wide that even Shogunate officials cannot make sense of them. It also notes that Ayaka, the Shirasagi Himegimi, is better loved by the people than the head of the household.

Places: The main building houses the Yashiro Commission Headquarters, which has its own map icon and interior; the Traveler compares its grand feel to Dawn Winery and the Jade Chamber. Bookshelves in the left-hand room hold volumes of A Legend of Sword, New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune and Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation. Furnishing items sold in game refer to rooms here, such as a kimono rack that holds the robe Ayaka wears for calligraphy.

Outside the estate, the clan also runs the Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City, a members-only teahouse used as a base and private meeting place.

People: The household and staff named on the estate's page are the housekeeper Furuta, the house servant Koharu, the shrine maiden Toda, and the Yashiro Commission representatives Hirano, Hirotatsu and Madarame Hyakubei, with Hiratsuka also present. Thoma is the clan's chief retainer, and the ninja Sayu belongs to the Shuumatsuban, the clandestine group that the clan, and Ayato in particular, controls.

Ayato handles governmental affairs of the Yashiro Commission; Ayaka looks after the clan's internal and external affairs, and her kindness and public work make her widely beloved.

Governance: The Yashiro Commission, led by the Kamisato Clan, is part of the Tri-Commission under the Inazuma Shogunate and is in charge of shrines, festivals and cultural events. It has less influence than the Kanjou and Tenryou Commissions, yet each of the three can keep the others in check. The clan also controls the Shuumatsuban, a clandestine organisation of ninja that gathers information.

Soldiers of the Shogun's Army assigned to the Yashiro Commission are described as relaxed, and the Commission is regarded as the least controversial of the three: it did not get involved with the Fatui during the Vision Hunt Decree or the Sakoku Decree, and Ayato declined a Fatui offer of cooperation. The Commission's reputation and influence rose a little afterwards.

History: When a generation of the clan caused great errors that shamed the family, Ayato and Ayaka's father worked to undo the damage and died, and their mother soon followed. Following their dying wishes, Ayato took the post of Yashiro Commissioner and protected Ayaka from those who saw them as expendable. Several groups tried to profit from the clan's weakness; Ayato outmanoeuvred them and restored its prestige.

The clan's early history is unknown. Its martial and elemental skills (Ayaka's "Senho" sprint is a Kamisato Art) imply that the bloodline is trained in swordsmanship and elemental magic. A past head, great-grandfather of the siblings by wiki inference, is mentioned in the Archon Quest The Palace, Dyed in Black.

Atmosphere: An orderly, formal noble house with quiet servants, calligraphy, shrine business and ledgers; official work of the Commission mixes with family life. Gentle, dutiful and politically careful rather than martial.

Quests: A point of interest in the Inazuma Archon Quests; the headquarters can be entered as an interior. The clan's Komore Teahouse and Thoma's and Ayaka's stories connect to it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the estate is the working seat of the Kamisato Clan and the Yashiro Commission, with Ayato as head and Ayaka as the public face of the clan. No change to its position has been recorded.

102.content: The headquarters is inside the main building of the Kamisato Estate and is marked on the map with the estate's icon. The Yashiro Commission manages shrines, festivals and cultural events, and keeps a lower-profile, more relaxed Army contingent than the Kanjou and Tenryou Commissions.

103.comment: Kamisato Estate: Ayato and Ayaka's family
103.content: Ayato and Ayaka's mother, Kamisato Kayo, is a historical figure whose death followed their father's. Their father worked to repair the clan's reputation and died doing so; the wiki cites the quest The Wind Settles for this account. Keep the family history short and avoid inventing specifics.

104.content:
Kannazuka: Kannazuka is an area of Inazuma made of rocky, cliff-ringed islands lying between Narukami Island and Yashiori Island. Its name is said to mean "the hill where no gods reside": neither the Shogun's faith nor Watatsumi's has a hold there. It holds Tatarasuna, where the Mikage Furnace (Inazuma's largest smelter) makes Jade Steel for swords. It also holds the Kujou Encampment, the Shogun's Army headquarters that faced the Watatsumi resistance during the recent civil war.
