In Yoimiya's first year as owner, Kamisato Ayaka asked her to include the Raiden Shogun's emblem, the Electro Mitsudomoe, because the Shogun would watch from Tenshukaku. Yoimiya laid thousands of launch tubes across the city so that, from the Tenshukaku angle, the fireworks formed the crest.

Ryuunosuke recalls that Yoimiya was once invited by the Yashiro Commission to host a ceremony and accidentally started a very big fire, and the angry fire brigade wanted fireworks banned from the occasion. Imatani Saburou proposed to his wife Imatani Kaori at the show fifty years before the Traveler's visit. Yoimiya has had the Crux fleet carry Naganohara fireworks overseas to spread the shop's name.

Quests: The shop is a hub of Yoimiya's story quest, the Carassius Auratus Chapter Act I, "Dreamlike Timelessness". In "The Firework Girl's Strange Stories" the Traveler meets children chasing the invented Great Mujina Youkai; Yoimiya comforts them and invites the Traveler to the show. In "A Sliver of Hope" and "Together Under the Fireworks" the shop hides Sakujirou, a man who slipped back into Inazuma after the Sakoku Decree and wants to leave again. Yoimiya works with the Traveler and with the Imatani family until Sakujirou can make peace with his childhood friend Imatani Keisuke of the Tenryou Commission, and the Traveler receives the Naganohara Fireworks Note, the recipe of a special gold firework.

The Tenryou Commission closes in on the shop during the final part, which is why Yoimiya fears for Sakujirou's last chance to carry out his wish.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shop is still run by Yoimiya, with her father living in Hanamizaka. The Sakoku Decree, which was in force while Takami spoke of shipping lanes, has since been lifted. No 5.x-7.1 content changes the shop.

147.comment: Naganohara Fireworks: The paper slip system
147.content: The Naganohara shop writes each custom firework recipe in a family code on a slip of paper and gives it to the buyer. Returning the slip lets the shop reproduce the same firework later; the slip is handed back instead of copied, so a customer's copy is the only record. At the end of her quest Yoimiya gives the Traveler a Naganohara Fireworks Note for the gold firework her father made for them, so the Traveler can request it again later, however much changes over time.

148.content: Sakujirou left Inazuma because it seemed too peaceful and wanted to see the world. He sneaked back after the Sakoku Decree because he regretted it and wanted to make up for past mistakes, and the Tenryou Commission chased him, so he took refuge at Naganohara Fireworks until it was safe for him to leave. In "A Sliver of Hope" Yoimiya remembers an elderly couple among the shop's clients, the Imatanis of Konda Village, who might help; their son Keisuke turns out to be Sakujirou's former childhood friend and an officer of the Tenryou Commission, who regrets confiscating Visions.

149.content:
Narukami Island: Narukami Island is the largest island of Inazuma and the heart of the Shogunate. Its coast holds Inazuma City, crowned by the castle Tenshukaku from which the Raiden Shogun rules. Ritou is the walled-off port where all foreigners enter. Above them rises Mt. Yougou, topped by the Grand Narukami Shrine and the Sacred Sakura. Inside the island are farming and dyeing villages, fox-haunted plains and moonlit sacred forests. Inazuma's public festivals and cultural events are held here.

During the Sakoku Decree the island was the centre from which isolation was enforced. Visitors arriving by sea see the shrine and the Sacred Sakura on the mountain and the city on the shore.

Geography: Mt. Yougou rises in the north of the island. Inazuma City lies on the coast below Tenshukaku. Ritou ("outlying island") is a port district set apart from the rest of the island, joined to it by a guarded road. Byakko Plain, a low and sparsely wooded field in the southwest, carries the main road from Konda Village to the city. Chinju Forest sits in a river valley just south of Mt. Yougou and is wrapped in perpetual night under an unseen moon. Araumi, the northern promontory, is cut off by the mountain. Off the coasts lie Jinren Island, a group of broken isles at the northernmost tip, and Amakane Island, a small festival island west of Byakko Plain.

Thunder Sakura trees grown from the Sacred Sakura's branches stand across the island and draw filth out of the land. At the foot of Mt. Yougou lay a pool of Electrified Water, which was de-energised after the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual.

Places: - **Inazuma City**: the capital, with the Tenryou commercial district, the Hanamizaka suburb and Tenshukaku.
- **Ritou**: the Kanjou Commission's port and checkpoint for all non-Inazuman nationals, home to the Outlander Affairs Agency.
- **Mt. Yougou / Grand Narukami Shrine**: the mountain shrine of Yae Miko's shrine maidens and the Sacred Sakura.
- **Kamisato Estate**: residence of the Yashiro Commission's Kamisato Clan, reached through Chinju Forest.
- **Konda Village**: a quiet farming village, long the Shogunate's main source of dye, known for Konda Cuisine.

- **Byakko Plain**: open fields where wild kitsune roam near the city outskirts.
- **Chinju Forest**: a sacred grove of torii, tanuki statues and abandoned shrines; legend says it was once home to many demons, and tales of the tanuki-bayashi cling to it.
- **Araumi**: ruins of an abandoned city that extends deep under the earth and sea.
- **Jinren Island**: broken isles in the mountain's shadow, once overrun by deserters turned bandits.
- **Amakane Island**: in summer, people sit among its sakura and watch fireworks in the distance.

People: The Shogun, the Tri-Commission and most of Inazuma's population live here, along with the Grand Narukami Shrine's maidens under Guuji Yae Miko. Ritou hosts foreign merchants (from Liyue, Mondstadt, Snezhnaya and elsewhere), Kanjou Commission officers and the Hiiragi family. Kitsune and bake-danuki, youkai that live alongside humans, roam the forests and plains.

Konda Village's chief is Konda Densuke. Tejima, a samurai and Vision bearer, has long waited in the village for a lover who promised to meet him there and never came.

Governance: The island is ruled directly from Tenshukaku. The Kanjou Commission runs Ritou and its border controls, the Tenryou Commission keeps order and the army, and the Yashiro Commission handles ceremony and culture. Under the Sakoku Decree, foreigners could only pass beyond Ritou with a Travel Permit that was hard to obtain without the right connections.

History: Tradition records that Narukami was one of the islands that survived the great flood after the war of funerary flame. In that flood a kingdom north of Mt. Yougou, whose foolish ruler wished to build a high garden for the white tree, was swept away or buried in sand. After the cataclysm about 500 years ago, Araumi's survivors never returned, and Thunder Sakura were planted across the island to absorb filth. Hundreds of years ago Lord Hiiragi Hiroshi of the Kanjou Commission turned a deserted island into the trading port of Ritou.

Araumi was an underground city that stayed active until the cataclysm. Then the Kitsune Saiguu guided its people through the tunnels to safety. In the present, the Traveler's arrival in Ritou began the Inazuma Archon Quests. With Hanachirusato's help, the Traveler performed the latest Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual.

Atmosphere: Red maples and green roof tiles at Ritou. Lantern-lit streets and shop signs in the capital. Cherry blossom and the hum of Electro on Mt. Yougou. A hush of torii and tanuki statues under Chinju Forest's endless moon. Fishing and farming villages along the roads, and in festival season fireworks over the water.

Dangers: Bandits and ronin, Treasure Hoarders and Kairagi linger in the wilder corners. Araumi's depths hold Ruin Guards and other ancient machines. Under Sakoku, foreigners trying to leave Ritou without a permit were turned back by its guards.

Travel: Ships from abroad dock at Ritou; it is the official way in. Roads link Ritou, Konda Village, Byakko Plain and Inazuma City, and boats cross to Kannazuka and the other islands.

Gameplay note: before the Travel Permit quest, guards stop the Traveler from leaving Ritou on foot. Unlocking the Statue of The Seven here reveals the sea between Inazuma and the mainland on the map.

Quests: The opening of Chapter II (Ritou, the Travel Permit, the Vision Hunt ceremony) and much of its finale take place here. World quests include the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual and the tanuki-bayashi stories of Chinju Forest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Narukami Island is at peace. The Sakoku and Vision Hunt decrees are gone, foreigners move freely through Ritou, and Ei now takes a more active part in governing from Tenshukaku. No Narukami-specific story events appear in 6.x-7.1 content.

150.content: Araumi is the northern promontory of Narukami Island, cut off from the rest by Mt. Yougou. It is full of the ruins of an ancient city that extends deep under the ground and the surrounding sea. The city likely dates from the Archon War. Its tunnels held the mansion of the Great Tengu Reizenbou and stayed in use until the cataclysm. Then the Kitsune Saiguu led its people out through the passages. The survivors never returned. Its depths are now patrolled by ancient automatons, including the Perpetual Mechanical Array.

151.comment: Narukami Island: Konda Village and Byakko Plain
151.content: Konda Village, in the southwest of Narukami, has long been the Shogunate's main dye-producing village. It is simple, peaceful and known for Konda Cuisine, though Sakoku and the war aged it early. The road from Konda to Inazuma City crosses Byakko Plain, a low field where wild kitsune roam. Folk say a fox will not show itself twice to a traveler whose fate is not tied to its own.

152.content: Chinju Forest is a sacred grove just south of Mt. Yougou, on the path to the Kamisato Estate. For reasons nobody explains it lies under eternal night, lit by an unseen moon. Torii gates, tanuki statues and abandoned shrines fill it. Legend says demons once lived there, and rumour holds that pranksters still play tricks on those who walk through. The "tanuki-bayashi" tales of bake-danuki are tied to it.

153.content:
Nazuchi Beach (also: Nadzuchi no Hama): Nazuchi Beach is a stretch of shallow coast joining Kannazuka and Yashiori Island in Inazuma. Its name once meant "to be tenderly caressed by the hands of the gods", but the shoal has seen far too much battle. Torn flags, broken arrows, shattered masts and wrecked decks lie along it, and it has long been a haunt of scavengers, pirates and ronin. In the Archon Quest it is where the Sangonomiya Resistance faced the Shogun's Army.

During the Vision Hunt Decree war it was a front line between the Tenryou Commission and the Watatsumi Army, fought over by both land and sea. Few people live there; those who are met are mostly soldiers on missions, Treasure Hoarders and wanderers searching for lost things.

Geography: A shallow coastal strip joining Kannazuka and Yashiori Island, with a Teleport Waypoint in its western part and another in its northern part. Violet Ibis rest on the sand among the torn banners, arrows and wrecked ships. Dendrobium grows here, a rare flower for such a place.

A large ship is stranded between the two waypoints, and several wrecks hold pirate diaries. An islet just to the south, between the waypoint here and the one at Musoujin Gorge, is where a retired Shogunate soldier wanders. Sword hilts stuck in the sand and rock mark fallen samurai; with Electrograna they can be energised, which wakes the Ochimusha, spirits of the dead, so that they may be put to rest (a hidden exploration objective).

People: The Shogunate soldiers Genzou and a superior, Terada, are on a mission near the waypoint; Genzou is the self-effacing subordinate, and Terada is evasive when asked what his mission is. The Treasure Hoarders Miura and Onoda scavenge the south, with Miura the bold boss and Onoda the nervous underling who fears running into either army; Miura's plan is to say they are with whoever they meet. Utsumi, a retired Shogunate soldier, searches an islet for his late son's belongings.

Utsumi's son joined the Shogunate as a samurai and died on the battlefield; Utsumi says he was buried in Kannazuka. Pirates sheltered a sick miner at their camp in their diaries, mention caring for the boy Chouji on the instructions of a man called Onitaka, and write of marking their borders with the belongings of defeated Shogunate stragglers. One diary also records a pirate with a stubborn fever and crew waking from nightmares; it does not name a cause.

History: The beach has been a war zone for close to a thousand years, according to the in-game texts. In the Vision Hunt Decree conflict the Sangonomiya Resistance's front line was pushed back a couple of times until it settled at Nazuchi Beach, where fighting was chaotic and scattered forces could not tell friend from foe.

In the Archon Quest "In the Name of the Resistance" (Chapter II, Act II) the Traveler finds the front here. Kujou Sara, commander of the Shogun's Army, offers a deal, handing over the Traveler for a pause in the fighting, which General Gorou refuses, saying the resistance never betrays its own. She then proposes a "fight of honor" of single combat, and the Traveler beats three Shogunate fighters in a row. When Sara orders a full assault, Sangonomiya Kokomi, the Divine Priestess of Watatsumi Island and the resistance's organiser, appears with long-hidden reinforcements, including the mercenaries Beidou and Kaedehara Kazuha, and Sara retreats. Kokomi introduces herself to the Traveler and invites them to Sangonomiya Shrine.

Atmosphere: Violet Ibis over a shoreline of splintered hulls, pennants half sunk in sand and rusted blades; the smell of salt and smoke. It feels like the field where a long war has ended, but never stopped sounding underfoot.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Pyro and Electro hilichurl shooters, Hydro slimes, Electro Whopperflowers, Nobushi and Kairagi, plus elites such as the Mirror Maiden and the Crackling Axe Mitachurl.

Travel: Two waypoints (west and north); Musoujin Gorge and Kannazuka lie close by. Thunder Sakura boughs are available for Electrograna.

Quests: The Chapter II Archon Quest "In the Name of the Resistance" (2.0). Hidden objective Put Them To Rest; the pirate diaries are collectible lore.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the beach remains a deserted battlefield of wrecks, stragglers and scavengers, with the Vision Hunt Decree war long over.

The decree was ended after the Archon Quest; no later canon through 7.1 changes the beach.

154.comment: Nazuchi Beach: Kannazuka and Fort Fujitou
154.content: Kannazuka ("the hill where no gods reside") is the rocky disputed territory beside the beach, claimed by neither the Shogunate nor Sangonomiya, where neither Inazuman nor Sangonomiya faith has influence. Mikage Furnace, Inazuma's largest smelting facility, which makes Jade Steel, lies there. General Gorou of the resistance is found at Fort Fujitou.

155.content:
Oina Beach (also: Oina Kaigan): Oina Beach is a subarea on the coast of Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. It has little recorded lore of its own, but in the world quest The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna the Traveler uses a Thunderbird feather on a Mysterious Carving here and sees part of Kanna Kapatcir's memories.

It is the second of three places, after Wakukau Shoal and before the Autake Plains, where the feather is used.

Geography: A stretch of shore on Tsurumi Island with Mysterious Carvings, Thunderstones, Thunder Barriers, Seelie and a Thunder Sakura Bough. Fluorescent Fungus grows here.

Hostile groups include Ruin Cruisers, Ruin Destroyers and a Ruin Guard, plus Hilichurl Berserkers, Cryo Hilichurl Shooters, Pyro Whopperflowers, Crackling Axe Mitachurls and Electro Abyss Mages.

History: In the quest the feather draws out a vision from the Thunderbird's point of view: strange objects fell from the heavens and one landed on Tsurumi Island, after which her sky cleared and fog began to emerge. She had the power to disperse it and did not. The vision also shows the islanders gathering the feathers she shed at set intervals, a habit she found puzzling.

The memory contradicts the islanders' belief that the Thunderbird made the fog to protect them. Kama remarks that his ancestors may simply have been wrong. The feather then flies off towards Mt. Kanna, which leads the party on to the Autake Plains.

Quests: The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna (2.2). Ruin Cruiser and Ruin Destroyer must be defeated, then a Ruin Guard, before the feather memory is revealed. Ruu is not found here.

Dangers: Ruin Machines, hilichurls and Electro Abyss Mages; elites include Mitachurls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no later canon read for this entry changes the beach.

156.content:
Outlander Affairs Agency (also: Ongoku Kansatsu, Outlander Affairs Bureau, Distant Country Supervision): The Outlander Affairs Agency is the Kanjou Commission office in Ritou that handles documents and requests from visitors who are not from Inazuma. While the Sakoku Decree was in force, any outsider who wanted to stay in Ritou had to apply here for a Residence Permit and pay a "handling fee", and the agency used its position to fleece stranded foreigners. Inspector Yurika runs the counter and Chiba guards the entrance.

The agency sits on the Kanjou Commission's watch over Inazuma's finances, customs and borders. Its reputation changed when the commission was purged of corruption: it grew more lenient and later quoted a modest official fee.

Geography: The agency is a point of interest in Ritou, the port island that handles all foreign arrivals and departures. Yurika wanders its courtyard, Chiba stands by the entrance, and the merchant Robert paces on the stairs outside.

Ritou also holds the border checkpoint where the inspector Kageyama checks entry papers and the International Trade Association, whose members alone could import and export goods under the Decree. The agency is the next stop after the checkpoint for anyone who wants to remain on Ritou.

People: Yurika is the Inspector at the counter; Chiba, an officer of the Kanjou Commission, keeps the door; the merchant Robert is a recurring applicant. The wiki lists no other staff. The commission's head, Hiiragi Shinsuke, stood above them until his arrest, after which his daughter Hiiragi Chisato became acting head of the clan.

Yurika's patter barely changes across the story: forms to fill in, a handling fee, and a reminder to bring the necessary "materials". Chiba tells arrivals to have documents and identification ready and warns them to keep a wallet to hand.

Governance: The agency answers to the Kanjou Commission, the branch of the Tri-Commission responsible for Inazuma's wealth and borders. Rules for foreigners in Ritou were set by the Kanjou Commission's administration. Thoma tells the Traveler that to everyday Inazumans anyone from elsewhere is an "outsider" and that outlanders are unwelcome while the Sakoku Decree stands, even in the Outsider Settlement on Ritou.

Thoma explains that some agency officials treat the fees as easy money and charge as much as they think a stranded merchant can pay, so a local friend helps. Outlanders have little recourse because of their social and economic position.

History: When the Sakoku Decree left outsiders stranded on Ritou, the agency took advantage. In Confessions of an Outlander (2.0), Yurika asked the Traveler and Paimon for a processing fee of one million Mora each, two million in all. Out of courtesy to Thoma she cut it to 400,000 Mora, and Thoma then offered 600 Mora and dinner, which she accepted and recorded. The quest sets this in the Archon Quest scene where the Traveler registers at the border and the agency.

After the events of Omnipresence Over Mortals (2.1) the Kanjou Commission was purged of corruption, Shinsuke was arrested over the Fatui plot, and Yurika said the official fee was 500 Mora per visitor, remarking that it was the first time she had heard anyone complain about prices being too low. Once the Sakoku Decree ended in Transient Dreams, she described a procedure for foreign merchants wanting to do business in Ritou long term: an Entry Permit, identification papers and the same 500 Mora fee.

Atmosphere: A bureaucratic building where money changes hands openly. Counter clerks speak in official phrases while the applicant counts coins. Merchants outside grumble about missing "materials". After the reforms the same routines continue with less menace.

Quests: Confessions of an Outlander (Archon Quest, Chapter II Act I: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia, 2.0) sends the Traveler through the agency with Thoma. The agency is otherwise an ordinary map location with NPCs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the agency still exists in Ritou. Yurika and Chiba were last seen at their posts after the Sakoku Decree ended, and processing has become routine. No content from 5.x to 7.1 mentions the agency.

157.comment: Outlander Affairs Agency: Yurika's handling fee
157.content: Yurika quotes fees according to urgency: the more important an applicant's business, the higher the "handling fee" should be. During the Decree she demanded a Residence Permit application, an Entry Permit and unnamed "materials". After Omnipresence Over Mortals she says the fee is the official 500 Mora per visitor and invites doubters to check the Kanjou Commission's latest regulations. After the Decree ends she asks merchants for an Entry Permit and identification papers.

158.content: Robert, a merchant, travelled with a fleet and had a Snezhnayan friend help with his application, yet Yurika kept telling him he was missing "materials". He asks the Traveler what else he needs. After the Decree ends he muses about opening a shop in Ritou.

159.comment: Outlander Affairs Agency: Irodori Festival at the agency
159.content: During the limited Irodori Festival event (Hues of the Violet Garden), Yurika says guests may sign up at the agency to set up a fan-work booth and may certify family members to arrange their food and board; usual store and residency permits are still processed, with the handling fee reminder. Chiba urges visitors to stay mindful of their safety, and Robert says he wants to invite Ryouko to the festival. This is event-only dialogue.

160.content:
Outsider Shrine: The Outsider Shrine is a modest shrine at Serpent's Head on Yashiori Island, next to a man called Washizu. He insists that people who pray there three times in a day will be rewarded by a "he" who listens, and the shrine itself shows no sign of anything unusual. It is the centre of the hidden objective Washizu's Prayers.

The objective plays out over four real days. Washizu was once the kind chief of Higi Village; the Tatarigami outbreak on the island unmoored him, and the shrine is where his worship turned dangerous.

Geography: It stands at Serpent's Head, the bone-strewn coast of Yashiori Island, where Orobashi's remains lie. Flavour text for the prayers mentions sea breeze, gulls, distant whales, fireflies, wildflowers and wind through the great serpent's bones, as if weathered into the saddest instrument of the sea.

On a given day the Traveler prays three times in a row; each prayer produces a short description of sounds and scents, always ending with the Traveler hearing nothing. Prayers on the first three days cause a chest to appear the next day. By the fourth day the descriptions comment that the shrine seems unresponsive.

Quests: Washizu's Prayers (requires having done Ritou Escape Plan) is time-gated: pray daily for three days, then speak to Washizu on the fourth. His talk grows more feverish: the "words of the heart" over the "words of the tongue", a woman who refused tribute and fled, and a growing sense that "he" is angry. On the last day he attacks the Traveler as a maddened samurai and is defeated, which opens the hidden world quest Sinister Instruction in Higi Village.

In Sinister Instruction he leaves behind notes and a village register. The register records villagers who died of illness, others lost to the war or sea, and strangers listed as sacrificed, plus a plan to leave the dead's belongings out as a lure for living sacrifices. It also records his search for Chouji's mother and, at the end, marks the Traveler as a "Nameless Outlander".

People: Washizu, village chief of Higi Village. According to the wiki's profile he built several shrines around the island to appease Orobashi's soul and protect villagers near Jakotsu Crystal. After Watatsumi fanatics inside the Watatsumi Army broke the seals on the island and the Tatarigami spread, he tried to keep order for refugees from Jakotsu Mine, locked up two villagers who had gone mad, and then fell to the Tatarigami himself. Locals later told Chouji that people who questioned him vanished.

Dangers: The shrine itself is harmless. Washizu is hostile only on the final day of the objective, and the following quest touches on human sacrifice (kept off-page here).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the objective and follow-up quest are unchanged, Washizu is dead, and the shrine's prayers no longer function after completion.

161.content:
Palace in a Pool: Palace in a Pool is a one-time domain beneath Suigetsu Pool on Watatsumi Island, Inazuma. Its description says that seawater once did not fill the pool and that moonlight, brighter then, flowed through it like quicksilver. It holds the ancient mansion of Umigozen, famed throughout Inazuma for a window where one could drink wine and watch the flowers; now it is empty and only bandits and thieves dwell there.

It has a single level, Tutelage: Umigozen's Mansion, and was added in Version 2.1.

Geography: Reached by draining part of Suigetsu Pool: Electro monuments are unlocked by using an Electrogranum on four probes, then the player dives through an opening toward a root, climbs it, opens a door by switches and drains the rest of the water.

Inside, sliding doors must be moved to obtain two amulets that open the final gate.

Dangers: Nobushi: Hitsukeban, a Mirror Maiden, a Treasure Hoarder Pugilist and Cryo and Pyro Potioneers.

Atmosphere: A flooded grandeur gone silent: rooms with sliding screens and the lingering sense of a once-celebrated house now squatted by thieves.

162.content:
Plane of Euthymia (also: Euthymia, Pure Land of One Mind, Isshin Joudo, Ei's inner world): The Plane of Euthymia is the inner world of Ei, the Raiden Shogun. Over 400 years ago, after building the Shogun puppet to rule in her place, Ei withdrew her consciousness into it to meditate on eternity and protect her spirit from decay. It is a space of mind, not a place one walks to, and it lies within the sword Musou Isshin kept inside the Shogun. For centuries Ei admitted no one.

The Traveler was drawn in three times: first as an "exception" to be judged, then to shake Ei's resolve with the light of the confiscated Visions, and later to persuade her to leave and see modern Inazuma. In Chinese the name is Yixin Jingtu, "Pure Land of One Mind".

Geography: It has no map as such. In the first judgment the Traveler finds bare gravel ground with torii rising from it in a dark void. Later it appears as a quiet, dark-skied space where Ei meditates, with Ei standing some distance away. It reflects her inner world, so its look follows her state of mind.

In The Omnipresent God the people's ambitions shine into the Plane and light it. Yae Miko remarks that the sky, once so dark, is glowing again and takes it as a sign that Ei is happy to see her. Ei herself later says she saw human aspirations light up the sky as countless stars when the Traveler charged in. The clearest guide for use in a scene: its weather and light are emotional, not physical.

People: Ei is the only permanent occupant. The Shogun puppet does not live there, though she can confront Ei in consciousness-spaces. Outsiders enter only because Ei pulls them in or, on the Traveler's second visit, because Yae Miko appears through the Grand Narukami Shrine omamori she had given them.

History: Yae Miko once taught Ei how to place consciousness in objects. Ei used this to create the Plane and set it in the blade Musou Isshin, a sword made from her sister Makoto's divine might that passed to Ei after Makoto died in the cataclysm about 500 years ago. Over 400 years ago she retired into it, leaving the Shogun to pursue Inazuma's eternity. She could watch the world and take over the puppet at will, but cared only about matters touching eternity, which is why she tacitly accepted the Vision Hunt Decree.

The Traveler, able to use elements without a Vision, disrupted the Vision Hunt Ceremony at the Statue of the Omnipresent God. The Shogun called them an exception and an enemy of eternity and drew them into the Plane to judge their strength; the Traveler was struck down and woke outside (Amidst Stormy Judgment).

In The Omnipresent God the Traveler returned, this time carrying the people's ambitions, with Yae Miko joining through the omamori. Ei was defeated, agreed to end the Vision Hunt Decree, and admitted she was glad to see Yae again, though she still held to eternity and asked for time to think about whether Inazuma should move forward.

Atmosphere: Quiet, dark and lonely at first, with a pressure the Traveler feels as static and headaches before entering. It is a place for slow, unhurried thought, where Ei refuses to reach a verdict just to have one. It brightens when someone she cares about arrives.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Plane remains Ei's inner retreat, but she is no longer sealed in it.

Ei has ended the Vision Hunt Decree, and spends time in the outside world. No Plane of Euthymia content was found for the 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0-7.1 releases.

163.content: The legendary sword made from Makoto's divine might. In her hands it was kept unsharpened as a symbol of true peace; after her death Ei took it into battle. Ei placed the Plane of Euthymia inside it, and the Shogun summons it from her chest. Makoto left a faint trace of her will in it, which was released after Ei's change of heart.

164.comment: Plane of Euthymia: The Vision Hunt Ceremony Trial
164.content: At the ceremony marking the 100th seized Vision, held at the Statue of the Omnipresent God, Thoma was to lose his. The Traveler intervened, was marked as an enemy of eternity and drawn into the Plane. In the fight the Shogun invoked the decree to stop other characters' Elemental Skills and Bursts, then delivered divine punishment. Thoma escaped with the unconscious Traveler.

165.comment: Plane of Euthymia: Ei's Lonesome Retreat
165.content: Ei had the Shogun disabled in part while she thought about Inazuma's eternity. The Traveler and Paimon persuaded her to tour Inazuma. The scene shows she is lonely in the Plane but sees her isolation as necessary.

166.content:
Police Station (also: Inazuma City Police Station, Bugyou-sho, Commissioner's Office): The Police Station is the Inazuma City office of the police, in the Tenryou district. Its in-game description says it is responsible for maintaining law and order in Inazuma, and the Japanese name means Commissioner's Office. It is staffed by the yoriki Owada, who just wants a quiet career, and a new doushin, Uesugi, who wants bigger cases.

Day-to-day the station takes reports from neighbours, which are mostly minor troubles and clumsy mistakes. It is a place for citizens to report anything out of order or any suspicious outsider, and a notice outside urges everyone to stay alert after hostile people were seen in Inazuma City.

Places: The office sits in Tenryou, the commercial district below Tenshukaku. Both officers wear the standard ashigaru-style uniform of the Inazuma Shogunate: purple-grey underclothes, eggplant-coloured armour with the Shogunate crest, and a cross-shaped spear. The notice board outside carries a public safety notice about hostile people in the city.

The notice asks citizens to report any suspicious outsiders entering the city immediately. The board's heading calls it a 'Hanamizaka Public Safety Notice', which is why the station's precise district is recorded as disputed.

People: Owada, the yoriki, is superior to every doushin there. He describes himself as getting too old, hoping only to clock out on time and retire in peace, and insists he is not slacking: he has seen everything in his long career and simply wants a peaceful world. He prays each day that nothing eventful happens, and refers pet-loss cases to Ryuuji. Uesugi, the doushin, is a recent recruit who greets visitors with a cheer for the Shogun and her everlasting reign and wishes the job gave him a big case worth his skill.

Owada and Ryuuji are old acquaintances. Ryuuji, now a detective at the Bantan Sango Detective Agency, used to be a doushin here until someone framed him and he was suspended; Owada wanted to help but, as he admits, his power was limited, and he is glad Sango cleared Ryuuji's name. Uesugi sometimes works alongside Ryuuji and prizes the sense of accomplishment that desk work lacks. He fears turning into Owada, insignificant until retirement, and is unsettled by how casual things at the station can be.

Governance: The station is part of Inazuma's law-and-order machinery under the Shogunate; Owada and Uesugi swear by the Shogun and the Electro Archon, and doushin answer to the yoriki. The link to the Tenryou Commission, which the Kujou clan leads, is implied by Rikuto's remarks below rather than stated by the officers.

Rikuto, the retired Tenryou Commission man who owns Uyuu Restaurant, says that yoriki and doushin still come to him for advice even though he is retired. Ryuuji says that in the present state of Inazuma even the police are not fully reliable, a remark about the Sakoku era rather than about this station in particular.

History: No founding history is given. Within the game's story the station appears during the period of the Sakoku Decree and the Vision Hunt Decree, when the city is on guard against outsiders.

The station figures in the background of Ryuuji's frame-up, which Owada recalls and which happened before the Traveler's arrival. Uesugi's Itto-and-Sara anecdote belongs to the time of the Vision Hunt Decree.

Atmosphere: Quiet, stiff and a little sleepy. Owada startles easily and hopes nobody has come to report anything; Uesugi is eager and slightly bored. Behind the calm there is a sense that officials are anxious about outsiders and that the world outside is getting complicated.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the wiki records no change to the station: Owada and Uesugi are still listed as its staff and the notice text is the same.

167.content: Owada is the yoriki at the Police Station, an older officer who wants peace and a calm retirement rather than excitement. He prays that the Electro Archon will bless everyone, treats frequent reports with alarm, and recommends the Bantan Sango Detective Agency for lost pets. He is an old acquaintance of Ryuuji and regrets he could not help him when Ryuuji was framed.

168.content: Uesugi is a new doushin, eager for important cases and mildly horrified at the thought of ending up like Owada. He sometimes helps Ryuuji with cases, takes missing-family reports (including the Traveler's), and tells the story of Arataki Itto's planned sumo rematch with Kujou Sara.

169.content:
Ritou (also: Ritou Harbor, Outlying Island): Ritou is the port on Narukami Island where every non-Inazuman entering or leaving Inazuma is processed. It is under the jurisdiction of the Kanjou Commission, whose ruling Hiiragi Clan has its estate here, and it holds the Outlander Affairs Agency, the foreign merchants' International Trade Association, and a plaza shaded by a great red maple. Under the Sakoku Decree, foreigners who arrived could go no further without a hard-won Travel Permit.

Legend says Lord Hiiragi Hiroshi of the Kanjou Commission built it centuries ago from a deserted island into a thriving trade centre, greatly impressing the Shogun. The Traveler arrived here at the start of the Inazuma Archon Quest (2.0).

Geography: Ritou sits on a peninsula of Narukami Island, its name meaning "outlying island", with the docks at its entrance, a central area around the plaza, the Hiiragi Estate, a southern coast, and a guarded exit on the road toward the rest of Narukami. The official map describes a fishing village of red maples and green roof tiles. A Statue of The Seven stands near the shore.

Places: The docks, with Kanjou inspectors and the harbour bulletin board; the Outlander Affairs Agency, which handles foreigners' documents; the International Trade Association; the Hiiragi Estate, which serves as the Kanjou Commissioner's office; and the central plaza with its large maple, known since the Irodori Festival as the Five Kasen Plaza.

Shops include Eipekkusu (Kaede's souvenir shop: Inazuman novels, porcelain tanuki and lucky fox figures, and once statues of the Shogun), Sailing Breeze (Karpillia's old Mondstadt liquor brand, which moved here after failing to compete with the Dawn Winery), the Syavushi Bakshesh Shoppe (Vahid's shop selling Sumeru's Anahitian Blessing fertiliser), a branch of Liyue's Chuyu Trading Company, and street-food stalls.

People: Kanjou Commission officers, inspectors and ashigaru; Hiiragi Chisato, acting head of the Hiiragi Clan; and a community of foreign merchants and sailors from Mondstadt, Liyue, Snezhnaya, Sumeru and elsewhere. Kurisu, born Christopher in Fontaine, founded and leads the International Trade Association and has helped many newcomers.

Governance: The Kanjou Commission, one of the Tri-Commission, manages Inazuma's finances, customs and borders from Ritou. Under the Sakoku Decree it ran a strict and corrupt regime: complicated assessments for entry or exit, heavy fees, and harsh treatment of foreigners. Commissioner Hiiragi Shinsuke conspired with the Fatui and was arrested after the 2.1 Archon Quest; his daughter Chisato now acts as clan head, and the commission has treated foreigners far better since.

Kanjou notices under Sakoku required valid documents to land, registration and taxation of weapons, camping gear and foreign goods, and a year's surveillance in Ritou for anyone who had dealt with the Sangonomiya. Snezhnayan merchants and the Fatui were initially exempt from the restrictions thanks to diplomatic ties; after the Fatui plot came to light, Snezhnayan merchants' special trade privileges were revoked and their arrears called in.

History: Lord Hiiragi Hiroshi wanted foreign trade centralised under the government and built Ritou to do it. To prove its worth he imported foreign inventions, among them a Snezhnayan blast furnace used to create the hot springs at Tenshukaku as a gift for the Shogun. When the Sakoku Decree sealed Inazuma about a year before the Traveler arrived, storms ringed the islands and foreign merchants were stranded in Ritou; the official viewpoint says the streets lost the bustle of a century before while the Kanjou Commission itself still flourished.

The Traveler landed here with Beidou's Crux fleet, which once docked at Ritou, and was met by Thoma (2.0). They exposed a Kanjou officer's Crystal Marrow racket against the International Trade Association, then escaped Ritou with Chisato's help after learning that Signora had conspired with her father to keep them there. After the Vision Hunt Decree ended, Shinsuke was detained, Ei abolished the Sakoku Decree (2.5), and visitors and trade returned. Yae Miko then revived the Irodori Festival in Ritou (2.6).

Atmosphere: Red maples, green tiles, the creak of the docks and a mix of accents. Under Sakoku it felt like a waiting room: outlanders idling in the plaza, staring out at the empty sea, short of money and patience. Since the decree ended it has been busier, though still the place where foreigners first deal with Inazuman paperwork.

Dangers: The worst danger in Ritou was bureaucratic: extortionate fees, arbitrary taxes and threats of arrest from corrupt officers. The harbour board once warned sailors about piracy and told them to stock up before leaving. Outside the town, nobushi and kairagi ronin and Treasure Hoarders work the roads, as the Traveler found when escorting Chisato's supply convoy.

Quests: Chapter II Act I (2.0): Setting Sail, Confessions of an Outlander and Ritou Escape Plan, followed by the world quest Chisato's Letter, which earns the Travel Permit. Kamisato Ayato's story quest (2.6) involves a plot inside the Hiiragi Clan. The 2.6 event Hues of the Violet Garden takes place here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Ritou is open: the Sakoku Decree was abolished in 2.5, foreigners come and go freely after processing, and the Kanjou Commission is far less corrupt under Hiiragi Chisato.

Hiiragi Shinsuke remains imprisoned. No new events in Ritou appear in the Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) storylines.

170.content: The Kanjou Commission's office for foreign visitors' documents and requests. Under the Sakoku Decree it fleeced stranded outlanders: the inspector Yurika first asked the Traveler for two million Mora, and Thoma talked her down to 600, saying such practices were common. After the commission was purged of corruption, the agency became more lenient and charges a processing fee of 500 Mora.

171.content: Founded by foreigners to trade in Inazuma (importing goods such as Silk Flowers) and to help newcomers survive the Kanjou Commission's harsh treatment. Its president Kurisu, a Fontainian who took an Inazuman name, welcomes outlanders in trouble. During the Irodori Festival it housed the foreign guests of honour, and the plaza in front of it was named the Five Kasen Plaza.

172.content: The Kanjou Commission suddenly demanded the association's taxes in Crystal Marrow rather than Mora. The officer Keijirou and his men bought up the supply and resold it through Werner, a former member from Mondstadt, at ever-higher prices. The Traveler found Keijirou's hidden ledger; when an officer, Katsuie, moved to arrest the merchants, Thoma produced a Yashiro Commission card and an ornate fan, and the matter was dropped. The Crystal Marrow the commission collected later turned out to feed the Fatui's Delusion factory.

173.comment: Ritou: Ritou Escape Plan and the Travel Permit
173.content: Barred from leaving Ritou, the Traveler visited Commissioner Hiiragi Shinsuke, who set absurd tasks (300 freshly picked Qingxin, or delivering 709 letters). His daughter Chisato secretly summoned them at night, revealed that an arrogant woman (Signora) had conspired with her father to keep them on Ritou, and slipped them out as the "qualified escort" for a Kanjou shipment she accompanied personally. Her letter to Kujou Kamaji of the Tenryou Commission in Inazuma City then earned them a Travel Permit to come and go freely.

174.content: After the Sakoku Decree ended, Yae Miko revived the long-forgotten Irodori Festival, which once honoured the poets known as the Five Kasen, as an international cultural convention centred on light novels. Kamisato Ayato invited celebrities from several nations to Ritou. The plaza before the International Trade Association became the Five Kasen Plaza, shops sold light-novel goods and fan-fiction stalls appeared outside the Outlander Affairs Agency. This took place during the limited-time event Hues of the Violet Garden (2.6).

175.content: In Kamisato Ayato's story quest, rumours spread that Chisato would marry Kujou Kamaji. Chisato had sent no proposal letter: the match was pushed by plotters among the Hiiragi Clan's supporters, including the Kanjou official Matsuura, while the commission was unsettled by Shinsuke's imprisonment, and Shinnojou was seized after he objected. Ayato, with Kamaji's help, turned public opinion so that Chisato became an asset the plotters could not discard, and she asserted her authority over them for the first time.

176.content:
Royal Hot Springs (also: Royal Bath, Royal Bathhouse, Go-onsen, Imperial Onsen): The Royal Hot Springs is a hot-spring bathhouse at the headquarters of the Tenryou Commission in Inazuma City, near Tenshukaku. It is reserved for the lords of the Shogunate, who are served and housed by its manager Mikawa Akane, and outsiders are not allowed in.

Access is based on a strict hierarchy. With private rooms and very few customers, the springs are often used for the lords' private discussions. Inazuma has no natural volcanic hot springs, so the water is heated artificially and mixed with minerals and plants from many nations.

Places: The baths lie in the Tenshukaku part of Inazuma City, within the Tenryou Commission's headquarters. The Court Lantern "Thundering Heart" furnishing describes lanterns found in Tenshukaku and at the Royal Hot Springs, coated in a solution made from trace amounts of Amethyst Lumps and Electro Crystals, which makes them brighter and lightning-resistant.

A courtyard by a cliff lies on the grounds, where the Fatui spy Tae slacks off in the 2.4 quest "Shuumatsuban Operations".

People: Mikawa Akane greets visitors by naming the Royal Hot Springs and its location at the Tenryou Commission headquarters, and asks whether an unfamiliar visitor has got lost. She arranges service and rooms for Shogunate lords who come for the hot springs. She is happy to tell new arrivals about Inazuma's hot-spring culture, but refuses to let an outsider bathe.

Akane explains that the Kanjou Commission's Hiiragi Hiroshi brought a high-efficiency boiler from Snezhnaya to reach hot-spring temperatures, and that the water is mixed with precious minerals and plants from various nations. She says ordinary commoners' hot springs cannot afford those minerals and so do not offer the same benefits, though one funded by the Kanjou Commission could be different.

Governance: The springs are for the Shogunate's lords, and the baths sit at the Tenryou Commission headquarters. Akane says access priority follows a strict hierarchy. The Kanjou Commission figure Hiiragi Hiroshi is credited with the first Inazuma hot spring, and Akane muses that a spring funded by that Commission could offer commoners the same benefits.

Akane says outlanders are not allowed in, which fits the Sakoku-era restrictions on outsiders but is stated in terms of hierarchy rather than the decree.

History: Hot-spring culture came to Inazuma from elsewhere, and the locals were enchanted by it. Having no volcanic springs, they tried many ways to make one. According to Akane, Hiiragi Hiroshi of the Kanjou Commission solved it with a Snezhnayan boiler, creating the first Inazuma hot spring.

Akane contrasts Inazuma with Natlan, where natural hot springs form from volcanic activity. The springs here are therefore a product of engineering and trade rather than geology.

Atmosphere: Quiet, formal and secluded: private rooms, very few customers and staff who know who may enter. The temperature of the water is, as Akane says, just right.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the springs are still reserved for Shogunate lords with Akane as manager; the wiki records no change since 2.0.

177.content: Mikawa Akane is the manager of the Royal Hot Springs. She is polite but firm, offers hot-spring history to newcomers, and refuses outsiders because the springs are for the Shogunate's lords by strict rank. She is irritated by Tae, a new employee who skips work.

178.comment: Royal Hot Springs: Tae, the Fatui Spy at the Baths
178.content: In the world quest "Shuumatsuban Operations" the Traveler is told one of three Fatui spies has recently started working at the Royal Hot Springs. Tae is a Fatui agent, disguised as staff, who dislikes Lyudochka Snezhevna, whom she accuses of getting the Grand Narukami Shrine post through luck. She is touchy, uses Fatui code phrases, and is suspected by the Tenryou Commission after the frostbite incident.

179.content:
Sacred Sakura (also: Shin'ou, Giant Thunder Sakura, Primeval Sakura, Crimson Sakura): The Sacred Sakura is the divine tree that towers over the Grand Narukami Shrine at the top of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island. It stands for the Electro Archon's protection of Inazuma: its roots purify the land's ley lines and keep Abyssal corruption from invading, and the sakura blossoms across the island have all fallen from it. Because filth builds up in its roots, the Grand Narukami Shrine must perform the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual from time to time.

Its offshoots, the Thunder Sakura, are found all over the land, and it is said that its protection reaches wherever its petals come to rest. The people of Inazuma remember it as having always been there, though its origin is stranger than that.

Geography: The tree rises over the Grand Narukami Shrine at the top of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island. Its roots spread under the whole land, and the Thunder Sakura grafted from its side branches are connected to the same single root system. Beside the mountain at its foot is a large pool of Electrified Water that drains health until the cleansing is done.

The Depths of Mt. Yougou beneath the tree is where the tree's accumulated filth gathers into a Miasmic Tumor when the major cleansing lifts the barrier around the central roots. After the Cleansing Ritual of the Traveler and Hanachirusato, the pool is de-energised and the tree glows a soft blue that can be seen from the mainland.

History: Inazuman tradition holds that the Sacred Sakura cleanses the land of impurity through the Thunder Sakura, defending earth and water alike. Records say the Thunder Sakura almost withered several hundred years ago, when monsters raged and the seas around Inazuma turned black; someone eventually performed the Cleansing Ritual and the crisis ended. The ritual has a minor form, done often to check the roots and set up protective barriers, and a major form needed every sixty years: first the Thunder Sakura roots are purified, then the central roots of the Sacred Sakura.

According to the ritual summary, the performers beg forgiveness from both the Narukami and the Watatsumi shrines before beginning, which may suggest that Orobashi's people once shared in the tree's worship. The most recent cleansing was carried out by the Traveler with Hanachirusato; the Grand Narukami Shrine had been preparing the ritual, but Yae Miko called it off and had the Memento Lens ready for a blonde-haired outlander.

Quests: The Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual is a World Quest series that begins at Konda Village. The Traveler meets the masked shrine maiden Hanachirusato, lifts barriers with wards, clears the Thunder Sakura roots at Araumi, the Kamisato Estate and Chinju Forest, then breaks the barrier at the Depths of Mt. Yougou and purges the Miasmic Tumor there. Hanachirusato then reveals she is filth condensed from the memory of the Kitsune Saiguu, and must be cleansed with the rest.

As a game mechanic, offering Electro Sigils to the Sacred Sakura raises Sacred Sakura's Favor, which unlocks rewards and upgrades Electrograna. In the Raiden Shogun's story quest, the quests Cleansing Light and Radiant Sakura revolve around the tree's connection to Makoto.

Atmosphere: A towering tree whose roots run through the whole land, quiet and sacred, glowing blue after the cleansing; shrine bells and falling petals around a place felt to be watching over the islands.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sacred Sakura is cleansed and glowing. No 6.x or 7.x content altering that was found on the wiki.

The story of the tree's origin is already told in the Raiden Shogun's Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter.

180.comment: Sacred Sakura: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual
180.content:
The ritual keeps the connected roots of the Sacred Sakura and the Thunder Sakura clean. The Grand Narukami Shrine ordinarily performs it. Minor cleansings check the roots and raise barriers that protect the roots from malicious people such as the Fatui and protect the people from leaking filth. The major cleansing, due every 60 years, breaks those barriers with wards so the filth is driven out and condenses into forms: harmless ones such as the tofu-like figures in peaceful times, dangerous ones in times of strife. At the central roots the filth condenses into a Miasmic Tumor.

If too much filth accumulates the roots are corroded, the tainted parts form tumors, and left alone the tree withers, which would be catastrophic for Inazuma.

181.content: The Thunder Sakura are trees grafted from side branches of the Sacred Sakura; they absorb filth into their roots to purify the land. Their roots connect to the central tree's, so pollution spreads between them. Sakura Bloom, a local specialty of Narukami Island, comes from the Sacred Sakura.

182.content:
Sangonomiya Shrine (also: The Pearlescent Palace, Coral Palace): Sangonomiya Shrine, also called the Pearlescent Palace, stands at the centre of Watatsumi Island, the outermost island of Inazuma. A palace flanked by shells and sea rocks, it is the island's centre of government and religion alike: here the Divine Priestess Sangonomiya Kokomi rules, and here rest relics of Orobashi, the dead serpent god whom Watatsumi's people still worship instead of the Raiden Shogun. During the war against the Vision Hunt Decree it was the headquarters of the Watatsumi Army.

Its name means "Coral Palace". The island's shrine maidens are trained here. The present shrine is said not to be the island's original one, but a newer building raised after Orobashi was slain by the Electro Archon about 2,000 years ago.

Geography: The shrine lies in the middle of Watatsumi Island, ringed by mountains and waterfalls and surrounded by the island's strangely coloured, densely growing vegetation, with its violet-leaved forests. Bourou Village, the island's main settlement and the resistance's training camp, lies nearby, and Mouun Shrine stands elsewhere on the island. Sango Pearls and Sea Ganoderma are gathered in the surrounding area.

The whole island is built on coral that Orobashi broke from its own body to raise a home for its people. Watatsumi has little arable land; its soil is also prone to "Holy Soil", a bleaching and erosion that legend blames on Enkanomiya drawing on the island's spirit.

Places: The main palace-shrine, where Kokomi receives officers and guests; the shrine grounds, where Watatsumi soldiers keep watch; and nearby woods with a tree with purple foliage that Kokomi's written directives name as a landmark for finding her when she has slipped away.

Kokomi keeps a private retreat away from the shrine where she reads in peace; her standing orders tell guards to send important visitors southward to that purple-leaved tree if she has vanished without word. Victory feasts after the war were held on the island under open sky at night.

People: Sangonomiya Kokomi, Divine Priestess and supreme leader of Watatsumi Island, lives and works here. General Gorou commands the island's army. Shrine maidens trained at the shrine include Izumi Naki, Mochizuki, Tsuyuko, Shizuru and Miwa; Sangonomiya samurai such as Shibata and Sugiyama stand guard, and officers such as Ookubo Daisuke report here on supplies.

Tsuyuko, a shrine maiden who studied at the Sumeru Akademiya, comes from a family charged with the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri and keeps an ancestral secret about a second set of trials. Kokomi's mother taught her that "as the ruler is, so shall the people be".

Governance: The shrine is the seat of the Sangonomiya Clan, the only great Inazuman clan with no post in the Shogunate. The heir of their bloodline holds the title Divine Priestess, which means inheriting the will of a god in a mortal body and defending the land and people in that god's place. Kokomi handles war, trade, diplomacy and domestic affairs herself and governs through detailed written directives.

When Kokomi became Divine Priestess, crowds came to the shrine to look at her and were openly doubtful because she looked so young; ambitious people schemed, yet the island soon returned to normal under her rule. Her directives were at times very thick, but they kept the island developing steadily; as more capable officials have been appointed, she has had to issue fewer of them. Her fairness in rewards and punishments won most people over, and the island's most common saying became that things will be alright as long as Her Excellency is here.

Culture: Watatsumi's people descend from Enkanomiya, a realm deep beneath the sea; Orobashi brought them to the surface, and they revere it as Watatsumi Omikami, their guardian god. Faith in the slain god, pride, and a long memory of defeat bind the community. The island keeps customs distinct from the capital's.

A recurring rite, the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri, holds back the Holy Soil using a Jade Coral Branch (Bloodbranch Coral) from Enkanomiya; the shrine maiden Tsuyuko enlisted the Traveler to prepare it in the world quest series "The Moon-Bathed Deep". After the Three Realms Gateway Offering events, Kokomi resolved to find a new way to counter the Holy Soil so as not to disturb the vishaps of the depths.

History: About 2,000 years ago, near the end of the Archon War, Orobashi raised Watatsumi Island from coral and led the people of Enkanomiya there. Hunger drove them to invade Yashiori Island; the Electro Archon struck back, and Orobashi was slain with the Musou no Hitotachi, which split Yashiori and left the Tatarigami behind. The old main shrine was abandoned and the present one built, with the Divine Priestess leading the island. When the Vision Hunt Decree came, the shrine became the resistance's headquarters.

Orobashi's navy was led by the shrine maiden Mouun and her twin sister Ayame; Mouun fell to the troops of the Shogun's lieutenant Sasayuri and Ayame vanished. A Sumeru scholar's study, found in Bourou Village, records the people's grievance at seeing their god's body mined for its ore by their overlord, and warns that such old resentments can be used by people with their own agendas. In the 2.1 Archon Quest, Kokomi accepted an anonymous sponsor's supplies at the shrine to grow the army. The sponsor turned out to be the Fatui, whose Delusions killed resistance soldiers, Teppei among them.

Atmosphere: A luminous, sea-washed palace of pearl and coral tones, with the sound of waves, soft violet woods and shells on the shore. During the war it was quietly busy: officers reporting on food shortages, soldiers on guard, a young leader calm in public whose hands shook before speeches. Since the peace it has felt calmer and more welcoming: Kokomi invites friends to stay, eat and read books with her.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter II, Act III "Omnipresence Over Mortals" (2.1): in "Sword, Fish, Resistance" Teppei brings the Traveler to the shrine, where Kokomi appoints them captain of the special operations unit Swordfish II; later the Traveler returns here and identifies the sponsor's weapons as Delusions. Kokomi's Story Quest (Dracaena Somnolenta Chapter) starts near the shrine. The world quest series "The Moon-Bathed Deep" begins when Tsuyuko, a shrine maiden of Sangonomiya Shrine, approaches the Traveler at Mouun Shrine; the entrance to Enkanomiya she describes is the deep pool directly across from Sangonomiya Shrine.

The anecdote "Sangonomiya Kokomi: Reunion" (Travelers' Tales) begins with Kokomi standing outside the shrine.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine is peaceful and still Kokomi's seat. The Vision Hunt Decree was abolished, peace talks with the Shogunate followed, and the Watatsumi Army now serves mainly as peacekeepers and helps rebuild.

Talks on bringing the island back under direct Shogunate rule made progress but were paused after the Fatui's meddling in the war came to light, so the island kept its army. Some residents still find peace with the Shogunate hard to accept. No 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story shown involves the shrine.

183.comment: Sangonomiya Shrine: Divine Priestess of Watatsumi
183.content: The Divine Priestess is the hereditary head of the Sangonomiya Clan and supreme leader of Watatsumi Island, ruling from Sangonomiya Shrine. The title means carrying a god's will in a mortal body and protecting the island and people in Orobashi's place. The current holder, Sangonomiya Kokomi, would rather have been a strategist working behind the scenes, but took up the role and is deeply loved by her people. Soldiers and islanders call her "Her Excellency".

184.comment: Sangonomiya Shrine: Orobashi's relics at the shrine
184.content: The viewpoint text calls the shrine the place where the relics of the serpent god lie. Orobashi, called Watatsumi Omikami, once ruled in Enkanomiya, taught its people to farm and smelt, and raised Watatsumi Island from its own coral before dying at the Electro Archon's hand. Its bones lie on Yashiori Island and its resentment became the Tatarigami. The shrine remains the heart of its worship.

185.comment: Sangonomiya Shrine: Three Realms Gateway Offering at Sangonomiya
185.content: During the limited-time event Three Realms Gateway Offering (2.5), Tsuyuko at Sangonomiya Shrine, now that the island was no longer under threat, revealed a family secret: besides the Goryou Matsuri, her ancestors had set a second set of trials concerned with the truth. This led the Traveler to Eboshi (Erebos), who introduced herself as an auxiliary of Sangonomiya and one of Enkanomiya's shrine maidens, and into the "Erebos' Secret" quests. Kokomi also commissioned the Traveler to go back down to Enkanomiya, then shrouded in darkness, for the sake of Watatsumi's future.

186.content:
Seirai Island: Seirai Island is a broken, storm-wracked island of Inazuma. About 1,500 years ago the Thunderbird, Kanna Kapatcir, ravaged it until the Electro Archon killed her on Amakumo Peak, and wards held back the storm her death left. About 500 years ago a shrine maiden broke those wards to help the pirate Ako Domeki rebel against the Shogunate. A huge Electro storm then engulfed the island's centre, shattered the land and drove its people away for good. Today only Asase Shrine stands intact, kept by a talking cat called Neko who still waits for her mistress to return.

The Traveler recently resealed the storm with the help of two Adventurers' Guild members.

Geography: Seirai is a cluster of fragmented landmasses around a central basin. Until recently a perpetual thunderstorm filled that basin, with Balethunder and lightning striking anyone who entered. Amakumo Peak rises inland above a lake, with flooded underground ruins below it. Koseki Village, the abandoned fishing village, lies on the coast, as do the wreck of the flagship Seiraimaru and the ruins of Fort Hiraumi. Asase Shrine sits apart with fair weather of its own.

Even after the storm ended, Electrified Water remained at the island's centre until a nearby puzzle drained it, revealing a large hole. Floating Warding Stones once hung in the sky above the island.

Places: - **Asase Shrine**: built to manage the wards over the Thunderbird's lingering hatred; the only place the storm left untouched.
- **Koseki Village**: the island's former fishing village, now silent; its people helped keep the shrine and made offerings there.
- **Amakumo Peak**: where Ei slew Kanna Kapatcir and where the Thunder Manifestation later appeared.
- **"Seiraimaru"**: the stranded wreck of Ako Domeki's flagship.
- **Fort Hiraumi**: ruins of the city of Hiraumi, destroyed by the Thunderbird.

- **Slumbering Court**: a domain at Fort Hiraumi.
- Amakumo Peak's drained lake opens into a maze of submerged ruins guarded by Ruin Sentinels.

People: Since the evacuation Seirai has no settled human population. Neko, a cat who can speak and no longer ages, calls herself the shrine's "Provisional Head Priestess" and watches over generations of shrine cats. The cats are named after "good things", and the names pass down the generations. The Adventurers' Guild members Etsuko and Taisuke stay at the shrine after the storm ends.

After the shrine's repair, Ooshima Junpei, a craftsman left jobless when Tatarasuna was evacuated, carved a giant statue of Neko there. Konbumaru, one of the cats, is named after Takamine the Mistsplitter's nickname.

History: Seirai is thought to be one of the few islands that survived the great flood after the war of funerary flame. About 1,500 years ago, after destroying the tribe on Tsurumi Island, Kanna Kapatcir came to Seirai, wrecked much of it and left the city of Hiraumi in ruins. To protect her people, Ei hunted and killed the Thunderbird on Amakumo Peak. Warding Stones held back the storm left by her death, and the Asase Clan's shrine maintained the wards. About 500 years ago, a few years after the cataclysm, the pirate captain Ako Domeki led Seirai in rebellion against the Shogunate. Asase Hibiki, the shrine's head priestess, unsealed the wards with magic she had learned from the Yougou Tengu to destroy the Shogunate's ships. The storm that followed tore the island apart. The Shogunate evacuated the islanders to Narukami Island, and Hibiki never came back from the storm.

Hibiki had trained at the Grand Narukami Shrine as one of the Yougou Three, and the cataclysm cost her Takamine the Mistsplitter. She agreed to help Domeki partly out of friendship and partly because he reminded her of Takamine. The storm swept Domeki's fleet far out to sea. His chief mate Janome and the ship carrying a Maguu Kenki that Domeki had captured (a detail told during the limited-time Echoing Tales event) were stranded on the Golden Apple Archipelago while protecting him. Domeki himself returned to find Seirai in ruins and sailed off to live freely and see the world as Hibiki had wished.

Atmosphere: Rain-black skies, fractured cliffs and abandoned houses, with the thunder only recently stilled. The Koseki Village viewpoint says the old laughter and cicada song have been lost to the thunder, and people now only remember that the place was abandoned to the storms. Asase Shrine, by contrast, is bright, tidy and full of cats.

Dangers: Before the Traveler resealed the Warding Stones, Balethunder and targeted lightning made the centre deadly. The Thunder Manifestation, a coagulation of the Thunderbird's regret, still appears there (gameplay: a repeatable boss on a platform formed above the island). Ruin Sentinels and slimes haunt the flooded ruins under Amakumo Peak.

Culture: Seirai's islanders kept Asase Shrine and made offerings there, and the shrine and villagers blessed Domeki's flagship before it sailed. According to Neko, Hibiki ran the shrine, received guests and cooked for the cats, and she also gave Neko her name.

Quests: In Seirai Stormchasers (2.1), sent by Katheryne, the Traveler joins the adventurers Etsuko and Taisuke. With Neko's guidance they reseal the four Warding Stones and defeat the Thunder Manifestation, which ends the storm. The Traveler also finds a Peculiar Pinion, a Thunderbird feather that matters later on Tsurumi Island. In Neko Is a Cat, the Traveler restores Asase Shrine for Neko.

At the end of Through the Mists (2.2), the Traveler uses the Pinion's power to bring the spirit of Ruu from Tsurumi to Seirai. There he sings for Kapatcir once more, and the curse on Tsurumi is lifted.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the storm is sealed but the island stays depopulated, with only adventurers passing through and Neko tending Asase Shrine. She still believes Hibiki, Domeki and Janome will come back. No Seirai-specific story content appears in 6.x-7.1.

187.comment: Seirai Island: Asase Shrine and Neko
187.content: Asase Shrine on Seirai Island was founded after Kanna Kapatcir's death to manage the wards over her lingering hatred, and the Asase Clan ran it. Five centuries ago its head priestess Asase Hibiki broke the wards, but the shrine itself was spared by the storm. Neko, the cat Hibiki named, somehow stopped ageing, learned to speak, and has kept the shrine ever since, calling herself its "Provisional Head Priestess". She does not know that the islanders were evacuated, or that Hibiki must have died long ago, and she hopes a restored shrine will bring visitors and Hibiki back.

188.content: About five hundred years ago, the famed bandit and pirate Ako Domeki Zaemon of Seirai rose against the Shogunate with a fleet of over ten ships led by the flagship Seiraimaru. According to the limited-time Echoing Tales event, he even captured a Maguu Kenki puppet in battle. His friend Asase Hibiki unsealed the Thunderbird's wards to sink the Shogunate's ships. The storm destroyed them, but it also tore Seirai apart and scattered Domeki's own fleet. The Seiraimaru's wreck still lies on the island. Domeki was the original wielder of the polearm "The Catch" and owned the item known as Ako's Sake Vessel.

189.content:
"Seiraimaru" (also: Seiraimaru, The Stranded Flagship): "Seiraimaru" is a subarea of Seirai Island named for the flagship of the bandit captain Ako Domeki, which was destroyed there. The rundown atakebune warship lies stranded among thunder-scarred terrain, its wreck still marked by what looks like starlit tears.

The viewpoint text recalls a vessel that once sailed proudly, blessed by the shrine maidens and villagers of a bygone age.

History: Ako Domeki, called the Deathless Oni of Seirai, was a famed bandit and pirate from Seirai Island who led a rebellion against the Shogunate around 500 years ago and commanded over ten ships. The Seiraimaru was his flagship. The Shogunate's ships, and the island itself, were wrecked when Asase Hibiki unsealed the Thunder Manifestation to help his cause; the storm swept Ako and his crew away.

In his own words from the weapon text of "The Catch", Ako once called himself master of this ship, then found Seirai ruined on his return, with no home left in the Inazuman islands and even the "naggy" old shrine maiden gone. He sailed off again, vowing to see the edge of the world in her place.

Geography: The wreck sits close to a Thunder Sakura Bough on Seirai Island, whose centre was once swallowed by a perpetual thunderstorm.

Quests: Exploring the ship is a multi-stage puzzle. Four wheels by the mast must be turned so single-pointed "sword" marks face three-pointed "halberd" marks, opening a hatch into the hull. Seelie guide the way inside: a Rust-Worn Key and wheel puzzle unlock an Exquisite Chest, and an Intact Key does the same for a Luxurious Chest (and the Davy Jones' Locker achievement) before another Seelie Court.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ship remains a wreck on Seirai Island, nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes it.

190.content:
Serpent's Head (also: Serpent Head, Orobashi's skull): The Serpent's Head is the skull of the great serpent god Orobashi, the Watatsumi Omikami, left on Yashiori Island where the Electro Archon killed it. The weathered bones now form a landscape of their own: a subarea of Inazuma battered by rain and thunder. The skull still gazes at the sky, but the god is dead and its name is slowly being forgotten.

The Tatarigami left by the god's remains drove the island's people away. The sea wind through the skull's eyes and fangs is said to make a whistling sound, called the requiem the serpent composed for itself.

Geography: The Serpent's Head is a subarea of Yashiori Island, the bony remains of Orobashi's skull rising over the sea and surrounded by thunderstorms. A viewpoint, Overlooking Serpent Head, looks over it. Inside the serpent's mouth a closed grate blocks the way down to a Simple Tomb under the skull, which is opened by a short puzzle: chase two Electro Seelies to the serpent's eyes, pull a lever beside a Thunder Sakura Bough in the first chamber, defeat a Ruin Sentinel in the second and trip the door switches in order. In the bottom chamber lies Kikuchiyo's Simple Tomb, guarded by a Kairagi.

Narukami Pillars, Thunder Barriers and Thunder Sakura Boughs stand on and around the skull, and a gate in the bottom chamber leads out to the Serpent's Head Ward. Maguu Kenki, a boss on the island, and Nobushi, Kairagi, Fatui Cryo Cicin Mages and Treasure Hoarders also appear. Local specialties are Crystal Marrow, Dendrobium and Onikabuto.

History: After the Raiden Shogun and her twin Makoto united Inazuma, the other gods did not claim land that was not theirs. Orobashi, god of the Watatsumi people, was among them. Its island home was poor soil, and between the cries of its starving people and a decree from Celestia it invaded resource-rich Yashiori Island with a navy led by the shrine maiden Mouun and her sister Ayame. Ei gathered her troops and waged a brutal war, and slew Orobashi with Musou no Hitotachi, the blow splitting the island into two with Musoujin Gorge and leaving the god's remains across the land. The god's lingering hatred became the Tatarigami, which Ei suppressed with wards.

The Kitain Clan, descended from Kitain Bunsou, became the Yashiori Guardians who suppressed the Tatarigami, until the bloodline ended after Kitain Hideie's escape during the cataclysm. During the war between the Shogunate and Watatsumi that followed the Vision Hunt and Sakoku decrees, a radical faction of the Resistance, at the Fatui mole Nathan's urging and without Kokomi's knowledge, disguised itself as Shogunate troops and destroyed the wards, hoping to restore Orobashi's dignity. The Tatarigami broke free, sickening the villagers of Higi Village and the troops stationed on the island.

Quests: In Orobashi's Legacy the Traveler meets Kaji at Fort Fujitou, who is investigating the island's endless rain and lightning and traces it to broken ancient wards. One of the early parts (I to III) has the Traveler find missing Rock Pillar Warding Stones and Pearls and return them to the ward at the Serpent's Head, solving Sacred Stone Puzzles, as is also done at Musoujin Gorge and Jakotsu Mine. After the three wards are mended, Fort Mumei rises from the sea and the final, larger ward is repaired in Parts IV and V; the permanent rain and storm then cease.

The Simple Tomb puzzle also unlocks the full set of Kid Kujirai's Temari challenge.

Dangers: Constant rain and lightning until Orobashi's Legacy is completed, which applies Wet and can chain into Electro-Charged; Tatarigami influence; Maguu Kenki; Nobushi, Kairagi and Treasure Hoarders.

Atmosphere: A white skeleton so large that its fangs frame the sky, the wind whistling in its eye sockets, and endless thunderstorms trying to wash away the remains of a past that nobody here wants to repeat.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Serpent's Head remains a desolate, largely deserted site; the storms cease once Orobashi's Legacy is completed.

No 6.x or 7.x events concerning it were found on the wiki. The Fatui who lingered on Yashiori after the war are few.

191.content: Orobashi was born some 6,000 years ago, was defeated in the Archon War and fled Teyvat, ending up beyond the seal around Enkanomiya, where a child asked it to become their god. There it overthrew the Sunchildren's rule, learned the forbidden history in the book Before Sun and Moon and, for that knowledge, was judged by Celestia and allowed to sacrifice itself to spare its people. About 2,000 years ago it broke off its coral to make Watatsumi Island. It died fighting the Electro Archon. Its own entry carries its full story.

192.content: Ei's wards, tied to Narukami Pillars, suppressed the Tatarigami for centuries, but a group of Watatsumi radicals destroyed them. In Orobashi's Legacy, the Traveler, working with Kaji's investigation, mends them by returning Warding Stones and Pearls. Each repair clears the Tatarigami over its own area; the Serpent's Head, Musoujin Gorge and Jakotsu Mine come first, then Fort Mumei's ward.

193.content: Beneath the skull lies Kikuchiyo's Simple Tomb, one of the Simple Tombs on Yashiori Island, reached through the grate in the serpent's mouth.

194.content:
Shakkei Pavilion (also: Tutelage: Castle of Scrolls): Shakkei Pavilion is a one-time domain in Tatarasuna, Kannazuka, Inazuma. Its description says the magnificent mansion was built by an ancient ascetic warrior in the depths of the earth, using scenery borrowed from the outside world (shakkei, a garden-design principle), and was sealed at some point for reasons unknown.

It has a single level, Tutelage: Castle of Scrolls, and was added in Version 2.0. The entrance is hidden behind rocks that must be broken by firing a Kamuijima Cannon.

Geography: Deep within Tatarasuna's rocky mountains, a mansion of brittle floors (broken by plunging attacks), amulet shrines and a main door that opens when three amulets are placed.

It holds common and exquisite chests, and a precious chest appears after the final fight.

Dangers: Nobushi: Jintouban and Hitsukeban guard the shrines; the final room holds a Fatui Pyro Agent and a Mirror Maiden.

History: Before Version 3.3 the domain's description ended: 'In latter days, a deeply disheartened eccentric would be discovered within.' The wiki reads this as a veiled reference to the Wanderer (Scaramouche), called a kabukimono (eccentric) in Tatarasuna.

Per the wiki's summary of Inversion of Genesis, Nahida says the pavilion was like a birthplace for Scaramouche, that Raiden Ei left him there, and that Katsuragi of Tatarasuna found him after he had spent a long time in it. Treat as secondhand until re-read in the quest.

195.content:
Shirikoro Peak (also: Shirikoro-yama, Shirikoro Mountain): Shirikoro Peak is a rugged part of Tsurumi Island, the fog-shrouded island of Inazuma that once held two ancient civilisations. A great tree called a perch stands in a cave here, one of the places where the islanders once made offerings to the Thunderbird. Beneath the peak runs a stretch of underground ruins full of Electro puzzles, Seelie courts and ancient Ruin machines.

It is one of several perch sites (with Chirai Shrine, Autake Plains and the first perch) in the world quest series Through the Mists, where the Traveler helps the spirit of a boy named Ruu break a curse laid on the island by the Thunderbird. The name is Japanese Shirikoro-yama; "shirikoro" may come from the Ainu for "owning land".

Geography: The peak lies on Tsurumi Island, and its perch is inside a cave reached from the southeast, with three Seelie Courts nearby. Features of the peak include Mysterious Carvings, Phase Gates, Ruins Torches, Thunder Barriers and Thunder Sakura boughs. Local specialties are Fluorescent Fungus and Sea Ganoderma.

An underground cavern connects the peak to Chirai Shrine, and seven Stone Slates can be used there; the ruins can be opened and partly solved before Ruu's questline, though some puzzles and the hidden exploration objective need the quest steps. Three Star-Shaped Gems can be placed on the murals to release Electro Seelie. Waverider Waypoints and Lightning Strike Probes are also listed among its features.

Places: The perch cave. A broken dome holding a remarkable chest. Doors of the buried ruin that open when Electro Current puzzles are solved. Seelie courts around a central mechanism.

History: Tsurumi Island is the home of two ancient peoples: an older civilisation buried deep underground, and later the tribe that worshipped the Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir. The perches were trees where the Thunderbird once alighted, and the islanders believed offerings to them were needed. The story that unfolds in the quests: Ruu, child of the last priest Mata, befriended the Thunderbird by singing and named her Kanna Kapatcir; when the island declined he was chosen as a living sacrifice, which enraged her and she destroyed the village and cursed the island to relive its ruin.
