After the Traveler destroyed the perches in "The Sea of Fog and the Rite of the Trees", the ceremony fell into chaos under a crimson storm. In "The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna" the Peculiar Pinion shows that the curse can only lift when Kapatcir hears Ruu sing again. Because the Raiden Shogun had slain Kapatcir, the Traveler and Paimon bluff that she has moved to Seirai Island, and the Peculiar Pinion carries Ruu there to sing and the curse ends; the time loop closes, and Ruu is expected to pass on.

Atmosphere: A cave of roots and water, glowing fungus and quiet Electro, under a fogged island where the dead still seem to carry on their festival. It feels stilled, sad and a little uncanny.

Dangers: Hilichurl Fighters and Shooters, Samachurls, Electro Whopperflowers, and elites: Electro Abyss Mages, Wooden Shieldwall Mitachurls, Thundercraven Rifthound Whelps and several Ruin machines. The fog of Tsurumi Island teleports travellers away until cleared by the quests.

Travel: Reached by Kama's boat; the gate in the fog must be walked through during the quest to clear most of the island. A "Boatman" NPC is associated with the peak, and a follow-up hidden objective is called "Boatman's Task".

Quests: Through the Mists (2.2): A Particularly Particular Author includes the Shirikoro perch puzzle; it requires completing Seirai Stormchasers. Follow-up hidden objectives and The Saga of Mr. Forgetful continue the island's stories.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tsurumi Island's fog is gone and the curse is lifted, so the peak is a quiet ruin-filled hill.

Ruu is expected to pass on. No later canon through 7.1 changes the peak.

196.comment: Shirikoro Peak: Through the Mists and the Perches
196.content:
In A Particularly Particular Author, the author Sumida, whose commission is posted through the Adventurers' Guild, asks the Traveler to fetch a Maushiro from Tsurumi Island for her novel; Kama takes them across by boat, and the Bantan Sango Detective Agency also takes an interest. The Traveler meets a boy, Ruu, and helps make offerings to perches, including the one at Shirikoro Peak. The locals behave oddly because they are illusions replaying the past. The Maushiro is gone when delivered, as for every adventurer before. The series continues in Octave of the Maushiro, and ends with the curse lifted and the island's fog permanently cleared.

Shirikoro's perch cave requires guiding three Seelie to their courts to lower the water level and following the Thunderbird feathers through ruined doors, past Thundercraven Rifthound Whelps, Ruin Cruisers and a Ruin Guard. The Tsurumi Island time loop makes spawns change on a three-day cycle.

197.content:
Slumbering Court: Slumbering Court is a Domain of Blessing at Fort Hiraumi on Seirai Island, Inazuma. Its description says this great hall stood when Seirai Island had neither its present name nor the colour of thunder, and that the scenery within will probably never change. The masterless mansion has become a haunt of rifthounds.

Clearing it yields artifacts: Husk of Opulent Dreams, Ocean-Hued Clam, Defender's Will and Brave Heart. It was added in Version 2.3.

Geography: A great hall in the Fort Hiraumi area of Seirai Island, the island of the perpetual thunderstorm.

Dangers: Hydro slimes and a Crackling Axe Mitachurl at the lower levels, then Thundercraven Rifthound whelps and Rifthounds at the higher ones, with Electro Hilichurl Shooters.

In-game, party members gain a 40% Electro DMG Bonus and Electro-Charged reactions trigger a shockwave of true damage; recommended elements are Electro and Hydro. This is a mechanic, not story.

Atmosphere: Still and suspended, a hall that time forgot, with the island's lightning flickering outside.

key: Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God
198.content:
Statue of the Omnipresent God (also: Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God, Symbol of Eternity, Shogun's statue): The Statue of the Omnipresent God is a vast statue built in front of Tenshukaku in Inazuma City as the "Symbol of Eternity". It was raised after the Vision Hunt Decree so that every confiscated Vision could be embedded in it. Its Visions were taken away and returned to their owners after the Traveler defeated Ei in Chapter II. Its earlier English name was the Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God.

Ninety-nine Visions had been seized by the time of Amidst Stormy Judgment. Who the statue shows is never stated: many Inazumans simply call it the Shogun's statue.

Geography: It stands before Tenshukaku, the Raiden Shogun's residence on Narukami Island,. Visions are inlaid across its body, including Arataki Itto's, set near the bottom just above a Pyro Vision whose owner is unknown. After Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow, a Patrol Soldier stops anyone approaching it.

Its base is damaged. When the Traveler first reaches Narukami Island the statue is still under construction, according to Thoma, and a teaser for the story shows it hauled from the water with ropes. Wings, hooded robes and a great necklace on the figure are what the debate over its identity leans on.

History: The Vision Hunt Decree was issued by the Raiden Shogun and the Shogunate about a year before the story, to seize Visions across Inazuma and inlay them in the statue; the Tenryou Commission carried it out. It began as a Fatui plot to cause unrest and create a market for Delusions; Kujou Takayuki agreed to help in exchange for their promises of support, and deceived the Shogun into continuing it. Ei, the true Shogun, knew of the Fatui involvement but approved, believing individual ambition would only lead to loss and suffering and was incompatible with her ideal of eternity. The Traveler challenged Ei in her realm by showing her the power of the seized Visions' aspirations, and Ei repealed the decree. The Visions were removed from the statue and returned to their owners.

In a year 99 Visions were seized, and those who lost them suffered a loss of ambition, except Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu, who seemed unaffected. Those serving the Shogun, such as Kujou Sara, kept theirs. The war between the Shogunate and the Watatsumi Army grew from the decree and the Sakoku Decree issued at the same time.

Quests: Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow (Chapter II, Act II) is the quest in which the Vision Hunt Ceremony is the reason the decree is being carried out. In The Omnipresent God (Chapter II, Act III) and the quest Omnipresence Over Mortals, the Traveler defeats Ei and the Visions are returned to their rightful owners.

The achievement The Aspirations of All refers to the statue as the symbol of Eternity, as does Thoma in Three Wishes.

Atmosphere: A towering, many-eyed figure over the capital, gleaming with stolen Visions in the early part of the story; after Chapter II its inlays are empty, a monument to a policy that was reversed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the statue's Visions are gone: they were returned to their owners after Chapter II. The decree was repealed.

Its identity remains debated, and no 6.x or 7.x content on the wiki changes this.

199.comment: Statue of the Omnipresent God: Vision Hunt Decree
199.content: The decree ordered all Visions in Inazuma seized and inlaid in the Statue of the Omnipresent God. The Tenryou Commission enforced it. People who objected hid Visions or made decoys; many joined the Watatsumi Army. The decree is repealed in Chapter II, and the Visions are returned.

200.comment: Statue of the Omnipresent God: Debate over the Statue's Identity
200.content: Canon does not name the figure. Candidates include the Raiden Shogun (people say it is her statue; a quest description calls Ei the Omnipresent God), Ronova (the design shares her wings and hairstyle and is covered in eyes, and a text describes her as someone who sees, hears and judges all), the Heavenly Principles or Four Shades as a whole, or a personification of Eternity. Treat these as unproven.

201.content:
Suigetsu Pool (also: Suigetsu-chi, Water-Moon Pool): Suigetsu Pool, the "Water-Moon Pool", is a subarea of Watatsumi Island in Inazuma. A once-famous mansion belonging to the warrior Umigozen lies beneath it, and the place is covered with ancient ruins and Ruin Machines. The mansion is the setting of the one-time domain Palace in a Pool.

The domain's lore text says that long ago seawater had yet to fill the pool and moonlight filled it instead, flowing like quicksilver.

Geography: A sunken pool and a ruin-strewn stretch of Watatsumi Island, with a hole leading down to the mansion. Electro Seelie, Electro Current puzzles, Thunder Sakura Boughs, Lightning Strike Probes, Thunder Dwellings and a Waverider Waypoint are found here. Sango Pearl and Sea Ganoderma are local specialties.

The surface ruins and the passages beneath include Ruin Sentinels, an inactive Ruin Guard and a small inactive Ruin Hunter. To open the domain the player energises four Lightning Strike Probes with Electrograna to unlock Electro monuments, lowers the water, and drains it fully with a switch in a room beyond.

Places: Umigozen's Mansion (Palace in a Pool, the single level "Tutelage: Umigozen's Mansion"): once a grand house with a window for drinking wine and watching blossoms, now empty except for bandits, Nobushi and Treasure Hoarders, with sliding doors that hide amulets needed to open the last gate.

People: Umigozen is Yuna Ayame, a diver of the Yuna Clan of Watatsumi Island who lived about 2,000 years ago and was one of the leaders of the Watatsumi forces in the Narukami-Watatsumi War. Her older twin sister was the shrine maiden Mouun. She was the first owner of the weapon Wavebreaker's Fin and disappeared into the ocean at the war's end.

History: After the war the mansion stood abandoned; seawater covered it and its entrance was sealed. Today the only occupants are criminals using the place as a hideout.

Ayame and Mouun taught a nameless orphan who later became the king Touzannou, Akuou. In the war that began when Watatsumi invaded Yashiori Island, Ei ended the fighting by killing Orobashi and Akuou, while Mouun was ambushed and killed by tengu who served under Sasayuri. Ayame's Wavebreaker's Fin was separated from her during the war and taken by the tengu.

Dangers: Treasure Hoarders (Pugilists and Potioneers), Nobushi including a Mirror Maiden, and ancient Ruin Machines.

Quests: No world quest is set here in the pages read; the Palace in a Pool domain is the main attraction, and a torn page of the Toki Alley Tales storybook can be found in the ruins.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the mansion remains abandoned; no later canon read for this entry changes it.

202.content:
Tatarasuna (also: Tatara Sands): Tatarasuna is an island in Kannazuka, Inazuma, ringed by mountainous crags with a huge blast furnace, the Mikage Furnace, at its centre. It was where Inazuma smelted its famed Jade Steel, powered by Tatarigami energy. Twice it has gone wrong: about 400 years ago in the incident remembered as the Tatarasuna Mystery, and again in the war years when the furnace's runaway power and Fatui interest in it brought the Traveler to help. Today the furnace is purified and the area is quiet.

Its Japanese name is Tatara-suna, echoing the tatara, the traditional Japanese smelting furnace. In the Traveler's day the furnace sits inside a containment dome and its surroundings are tainted by Balethunder, until the Tatara Tales quest series settles it.

Geography: A rough island of jagged, mountainous crags enclosing a central depression where the Mikage Furnace stands. It belongs to Kannazuka, near Yashiori Island, whose Tatarigami energy fed the furnace. The ground is stony and wind-scoured, dotted with thunder sakura, electric currents, lightning-strike probes and old Kamuijima cannons.

The Mikage Furnace is surrounded by floating rock formations and bridges; a house on the lowest rock holds worker records. Shakkei Pavilion, on the island, is where a young man was found unconscious during the Tatarasuna Mystery.

Places: Mikage Furnace: the plant itself, the largest smelting facility in Inazuma's islands, built to produce Jade Steel in bulk. Shakkei Pavilion: a pavilion tied to the Mystery. Kamuijima cannons: three unused cannons on the eastern side, later fired to breach the containment dome.

The Arsenal, an Inazuman weapons store whose key was meant to be divided in three: one piece for the Inspector, one for the Armory Officer and one left in Tatarasuna. A worker's record says the staff withdrew in such haste, with neither official to be found, that the three pieces were hidden in treasure chests around the island instead.

People: Present day: Xavier, a Fontaine engineer who stayed behind to maintain the furnace; Toranosuke, a Shogunate soldier, and Miyuki, a shrine maiden, who quarrel over what to do about it; and Fatui agents who breached the dome. Four centuries ago: the Armory Officer Niwa Hisahide, Vice Armory Officer Miyazaki Kaneo, Inspector Mikoshi Nagamasa and his yoriki Katsuragi, plus Nozomu and Kinjirou of Nagamasa's entourage.

Before the war the workers were led by Kagami Gozen, who accompanied Alice on a visit. Individual biographies belong to their own entries.

History: Tatarasuna and its furnace were built to smelt Jade Steel, and Dottore later claimed the site had first been established to dispose of Crystal Marrow safely. Around 400 years ago the Armory Officer Niwa Hisahide, Inspector Mikoshi Nagamasa and Nagamasa's yoriki Katsuragi befriended a young man they called the kabukimono, who carried a golden feather. He later became the Wanderer, and before that the Balladeer. A black gas, Tatarigami power from Crystal Marrow used to speed up forging, began sickening workers around the furnace, and Niwa imposed an information blackout.

Truth revealed in the Sumeru Archon Quest: a mechanic calling himself Escher, from Fontaine, introduced a Crystal Marrow forging method. Niwa learnt the name was an alias and confronted him, but Escher was the Fatui Harbinger Dottore and killed Niwa; the whole affair was an experiment with the kabukimono as the main subject. The kabukimono sailed to Inazuma City to ask the Shogun for help and was refused, because Ei had already withdrawn to the Plane of Euthymia; he gave his golden feather to Yae Miko, who could only meet him briefly. He returned in despair, took a device from Escher, entered the furnace and absorbed the Tatarigami. Escher falsely said the device held the heart of a subordinate Niwa had killed, when it was Niwa's own heart. The kabukimono left Tatarasuna and was later found by the Jester and made a Harbinger.

Quests: Tatara Tales: an eight-quest World Quest series in which the Traveler and Xavier monitor the Mikage Furnace, break the containment dome with the old cannons, fend off Fatui, and finally purify the Tatarigami core. Unlocking it requires finishing Ritou Escape Plan.

After Tatara Tales the Balethunder at the furnace disappears and Hanayama Kaoru appears with a Flowery Plan exchange. Also relevant are the Archon Quest recollection of the Tatarasuna Mystery (3.3) and the achievement Mystery of Tatarasuna.

Dangers: Electro-aligned wildlife and cicins, Fatui skirmishers, hilichurls, Samachurl, Nobushi, Kairagi and Treasure Hoarders. Before Tatara Tales the area also inflicts Balethunder, a lingering Tatarigami charge that harms anyone who stays.

Atmosphere: Grey stone, orange furnace-glow, humming electric currents and the stillness left by an abandoned industry. Everything hints at departed workers: documents torn in a raid, hurriedly hidden keys, a vast furnace no one dares approach.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the furnace is purified and stable since Tatara Tales, and the island is a quiet ruin of industry.

The Tatarasuna Mystery is no longer a mystery to those who followed the Sumeru storyline: Nahida showed the Balladeer the truth. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the island.

203.content:
About 400 years ago workers at the Mikage Furnace fell ill from black gas of Tatarigami origin while a young kabukimono lived among the Inspector's circle. Public memory has Niwa Hisahide fleeing a crime and the kabukimono purifying the furnace; the truth is that Dottore, posing as a Fontaine mechanic, killed Niwa and used the kabukimono as a test subject. Blame fell on Mikoshi Nagamasa and cost Katsuragi and Nozomu their lives.

Niwa's information blackout kept the truth hidden for four centuries. The account given at the time, by the mechanic, was that Niwa had fled and the kabukimono had cleansed the furnace in his place; help from the Shogunate arrived but found no disaster. When Yae Miko heard this, she merely had the golden feather returned.

204.comment: Tatarasuna: Mikage Furnace and Tatara Tales
204.content:
The Mikage Furnace was the engine of Inazuma's Jade Steel, run on Tatarigami energy from Yashiori Island. During the Shogunate's war with the Watatsumi Army, saturation of that energy shut it down and even its auto-restart failed. Xavier raised a containment dome around it and kept the Balethunder in. Shogunate officials worried about halted production; shrine maidens feared the Tatarigami's spill-over, felt even at the Sacred Sakura.

The Fatui, interested in Tatarigami power, breached the dome. With three Kamuijima cannons the Traveler broke it open for Xavier, then helped him gather data, repair paths and purify the core. Earlier, before the war, Alice visited with Kagami Gozen and modified the furnace, improving the dome and limiting output for safety.

205.content:
Tenryou (also: Tenryou district, Inazuma Commercial Street, Emperor's Land): Tenryou is the commercial heart of Inazuma City, the district below Tenshukaku built around a bustling commercial street. It is one of the city's three parts, with Hanamizaka and Tenshukaku. Adventurers, shoppers, watchmen and Shogunate officials mix here, among teahouses, restaurants, craftsmen, the Adventurers' Guild and a police station.

The word tenryou is not the same as the Tenryou Commission, though they share a root: the Commission is the arm of the Shogunate that keeps public order, and the district is where much of that order is visible, in its watchmen, notices and the nearby Commission headquarters.

Geography: Tenryou lies just below Tenshukaku on the city's hillside, where Inazuma City rises on the southern tip of Narukami Island. Its main feature is a commercial street. Komore Teahouse, Uyuu Restaurant, the Aisa Bathhouse, the police station and a park lie off it.

The Tenryou Commission Headquarters is classed under Tenshukaku rather than Tenryou, but its watchmen are seen in the district constantly. A small park area is home to a resident named Oda Tarou.

Places: Commercial street: the Adventurers' Guild receptionist Katheryne, shop owners and street-food vendors.
Komore Teahouse: a members-only teahouse owned by the Yashiro Commission, used by the Kamisato clan as a local base and private meeting place. Its boss is a Shiba Inu named Taroumaru.
Aisa Bathhouse: a Natlan-inspired bathhouse owned and run by the returnee Aikawa Susumu, with rumours of a special investor behind the scenes.
Uyuu Restaurant: run by Okazaki Rikuto and Okazaki Erika.
Police Station: the yoriki Owada and the watchman Uesugi work here.

Shops include Ogura Textiles & Kimonos (Ogura Mio), Yayoi Lacquerware (Yayoi Nanatsuki), Tsukumomono Groceries (Aoi), Netsuke no Gen Crafts (Mikoshi Genichirou) and Shimura's (Shimura Kanbei), plus street-food vendors such as Yukio and Tomoki. The teahouse's staff includes Kozue, a shop assistant who is the subject of a bulletin board joke and a police file.

People: Adventurers such as Furuya Noboru, Satou, Takeda and Yuzu use the street; the researcher Tang Wen, the gourmet Matsumoto and the watchman Sanada are among the regulars. The Guild receptionist Katheryne is here.

Komore Teahouse patrons and staff include Heihachi, Nakanishi, Nobumori and Ramsay. Taroumaru is a former ninja dog of the Shuumatsuban.

Governance: Tenryou is the city district the Tenryou Commission watches most closely. The Commission, led by the Kujou clan, manages security and military affairs and enforced the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees. Its yoriki and doushin are the police of the district.

After the Inazuma Archon Quest, Tenryou Commissioner Kujou Takayuki is under house arrest for colluding with the Fatui and Kujou Kamaji acts in his place; Ei challenged the Takatsukasa clan head for the post, Kamaji accepted the duel instead, and Ei decided to give the Kujou clan more time. A Tenryou notice about Takayuki was posted on the commercial street's bulletin board.

Culture: Tenryou is the city's shopping and dining quarter. Inazuma City is renowned for family businesses and a low crime rate, and Tenryou's street has lacquerware, textile and netsuke shops, a grocer, a restaurant, a teahouse and street-food vendors.

The Aisa Bathhouse is called a go-to place to relax and is visited by Tenryou Commission samurai.

History: The district's recent history is the war period under the Decrees, then peace after the Archon Quest. Later, after the Natlan events, the Aisa Bathhouse was renovated at the direction of Yumemizuki Mizuki, who became its main investor and decision-maker, adding therapy sessions run by yumekui-baku psychologists.

Yumemizuki Mizuki is working to expand the brand to Watatsumi Island and to Natlan.

Atmosphere: A busy street of shops below the Shogun's castle, with street-food vendors, watchmen in the crowd and adventurers coming and going. During the war the same street had a sharper edge, with notices, aid queues and rumours.

Dangers: Inazuma City is renowned for low crime. The district's dangers belong to the Decree era: arrests by the Tenryou Commission and its warrants and wanted notices.

Travel: The Adventurers' Guild's Inazuma receptionist, Katheryne, works on the commercial street, making it the usual first stop for travellers.

Quests: The Traveler is wanted by the Tenryou Commission after escaping the Vision Hunt Ceremony; later, the Komore Teahouse's staff figure in the quest "Three Wishes", and the Aisa Bathhouse in the quest "Dream Eater's Melancholia".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tenryou is a safe, prosperous market district; the Decrees are over.

The Aisa Bathhouse is now a therapy-and-spa venue under Yumemizuki Mizuki. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 plot is set in the district.

206.content:
Komore Teahouse is a members-only teahouse in Tenryou, owned by the Yashiro Commission and used by the Kamisato clan as a local base and private meeting place. Only people approved by the Kamisato clan may enter. Its boss is the Shiba Inu Taroumaru, a former ninja dog of the Shuumatsuban, and customers leave their payment in a box after drinking tea.

Staff are said to have signed a contract with Taroumaru to work there forever, a joke repeated by the shop assistant Kozue. The teahouse is mentioned in the descriptions of several furnishings, such as candlestands that burn without scent.

207.content:
The Aisa Bathhouse is an indoor bathhouse in Tenryou inspired by Natlan's hot springs, offering baths, fine dining and, since its renovation, psychotherapy from yumekui-baku. Aikawa Susumu, a returnee from Natlan, is the operator.

After the events of Incandescent Ode of Resurrection, the bathhouse was renovated at the direction of Yumemizuki Mizuki, its core investor and decision-maker, who is expanding the brand to Watatsumi Island and Natlan. Many Tenryou Commission samurai visit it.

208.content:
Tenryou Commission Headquarters (also: Tenryou-bugyou-fu, Tenryou Commission Office): The Tenryou Commission Headquarters is the seat in Inazuma City of the Tenryou Commission, the executive arm of the Shogunate. The Commission is led by the Kujou Clan and handles security and military affairs; in the Archon Quests it is the organisation that carries out the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree. The building has a courtyard exterior and an interior that the story opens in Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage.

The Commission is also the one the story exposes: its head, Kujou Takayuki, concealed the cost of the war from the Shogun and dealt with the Fatui. It remains in disarray, with Kujou Kamaji standing in as acting head.

Geography: The headquarters is a point of interest in Inazuma City on Narukami Island, near Tenshukaku. It has an outdoor courtyard, where Shogunate samurai, yoriki and doushin keep watch, and an interior instance, entered as a quest domain during the Archon Quest. The courtyard NPCs listed on the wiki are Ikeda Soushirou, the yoriki Mikoshi Genjirou and Yata Kouki, and the doushin Watanabe; Okawara Goemon, also a yoriki, is in the interior.

People: The Commission's personnel include Kujou Kamaji (acting clan head), Kujou Sara (General), Kujou Masahito (General), Okawara Goemon (Chief Samurai and Kujou Clan security head), and rank-and-file Shogunate Samurai, yoriki and doushin. Shikanoin Heizou is a Tenryou "Detective". Kujou Takayuki is a past commissioner who is under house arrest.

The Commission suffers a higher desertion rate than the other two, since the Vision Hunt Decree put its soldiers in fights against people rather than ancient monsters and Abyss denizens.

Governance: Of the three Commissions (Tenryou, Kanjou, Yashiro) in the Tri-Commission, the Tenryou Commission is the Raiden Shogun's executive arm, responsible for security and military matters including enforcement of the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree. The three Commissions share equal authority and can check each other.

After the events of Omnipresence Over Mortals the Commission is in disarray over Takayuki's collusion with the Fatui, and the Shogun planned to punish him in due course. In the Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter (Act I), Ei offers the post of Tenryou Commissioner as the prize of a duel; Takatsukasa Susumu refuses, Kujou Kamaji accepts knowing he will lose, and Ei afterwards says she will give the Kujou Clan more time.

History: The Traveler is placed on a wanted list by the Commission after escaping the Vision Hunt Ceremony with Thoma. Later, in Omnipresence Over Mortals, the Traveler and Yae Miko show Kujou Sara a Commission document that omits the cost of the war and a letter to the Fatui. Sara goes to the headquarters to demand an explanation.

In Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage Sara leads the Traveler into the headquarters as an instance: they defeat Commission guards, then reinforcements, then the Kujou Clan Internal Affairs Head, Takatsukasa Tokibeitetsu, who summons bodyguards, before the Traveler speaks with Takayuki.

Atmosphere: A formal military-bureaucratic compound: guards at the gate, officers moving papers, the strain of an institution that has turned on its own conscience. It is quieter in the courtyard than inside.

Quests: Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage (Chapter II, Act III: Omnipresence Over Mortals). The courtyard is also an ordinary map location with Tenryou NPCs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the headquarters is still the Tenryou Commission's seat. The commissioner's post stays unsettled: Kujou Kamaji acts as head and the Kujou Clan was given more time. Many Tenryou samurai relax at the Aisa Bathhouse.

209.comment: Tenryou Commission Headquarters: Takayuki's collusion with the Fatui
209.content: Kujou Takayuki, the commissioner and Kujou clan head, was shown by Yae Miko and the Traveler to have hidden the war's cost from the Raiden Shogun and to have exchanged a secret letter with the Fatui. Sara, who had served the Kujou Clan loyally, was shaken and went to confront him in the headquarters. Later accounts place him under house arrest.

210.comment: Tenryou Commission Headquarters: Tenryou Commission and the Vision Hunt Decree
210.content: The Commission enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree for the Shogun. Its soldiers fight other people, including the Watatsumi Army, which led to desertions. Distinguish its official line from what individual soldiers privately think.

211.content:
Tenshukaku (also: Tenshu, Shogun's residence): Tenshukaku is the castle keep at the top of Inazuma City on Narukami Island, the residence of the Raiden Shogun and the place from which she rules Inazuma. Built during the Archon War, it is one of the three parts of the city alongside Hanamizaka and Tenryou, and the Tenryou Commission Headquarters stands within its grounds. The Statue of the Omnipresent God, built to hold Visions confiscated under the Vision Hunt Decree, stands before it.

Its name means a castle's tower keep, literally "heavenly protector". Official material describes it as the residence of the most exalted one in Inazuma, standing on the city's highest point and watching over all under the Electro Archon's rule. Entry into the Shogun's presence is tightly controlled.

Geography: Inazuma City rises on cliffs at the southern tip of Narukami Island. Tenshukaku crowns it, above the city's other two parts, Hanamizaka and Tenryou. The Statue of the Omnipresent God stands in front of the keep.

Places: Entrance area, guarded by Shogunate officers; a central courtyard where officials go about their business; a southern tower; the Tenryou Commission Headquarters with its courtyard and offices; and the Shogun's throne chamber, where she receives visitors and where the duel before the throne was fought.

The building is decorated with antler-like ornaments of the kind worn as crests on samurai helmets. The chamber where the Shogun was found pacing alone during her seclusion is entered through the same doors that lead to the scene of the duel with Signora.

People: The Raiden Shogun resides here: the puppet Shogun who handles Inazuma's affairs, with Ei meditating within her Plane of Euthymia. The Tenryou Commission, led by the Kujou Clan, works out of its headquarters here. Okuzumeshuu guards such as Takeshi control access to the Shogun.

After the war, Kujou Kamaji, acting head of the Kujou Clan, is often found near the entrance. Other officials seen around the keep include yoriki and doushin of the Tenryou Commission, hatamoto retainers, the tax secretary Takatsukasa Tomohide, Mikawa Akane of the Royal Bath Commission, and the reserve official Nagaoka Hidemitsu.

Governance: Tenshukaku is the seat of the Raiden Shogun's rule over the Inazuma Shogunate. The Tenryou Commission, the Shogun's executive arm in charge of security and the military, enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree from here. Inazuman law recognises the duel before the throne, fought in the Shogun's presence with her approval; the loser dies.

The Shogun holds that the right to punish Inazumans for their crimes is hers alone. During the 2.1 Archon Quest the Fatui Harbinger Signora, styling herself a Snezhnayan diplomat, was before the throne when Kujou Sara stormed in after learning that the Tenryou Commissioner Kujou Takayuki had been colluding with the Fatui. After the war Kujou Kamaji took on his father Takayuki's position as acting head of the Kujou Clan.

History: Inazuma City, Tenshukaku included, was built during the Archon War. A year before the Traveler's arrival the Vision Hunt Decree began, and the statue in front of the keep was built to receive confiscated Visions. In 2.0 the Shogun personally presided over a ceremony there marking the hundredth Vision. In 2.1 the Traveler defeated Signora in a duel before the throne inside Tenshukaku, and the Shogun executed her.

At the Vision Hunt Ceremony, the Traveler snatched back Thoma's Vision; the Shogun named them an "exception" and an enemy of eternity, overpowered them, and let them escape only when Thoma created a distraction. The Traveler became a wanted criminal and joined the resistance.

Atmosphere: Formal, hushed and guarded. Officials pass through the courtyard, and the guards at the entrance remind visitors to behave impeccably in the Shogun's presence. Before the throne the Shogun's word is law, and her judgment can be final.

Dangers: Entering without leave is dangerous: during her seclusion the Shogun's first words to the Traveler were that trespassers are to be eliminated at once. A duel before the throne ends in the death of the loser.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter II: "Amidst Stormy Judgment" (Act II, 2.0) at the statue before the keep; "Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage", "Duel Before the Throne" and "The Omnipresent God" (Act III, 2.1). Raiden Shogun Story Quest: "The Lonesome Euthymia" (Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter, Act I).

The Trounce Domain "Narukami Island: Tenshukaku" re-creates the battle with Signora as a gameplay memory; this replay is not a new event in the story.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tenshukaku remains the Raiden Shogun's residence and seat of rule. The Vision Hunt Decree was abolished in 2.1, Signora died here, and Ei has since reconsidered how she rules.

After the war Ei briefly withdrew into seclusion inside Tenshukaku, temporarily disabling many of the puppet's functions rather than modifying its rules while she worked out the form Eternity should take; she then went out among her people in person. No later story found is set at Tenshukaku in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya).

212.content: A duel before the throne is a contest under Inazuman law, fought in the Raiden Shogun's presence at Tenshukaku with her consent; the loser forfeits their life. Signora called it making the law of the land work for you. The Traveler invoked it against Signora in 2.1; after her defeat the Shogun herself carried out the sentence with the Musou no Hitotachi and, acknowledging the victor's honour, let the Traveler leave Tenshukaku alive.

213.comment: Tenshukaku: The Shogun's seclusion and the Pass Permit
213.content: For a time after the war the Shogun saw no one, and rumours spread in the city that she was unwell. Only Yae Miko held a Pass Permit allowing entry to Tenshukaku and an audience with the Shogun, kept for emergencies and apparently never used; she lent it to the Traveler, and the guard Takeshi, astonished that it was genuine, let them in. Inside, the half-disabled puppet threatened them as trespassers before Ei drew them into the Plane of Euthymia and agreed to walk among her people.

key: The Altar at The Serpent's Heart
214.comment: The Altar at The Serpent's Heart
214.content:
The Altar at The Serpent's Heart (also: Altar at the Serpent's Heart, Serpent's Heart altar): The altar at the Serpent's Heart is a circular chamber in Enkanomiya with five blue wall panels, each tied to a different Key Sigil. In Evernight, entering a sigil pattern in the right order makes it spawn a chest, an enemy or a spirit, and two world quests start here.

It is where the Traveler first recovers a fragment of the Reins of Revival, and where the afterimage of the resistance leader Supada no Hiko is found, unable to leave.

Geography: The room sits at the heart of the Serpent's Heart island. A mechanism to the north-east switches the area to Evernight, which is needed to use the altar.

An Altar Pattern is a set of the five Key Sigil types arranged in a circle, each with one to five dots. The pattern must first be activated elsewhere in Enkanomiya, then entered here by walking into the panels in dot order. Right steps light the sigils and send the player back to the centre; a wrong one leaves the panels dark.

Quests: The Heart of Ouroboros (part of From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku) has the Traveler solve the altar's first riddle to receive the first Reins of Revival fragment. In Lotus Eater, an afterimage here, bound by the altar's prison, asks for help recovering his name.

The tablet near the altar names him as Spartacus the Righteous, now Supada no Hiko, and records a curse in the name of Tokoyo Ookami. He says the prison grinds away his soul and memories and wishes to send a message to his students. The quest leads to Adonis in The Narrows and ultimately the Dragonbone Flower.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the altar stays as released in 2.4 and has no further role in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content.

215.content:
The Arsenal (also: Tatarasuna Arsenal): The Arsenal is a cave under Tatarasuna in Kannazuka, south of the Mikage Furnace, where the Tatarasuna workers hid a ruined blade. The Daitatara Nagamasa was forged by Inspector Mikoshi Nagamasa and became "Katsuragikiri Nagamasa" after he cut down his yoriki Katsuragi with it.

Inside lies a Luxurious Chest holding the diagram for forging a replica of that sword.

Geography: The cave lies south of the Mikage Furnace; the gate is near the water on its eastern side. The surrounding furnace area is blocked by a Containment Field until part of the Tatara Tales quest is completed.

Three Keys to Some Place found in Tatarasuna's Common Chests open the gate. On first entry three Ruin Sentinels spawn. The cave also holds an Electroculus and an Enigmatic Page. Gameplay note: the Luxurious Chest has Primogems, Mora and Hero's Wit as well as the Diagram: Katsuragikiri Nagamasa, which gives the Blade of Tatara achievement.

History: Per the wiki account, Mikoshi Nagamasa, Tatarasuna's Shogunate inspector, grew fond of bladesmithing and forged the Daitatara Nagamasa with the Vice Armory Officer Miyazaki. His group celebrated: Nozomu painted the blade, while Katsuragi and a nameless wandering eccentric performed a sword dance. Soon afterward the group broke up.

The notes say Nagamasa flew into a rage over Katsuragi's alleged misdeed, slashed him with the blade (giving it its new name) and threw it into the furnace. Nozomu pulled the melted sword out and died of his burns that night. Kinjiro, with Miyazaki sharing his fear that Nagamasa could not be reasoned with, hid the remains and Nozomu's painting in the Arsenal.

Quests: Tatara Tales opens the furnace area; the Rather Aged Notes scattered around the Mikage Furnace recount the incident, and they read as if seized in a raid on the Fatui.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Arsenal stands unchanged as an explorable cave, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes the Tatarasuna story.

216.content:
The Emanant Skylight (also: Emanant Skylights): The Emanant Skylight names three places in Enkanomiya where a pool of ghostfish waits during Evernight. Gliding into the fish lifts the Traveler to a time tunnel that opens onto one of the three Locus subareas.

The fish only appear after the world quest The Three Great Martial Trials has been started, and Bathysmal Vishaps guard each pool.

Places: The skylight at The Narrows leads to Yachimatahiko's Locus; the one at the Evernight Temple to Yachimatahime's Locus; the one at the Serpent's Heart to Kunado's Locus.

Each skylight is guarded by a Primordial Bathysmal Vishap and two hatchlings. Ghostfish are schools that let the Traveler keep gliding if they stay inside the group.

Quests: The Three Great Martial Trials starts with Eboshi (Erebos), who calls herself an auxiliary of Sangonomiya, one of Enkanomiya's shrine maidens. She says the older trial to win the branch was meant to keep the full truth from later generations, whereas she wanted records kept, so Watatsumi Omikami let her add a path leading to the secrets. Starting the quest reveals the three Locus subareas.

Eboshi says that, because of the Sinshades phenomenon, Enkanomiya's past would persist on its own, so Sangonomiya worked to make the people forget; she disagreed and the two settled the matter with Omikami's mediation. Her clue refers to gazing upon the borders of Byakuyakoku in Evernight.

Atmosphere: Dim ceiling openings pouring light into dark cavern waters, with fish that rise like a stairway of ghosts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the three skylights remain tied to The Three Great Martial Trials, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes them.

217.content:
The Narrows (also: Narrows of Enkanomiya): The Narrows is a ruined subarea of Enkanomiya. In the earliest times it was squeezed between the mountain face and an area called the Roundlands, which gave it its name. Strange tectonic shifts in Byakuyakoku later dropped the Roundlands into the depths, so the Narrows widened considerably. Its ruins hide a chamber that only appears when the land shifts between Whitenight and Evernight.

That chamber, sealed by a Sunfire Phantasm, held one of the Reins of Revival fragments the Traveler sought in The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent. A hiding place used by Byakuyakoku's resistance also lies here.

Geography: A broad ruin-filled stretch of the Enkanomiya underground, with cliffs on one side and, where the Roundlands once stood, open depths on the other. The land shifts between Whitenight and Evernight, revealing or hiding structures.

The walkthrough for Lotus Eater notes a chest behind the afterimage holding a Secret Room Key, which belongs to a separate Hidden Exploration Objective, Adonis' Abandoned Safehouse.

Places: The Narrows ruins, and the hidden chamber for the fragment; a hiding place opened by a lantern puzzle during Whitenight, where an afterimage waits.

A Sunfire Phantasm conceals the chamber entrance, and Aru says its exact position must be found by the Traveler alone by switching between Whitenight and Evernight.

People: No living inhabitants. The guide Aru speaks of the Narrows, and an afterimage in the hiding place is met during Lotus Eater.

History: From the Byakuyakoku texts: in the earliest times the Narrows lay between the mountain face and the Roundlands. Tectonic upheaval brought the Roundlands down into the depths and widened the place.

Aru says the people of Byakuyakoku later learnt to use Sunfire Phantasms to conceal secrets; the chamber's entrance is one example. Supada no Hiko's quest sends the Traveler to find where his 'children' are hidden; the hiding place is in the Narrows.

Quests: The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent (the fragment) and Lotus Eater (the hiding place).

Dangers: The wiki lists no special hazards for this subarea beyond Enkanomiya's usual enemies.

Atmosphere: Dark, broken stonework above an abyssal drop, with the quiet of a place where something collapsed long ago.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Narrows are unchanged and the chamber is empty.

No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content touches Enkanomiya.

218.content:
The Serpent's Bowels (also: Serpent's Bowels): The Serpent's Bowels is a quiet subarea of Enkanomiya, the underground realm of Byakuyakoku. The wiki lists the Sangonomiya Shrine as its entrance. It is a damp network of caverns with silently flowing underground rivers, and no battle music plays here. It holds the giant Dragonbone Flower.

Its waters are home to fish, and the area includes a waterfall near which a rusted blade of the Iwakura Clan can be found, a link to Narukami Island's Byakko Plain. A note found here recalls how Watatsumi's people unwittingly fed the Bathysmal Vishaps.

Geography: Caverns and tunnels of wet stone, a great gate and rivers that run in silence. The fishing point's in-game description suggests, as speculation, that these waters might link the place to the outside world.

A waterfall lies near where the Iwakura blade is found. The Pathway to the Hidden Isles music accompanies the area.

Places: The Dragonbone Flower: a giant flower atop which, in Lotus Eater, the Traveler pours the Waters of Lethe. A great gate, a fishing point and a spot with damp Scribbled Notes.

The Hakuen Michimitsu Amenoma lies near the waterfall once the Hidden Exploration Objective Iwakura Art's Downfall has been done. Sango Pearls are the local specialty.

People: No residents. Only scribbled notes remain, left by an unnamed traveller who journeyed with Watatsumi's chosen hero.

History: The Scribbled Notes say the Bathysmal Vishaps suddenly became active, but a clerk of the Sangonomiya Shrine convinced the writer and the hero to spare them. The people of Watatsumi, throwing food offerings into the Moon-Bathed Deep, had been feeding the creatures, and the clerk said they could no longer threaten humanity, so Enkanomiya was best returned to them.

Hydrological Studies in Byakuyakoku notes the sealing of the depths and the emigration of Watatsumi's people. The Dragonbone Flower shares its name with the flower a child sought in the folktale of Vol. 1, though no text identifies the two.

Quests: Lotus Eater, in which the flower is watered; the Hidden Exploration Objectives Iwakura Art's Downfall and Adonis' Abandoned Safehouse touch the region.

Dangers: No battle music; the wiki does not list any enemies here.

Atmosphere: Damp stone, silent rivers and the sense of a place almost forgotten.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is unchanged: empty, quiet, with the flower still standing.

No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content touches Enkanomiya.

219.content: A giant flower in the Serpent's Bowels. In Lotus Eater, the Traveler pours the Waters of Lethe on it, waits until the next daily reset and takes the Dragonbone Orb; the orb is said to make one forget. The Waters of Lethe flow near the Evernight Temple and do not themselves cause forgetfulness when drunk.

220.content:
The Serpent's Heart (also: Serpent's Heart, Delphi, Heart of Ouroboros): The Serpent's Heart is a subarea of Enkanomiya, the underground realm of Byakuyakoku. It was made with the power of Sunfire Phantasms, to guard secrets, imprison criminals and worship the great imaginary serpent Ouroboros. At its centre stands an altar regarded as the heart of that Cosmic Serpent, a sealing device for storing important objects. Its oldest name was Delphi, the Serpent's Land.

Its name predates the arrival of Orobashi, the Watatsumi Omikami, and did not change after it. The Traveler retrieved a Reins of Revival fragment from the altar during the quest The Heart of Ouroboros.

Geography: A cavernous zone of Enkanomiya's underground sea. It is where space itself is said to overlap, a phenomenon the early Enkanomiyans noticed when they first found the place, and which they used to build the prison-vault.

A cave in its northern cliffs leads to the ruins where the Lotus Eater quest begins. Altar Patterns, Key Sigil seals, and day-night mechanisms scattered here change with Whitenight and Evernight.

Places: The Altar at the Serpent's Heart: the vault itself; patterns entered here retrieve stored objects. The Emanant Skylight: a spot with a pool and a Time Tunnel that leads to Kunado's Locus once the trials begin.

Cave systems, ancient stone tablets and a hiding place in the Narrows connect with the altar's puzzles. Messages about the altar's codes were scattered around Enkanomiya.

People: No standing population. An afterimage at the altar names itself Supada no Hiko (Spartacus), a resistance leader imprisoned here; he has forgotten his own name until the Traveler restores it. The guide Aru supplied information about the fragments during The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent.

The afterimage claims Byakuyakoku's nobles, who guard the Sunchild, were the real rulers, and that the prison erodes souls and memories.

History: The Byakuyakoku Collection describes the site as discovered with its overlapping-space phenomenon already present. Ancestors later built the Serpent's Heart on it. Before Orobashi arrived it was known as the Heart of Ouroboros; Delphi kept its name afterwards.

The altar functions through strict entry procedures: the right pattern retrieves the right object, which makes it equally useful as a prison. Aru says the codes were scattered across Enkanomiya. The site was among those that held fragments of the Reins of Revival, along with the Evernight Temple and the Narrows.

Quests: The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent (the fragment hunt), The Heart of Ouroboros (a Reins of Revival fragment is taken from the altar), and Lotus Eater (a side quest begun at the altar).

Dangers: Ruin Sentinels guard parts of the zone, and Abyss and hilichurl enemies are found in Enkanomiya generally. Switching between Whitenight and Evernight is part of exploring safely.

Atmosphere: A hushed vault beneath the world, lit by Sunfire glow, where altar mechanisms click into place and old prisoners' voices linger as afterimages.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the altar's prize is gone and the prison is empty save for afterimages.

The Byakuyakoku texts record the sealing of the depths and the emigration of Watatsumi's people; the Serpent's Heart is a relic of that age. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content revisits it.

221.comment: The Serpent's Heart: Delphi and Ouroboros
221.content: The Enkanomiyans revered snakes even before Orobashi became their patron. Ouroboros, also called the great imaginary serpent or Cosmic Serpent, was worshipped from the earliest times, and Delphi meant the land of snakes. After Orobashi came, they worshipped both. Ancient art depicts Ouroboros as scaleless and Orobashi as coral-adorned.

222.comment: The Serpent's Heart: Supada no Hiko
222.content: In the Lotus Eater quest an afterimage in the altar says he led a resistance against Byakuyakoku's nobles and that his students, whom he calls his children, hold the nation's hope. He forgot his name under the prison's erosion; the Traveler restores it from an ancient tablet naming him as Supada no Hiko and the 'Righteous', condemned as a bandit.

223.content:
Tokoyo Reisen (also: River Lethe, Waters of Lethe): Tokoyo Reisen, once known as the River Lethe, is a stream in the Evernight Temple area of Enkanomiya. Its water glows faintly in the dark. In the World Quest Lotus Eater the Traveler collects the Waters of Lethe here to grow a Dragonbone Orb, a fruit whose scent calms the mind and makes people forget their worries.

The water itself does not erase memory; only the orb made with its help does. The wiki notes the name echoes the River Lethe of Greek myth, whose water made the dead forget.

Geography: The stream runs near the Evernight Temple in Enkanomiya and is one of the places the Traveler is sent to in Lotus Eater. The water shines weakly in the darkness and looks unremarkable to Paimon on first sight.

The water is carried to the Dragonbone Flower, atop which it is poured; the orb condenses overnight, taking until the next daily reset. The Evernight Temple's wider neighbourhood is a region of Hilichurls, Abyss mages and Ruin machines.

History: Lotus Eater tells how a resistance member in Byakuyakoku, Adonis, and his comrades sold Dragonbone Orbs to fund their cause against the nobles. Soon they found that members of the resistance began to avoid conflict and asked to leave, which Adonis blames on contentment: when oppressed peoples grow satisfied they cease to resist. He suspects the orb's formula may have been leaked by the rulers, though he cannot say. He tells the Traveler that the orbs can only be made with the water of Tokoyo Reisen.

The Traveler meets the afterimage of a resistance fighter who has forgotten his own name and wants to find his "children", his students, who hide in the Narrows; this leads to Adonis.

Quests: Lotus Eater starts at the Altar at the Serpent's Heart and requires The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent. Its steps include going to Tokoyo Reisen, obtaining the Waters of Lethe, going to the top of the Dragonbone Flower, watering it, and collecting the Dragonbone Orb after a day. Afterwards the orb can be sold in a side objective.

The quest also yields a Secret Room Key for a separate hidden exploration objective, Adonis' Abandoned Safehouse.

Atmosphere: A dim stream of faintly glowing water in a cave of the temple, quiet and half-lit, with a faint glow that hints at the orb's quiet danger.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tokoyo Reisen is unchanged and still the source of the Waters of Lethe. No later story involves it.

224.content: A Dragonbone Orb is a rare fruit a Dragonbone Flower bears when watered with the Waters of Lethe. Its fragrance relaxes the mind and sweeps away worry, so it fetched a high price, and eventually the resistance in Byakuyakoku used its sale for funds. Its effect on the buyer is forgetting. The item text for the Waters of Lethe says the water by itself will not cause forgetting.

225.content:
Tsurumi Island: Tsurumi Island is a remote island of Inazuma that was long wrapped in a dense fog and avoided for years. It holds the remains of two vanished peoples. The older one was linked to Celestia and lies buried underground. The later one was a tribe that worshipped the Thunderbird, Kanna Kapatcir. When the boy Ruu was sacrificed to her, the Thunderbird destroyed the tribe in grief and rage and cursed the island to relive its final days. The Traveler helped Ruu's spirit keep his promise to sing for her again. That lifted the curse and the fog, and the island's spirits are now passing on.

No one lives there now apart from hilichurls, riftwolves and old automatons. Kama, who ferried the Traveler over from Ritou and has since been seen travelling with Sumida, is the tribe's only known living descendant.

Geography: A hilly island of grassland, beaches and ruins. Mt. Kanna, the tribe's sacred ground where the Thunderbird dwelt, rises in the centre. The Moshiri Ceremonial Site was where the rites were held. Shirikoro Peak and Chirai Shrine stand over a network of underground ruins. The coasts include Oina Beach and Wakukau Shoal, and the open Autake Plains lie inland. Wooden "Perches" for offerings once stood around the island.

The Tsurumi Underground Ruins link Shirikoro Peak and Chirai Shrine, and both civilisations left remnants in them, including murals of Celestia. Offshore islets surround Moshiri Kara, a masterless mansion whose builder nobody knows. Riftwolves now prowl it. Even after the curse ended, thin haze drifts over the ground, and fog still sits on the sea a little way out.

People: The island has no living inhabitants. Until the curse was lifted, illusions of the tribe re-enacted the final ceremony. Ruu alone among them became self-aware: he noticed changes on the island and the passing of time without understanding why. After the curse ended, spirits of the dead appeared, and a mysterious "Boatman" began ferrying them to a "golden land" once their last wishes were settled.

Known members of the tribe include Ruu, Abe, Ipe, Kina, Kito, Makiri, Mata, Onkami and Una, along with an illusory figure called "Kama" whom the Traveler saw burying the Maushiro. The living Kama in Ritou descends from tribespeople who left the island. In Inazuma City, the novelist Sumida commissioned adventurers to find the tribe's "Maushiro" for her book.

Culture: The Thunderbird tribe worshipped Kapatcir with fear and gratitude, read her unpredictable actions as divine revelations, and chose shamans to offer blood sacrifices. They called to each other through the fog with the Maushiro, at first an instrument made from her feathers and later a wooden imitation. They were taught never to leave the island, since anyone who did was believed lost in the "sea of darkness". The fog, they thought, was the Thunderbird's protection.

The tribe had a strict hierarchy with priests at the top, and they wrote in the Ishine Script. They used an amethyst hourglass to predict the Thunderbird's arrival and held a festival when she came. Ruu repeats the adults' "Rule of Three": a thing must be done three times to get a result.

History: In the age of the ancient unified civilisation, a people connected to Celestia lived on Tsurumi and worshipped the Three Moons. "Strange objects" later fell from the heavens, destroying that civilisation and producing the fog. Kanna Kapatcir, the Thunderbird who made the island her home, saw this and left the fog in place although she could have dispersed it. Later a new tribe came to worship her. She paid them no heed until, more than 1,500 years ago, the boy Ruu's song pierced the clouds. She landed beside him, he gave her the name "Kanna Kapatcir" (Great Eagle of the Storm), and he promised to sing for her again. When she returned she found him dead, sacrificed by his own people, his blood in a ritual cup. To her this was the murder of an innocent and a broken promise. She razed the tribe with lightning and cursed the island to repeat its last days until she heard his song again. She then flew to Seirai Island, where Ei later killed her.

In Through the Mists (2.2) the Traveler took Sumida's commission and crossed to Tsurumi in Kama's boat. They met Ruu and learned the truth from Kama. They destroyed the Perches to stop the ceremony and defeated a Thunder Manifestation on Mt. Kanna. Through the Peculiar Pinion found on Seirai, they saw that only Ruu's song would end the curse. The Traveler and Paimon told Ruu that the Thunderbird had "moved" to Seirai rather than reveal she was dead, though on seeing the ruins of Amakumo Peak he understood what had happened and did not blame them. With the Pinion's power they brought him there, he sang, and the curse lifted. Ruu chose to rest on the island for a while before passing on.

Atmosphere: Before the curse lifted: silence, grey fog that turned travellers around, and illusory villagers who acted strangely and vanished between visits. During the final confrontation the fog turned red and crimson lightning struck. Afterwards: open grass, waves, wind over ruined platforms, and the occasional spirit asking a stranger for one last favour.

Dangers: The fog once teleported intruders back to the island's edge. Riftwolves, Thundercraven rifthounds, hilichurls, Abyss Mages and Ruin automatons roam today. A Thunder Manifestation formed from the Thunderbird's rage appeared in the hollow of Mt. Kanna.

Gameplay note: Tsurumi runs on a three-day cycle that changes enemy and chest placement, and Remarkable Chests were introduced here.

Travel: Tsurumi lies apart from the main islands and was reached by boat with Kama's help. Before the questline, only the southern peninsula and the eastern isles near the Statue of The Seven could be reached.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the curse and the fog are gone, and the island's spirits are moving on with the Boatman. Tsurumi remains uninhabited. No Tsurumi-specific content appears in 6.x-7.1.

226.comment: Tsurumi Island: Ruu and the Thunderbird
226.content: Ruu was a boy of Tsurumi's Thunderbird tribe whose song drew down the Thunderbird. He named her Kanna Kapatcir and promised to sing for her again. Believing his sacrifice would set things right for his people, he let himself be sacrificed. She saw it as murder and a broken promise, destroyed the tribe, and bound the island in a looping curse until she could hear his song again. Through the loop Ruu lived on as an aware illusion. In 2.2 the Traveler, with Kama, helped him understand what she had wanted and brought him to Seirai to sing, ending the curse.

227.comment: Tsurumi Island: The First Civilisation of Tsurumi
227.content: Beneath Tsurumi lie ruins older than the Thunderbird tribe. They belong to the ancient unified civilisation, which was connected to Celestia and worshipped the Three Moons. Its murals depict Celestia, and Ruin Sentinels guard its halls. Kapatcir remembered strange objects falling from the heavens and creating the fog. The novelist Sumida guessed that something fell from Celestia, and Kama suspects it disturbed the island's ley lines. Nothing found on the island confirms what fell.

228.content:
Tsurumi Underground Ruins: The Tsurumi Underground Ruins are a network of caverns beneath Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. They link Shirikoro Peak, whose entrance is at the mountain's base under a Perch, with Chirai Shrine, whose entrance is beneath its ruins. They hold remains of the Thunderbird Civilization and of an even earlier civilization, together with murals.

The murals and torch puzzles are the main clues to a human civilization that predates the Thunderbird's worshippers. Ruin machines guard the halls.

Geography: Long underground passages between the two entrances, with a mural room, a submerged room and several Ruins Torches. Mysterious Carvings can be used to reveal hidden murals.

The Shirikoro Peak side also contains Seelie courts and seven Stone Slates can be used in the cavern between the peak and Chirai Shrine.

Places: The Mural Room holds three mountain murals: Shirikoro Peak on the left, the mountain on the road to the Moshiri Ceremonial Site in the middle, and Mt. Kanna on the right. Other murals near the Ruins Torches indicate puzzle solutions, and carvings reveal one beside the submerged room.

Each mountain mural is marked with a star-shaped slot; the Star-Shaped Gems found during the hidden objective "Opening Old Memories" can be placed in them. The murals are lettered in Ancient Teyvat Script.

History: Long ago a unified human civilization existed across Teyvat, including Tsurumi Island, and left murals through the underground ruins. Above it, over 1,500 years ago, the Thunderbird Civilization settled the island and worshipped Kanna Kapatcir; its people were later destroyed after the sacrifice of Ruu.

The Unified Civilization page, citing a line in The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna, says the earlier Tsurumi civilization worshipped the Three Moons and that, as elsewhere, ships carried the dead to the Golden Hall on the moon. It adds that an object fell from the heavens and landed on the island, after which fog appeared. The wiki Tsurumi Island page describes the earlier civilization as buried deep underground, before the time of the Thunderbird's reign.

Atmosphere: Dark halls, glowing Electro ruins and faded murals. A sense of an earlier world, older than the island's ceremonies, that no one now remembers.

Dangers: Elite Ruin Cruisers, Ruin Destroyers, Ruin Sentinels and Ruin Scouts. Some areas are flooded; Electro current puzzles and torch puzzles block doors.

Travel: Enter at Shirikoro Peak (base of the mountain beneath the Perch) or from beneath Chirai Shrine's ruins. The A Particularly Particular Author steps show how to open the Shirikoro entrance.

Quests: Gameplay note: three Ruins Torch puzzles require the Peculiar Pinion gadget from Octave of the Maushiro (2.2). Solving them is a prerequisite for the achievement "Guessing Game". The hidden objective "Tsurumi's Mountain Murals" begins here and needs the Pinion and the three Star-Shaped Gems.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins are abandoned. The Thunderbird's curse was lifted in 2.2, and no later content adds to the site.

229.comment: Tsurumi Underground Ruins: Tsurumi Mountain Murals
229.content: In the hidden exploration objective, the Traveler places the three Star-Shaped Gems in the mountain murals of the underground ruins. Electro Seelie fly out and mark the locations, at Mt. Kanna, Shirikoro Peak and the mountain on the way to the Moshiri Ceremonial Site, each guiding the player to a spot. Completing it gives an Exquisite Chest and then a Luxurious Chest, and is a prerequisite for the achievement "Guessing Game".

230.content:
Uyuu Restaurant (also: Uyuu-tei, Uyuu Pagoda): Uyuu Restaurant is a tavern-style restaurant on the commercial street of Tenryou in Inazuma City, owned by Okazaki Rikuto, who calls it an izakaya, with Okazaki Erika cooking and serving. A bulletin board beside the entrance carries messages from regular customers, including General Gorou. Its Japanese name Uyuu-tei is written with characters that echo a Chinese word for "nothing" or "nonexistence".

The owner is a retired figure of the Tenryou Commission who still gets visits from yoriki and doushin. Patrons use the bulletin board to thank him, tease him, ask him for favours and leave letters and gifts in his keeping, and he answers them there.

Places: Uyuu Restaurant has a ground floor with tables and an upstairs with a mural. A bulletin board stands by the entrance, and an aged temari, a children's ball with scars and burrs, sits by a table; the name Okazaki Seishimaru is written on it. Outside, the food critic Matsumoto can usually be found.

The temari raises two questions in the Traveler's mind: whether it has been there all along or was found and placed there by someone. Erika takes orders at the restaurant, while Rikuto sits and drinks sake, saying that after a busy life he is owed a drink or two.

People: Rikuto is the owner, an older man who was once with the Tenryou Commission and says he had a stand-up reputation there; yoriki and doushin still ask his advice. He praises Erika's cooking as among the best in Inazuma City, drinks sake at the restaurant and tells a young Traveler there is no hurry about drinking. Erika is the cook. When asked how they met, she says it is a long story: when she was young she was ordered to watch an important figure at the Tenryou Commission, and she thanks the archons he eventually retired so they could marry.

Matsumoto, a travelling food critic found outside, rates Uyuu and Kiminami Restaurants both mediocre; he prefers plain food and says he can only give fair reviews if food is given to him rather than paid for. Rikuto notes that major figures from headquarters have visited recently and that something seems afoot in Inazuma; asked about politics, he says the Tenryou Commission believes in the power of the Almighty Shogun, who must have her reasons, and that a traveller from afar need not worry.

Governance: It is a private business owned by a retired Tenryou Commission man. Customers include officials, soldiers and travellers, judging by the messages left there.

The Tenryou Commission and the Sakoku Decree touch the restaurant through its patrons. A message from someone close to the Tenryou Commissioner thanks Rikuto for his guidance, while a customer asks him whether his status at the Commission could help him find a way round the decree to get Dandelion Wine; Rikuto answers that there is no such way.

Culture: The bulletin board is the restaurant's best-known institution, a place where people leave messages and the owner answers them. The messages are sometimes comic and sometimes moving.

Examples from the board: Arataki Itto threatens Kujou Sara, the "tengu of the Kujou Clan", over taking his Vision and says he will await their duel; Rikuto replies that whatever Sara did, Itto is welcome to relax there. Beidou praises Rikuto's friendliness and the wine, and Rikuto asks for stories of Haishan. Madarame Hyakubei apologises to the Kamisato Clan for furniture damaged by his drunk son. Yae Miko thanks him for the sakura wine and mochi and notes that the wine tasted different; he says he prepared it specially. Ogura Yuu leaves a message that he is being stationed at Tatarasuna, and worries for his sister Ogura Mio's business. General Gorou and his people accidentally reveal in a message that they were conducting secret surveillance, and Rikuto notes nothing was actually removed.

History: The restaurant is first mentioned in Someone's Drifting Bottle, a message found in the world from version 1.2. The bottle's note, written by Hiromi to Yan'er, asks whether she remembers Uyuu Restaurant, says they will meet there and encloses money for wine. In the 2.0 world quest "Hiromi's Watch" the Traveler delivers the bottle's contents to Yan'er, who says the restaurant seems a fine place and that she will go there for drinks, and the Traveler later reminds Hiromi of the name.

Shun, one of Hiromi's old friends, says the three had a drink at Uyuu Restaurant the day before the Sakoku Decree took effect; Yan'er left Inazuma, he says, because of the decree. This ties the restaurant to the era of the decree.

Atmosphere: A drinking house with sake on the table, a bulletin board crowded with notes and a landlord who greets customers as youngsters. The board's messages show soldiers, adventurers and officials passing through under the shadow of the Sakoku Decree.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the restaurant is open under Rikuto and Erika; the board has Sakoku-era messages plus ones added after Radiant Sakura.

231.content: Rikuto is the owner of Uyuu Restaurant, a retired Tenryou Commission man who drinks sake at his own table. He answers the board's messages in person-to-person replies, calls young customers youngsters, offers barbecued skewers, and says Seishimaru was once a relative. His exact former rank is not stated.

232.content: Erika is the cook and waitress at Uyuu Restaurant, who welcomes customers and takes orders. She was once assigned to keep watch on an important Tenryou Commission figure, who later retired, and is implied to be Rikuto's wife.

233.comment: Uyuu Restaurant: Someone's Drifting Bottle and Hiromi
233.content: A drifting bottle found in waters southeast of Dragonspine holds a letter to a lost friend suggesting a reunion at Uyuu Restaurant with money for wine. The Traveler carries it to Hiromi, then to Yan'er, who says she does not know any officer who catches thieves but may go for drinks. Shun, the third friend, says the three drank at Uyuu the day before the Sakoku Decree took effect.

key: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon
234.comment: Uyuu Restaurant: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon Cameo
234.content: In the limited-time 7.1 event "Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon" (24 September to 12 October 2026), Rikuto, Erika and Matsumoto appear in the event's cast. Rikuto says it feels like being young again, and Erika wonders how long it has been since they took a trip together, suggesting they cook another hundred dishes together. Matsumoto notes that the food is seasoned boldly and says he will talk to Anna when he gets back. The event is canon but time-limited.

235.content:
Violet Court: Violet Court is a Domain of Mastery in Kannazuka, Inazuma, an altar where violet sakura bloom eternal. Its description recounts that in the ancient past the mountains rose higher than the sky and the earth was larger than the dome of heaven, until the mirror shattered and the oceans arose; in these legends the court of the primeval sakura was severed from the other islands. Monsters now storm the altar.

Clearing it yields Talent level-up materials (the Transience, Elegance and Light series by weekday). It was added in Version 2.0. The enemies are Electro-themed: Hilichurls, Nobushi, Treasure Hoarders and, at the top level, the Kairagi pair.

Geography: An island of Kannazuka with a sakura-ringed altar. The domain entrance island appears on the map once the Statue of The Seven on Narukami Island is unlocked, even though the domain belongs to Kannazuka.

Two Electro Crystalfruits stand at the arena's sides in the challenge; during the fight they occasionally produce Nascent Electro Pearls.

Dangers: Hilichurls and Electro Hilichurl Grenadiers and Shooters, Crackling Axe Mitachurls, Nobushi (Jintouban, Hitsukeban, Kikouban), Treasure Hoarders, and at level IV the Kairagi: Fiery Might and Kairagi: Dancing Thunder.

In-game, collecting Nascent Electro Pearls makes attacks release Falling Thunder, a true Electro damage effect, and all characters gain a 25% Electro DMG Bonus. At level IV the two Kairagi heal and strengthen each other if one falls first, so they must be defeated together. This is game mechanics, not story.

History: Only legend: the sakura court was cut off when the mirror shattered (the wiki links the wording to the war of the funerary flame, but the domain itself gives no names). The Sacred Sakura on Mt. Yougou is the better-known primeval sakura in Inazuma.

236.content:
Vishap Research Lab (also: Bathysmal Vishap research site, Byakuyakoku research lab): The Vishap Research Lab is a hidden laboratory of ancient Byakuyakoku in Enkanomiya, where researchers studied and bred Bathysmal Vishaps (the "Dragonheirs of the Depths") under the personal direction of Watatsumi Omikami. It does not appear on the map. The Traveler can reach it through a phase gate on the small island north of the Dainichi Mikoshi and finds there the afterimage of a researcher called Michiya, who guards the experiment records.

The lab is the starting point of the world quest "Tricolor File", which yields the Bathysmal Vishap Experimental Records, one of the five lost books in "Collection of Dragons and Snakes". Its text shows a programme of controlled breeding, intelligence tests and blood-grafting that was meant to protect Enkanomiya from a prophecy, and whose staff disagreed about whether to keep or burn the results.

Geography: The lab lies outside the ordinary Enkanomiya map. To reach it, go to the small island north of the Dainichi Mikoshi, either by gliding down from the northmost waypoint of the Dainichi Mikoshi or by gliding from the ghostfish cluster at the far east of The Narrows, and then use the Phase Gate at the island's northmost point.

Inside are a restricted area, an experimental site and a locked cell. An elemental monument must be activated (it uses Cryo energy) to open the cell that holds the experiment records and a captive Rimebiter Bathysmal Vishap Hatchling. The wiki lists the hatchling as the area's elite enemy.

People: The only resident is Michiya, the afterimage of a researcher of the lab, one of the Shades of Tokoyo. The quest that begins with him can only be started during Evernight. Like most shades he is a translucent figure without distinguishing features and does not seem to realise he is only an afterimage; Paimon notes it in an aside.

Michiya speaks as if it were still the eve of the exodus: he says this is the third group the others have sent to him on Enkanomiya's last day, assumes visitors are either Jibashiri or retainers sent by Sangonomiya, and says he will stay in the restricted zone until it is time to leave to keep anyone from approaching. He says he will probably have to change his name once he reaches the surface and begins a new life, because "our wrongdoings are not so easily wiped away".

Governance: The programme was directed by Watatsumi Omikami in person. The records say the research team was split between those who wanted to burn the records and those who wanted to save them for a later generation that might forgive them. Michiya favoured burning but accepted the hidden-records compromise.

The records set strict house rules: from a certain day, experiments were to be directed by Omikami; files from before the founding year of the Watatsumi calendar were destroyed; serial numbers were to use Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Ether and Void instead of the ancient Alpha-to-Epsilon categories; authors could be left unnamed or given by internal lab title, with ancient Byakuyakoku names and modern Watatsumi, Narukami or Inazuman names forbidden; and the records were not to be used for diaries, love letters or fantasy novels.

History: The records describe a programme on the Dragonheirs of the Depths. Researchers raised vishaps in altered environments and found they could awaken or generate traits for their descendants: a heat-resistant vishap raised in cold gave offspring with more body fat, more sleep and the Cryo element, while descendants returned to heat chose heat resistance again without gaining Pyro. After four generations the vishaps' language ability approached that of a twelve-year-old student, and the writer argued the experiments should stop, citing the prophecy that the Dragon Sovereign of Water would be born in human form, which they did not want to happen in Enkanomiya.

Under Omikami's special orders, researchers tried grafting its blood onto vishaps. Early attempts failed because the vishaps could not accept the blood. A later round counted as a success, with the rejection explained by the vishaps being creatures of the Light Realm (elemental beings), at odds with the Human Realm of Omikami and its coral vassals. The log closes with the claim that no vishap died in the experiments and that all lived out their days.

Atmosphere: A cold, enclosed research site of cells, an experiment area and an elemental monument, visited in the blue dark of Evernight, when the quest can be started. The sense is of scientists who ended their work with guilt and left a time capsule they could neither burn nor publish.

Dangers: The locked cell holds a Rimebiter Bathysmal Vishap Hatchling that is released when the elemental monument is lit. Bathysmal Vishaps hate man-made light and can drain a fighter's energy or, if energy runs out, health. Paimon warns that lighting the monument will summon dangerous vishaps, so prepare first.

Quests: "Tricolor File" (World Quest, 2.4; requires "The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent"): speak to Michiya, then light the Cryo monument to open the cell and obtain the Bathysmal Vishap Experimental Records. The records can be obtained without the quest. "Collection of Dragons and Snakes" requires them: Ema, an afterimage in The Narrows library, wants five lost books returned, and handing in the records contributes the fourth volume of The Byakuyakoku Collection.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the lab is unchanged: a hidden, abandoned Enkanomiya site whose records are in the Traveler's archive. No content from 5.x to 7.1 mentions it. Enkanomiya itself is little known outside Inazuma.

237.comment: Vishap Research Lab: The Bathysmal Vishap Experimental Records
237.content: Volume 4 of The Byakuyakoku Collection. It is signed with no individual name and kept in the file numbering that mixes Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Ether and Void categories. It contains the evolution experiments, the intelligence study, and the grafting trials directed by Watatsumi Omikami. The final entry praises Omikami as "gracious and beneficent" and notes that none of the Dragonheirs died in the experiments. Volume 5 in the same collection, a puzzle book for children, echoes the same prophecy and warns against making vishaps sound adorable lest children lower their guard.

238.content: Michiya is a Shade of Tokoyo, the afterimage of a researcher of the Vishap Research Lab. He speaks as one who feels guilt and duty: he will keep watch until departure, believes the research team did wrong, and will not give the records away easily. After "Tricolor File" he refuses to say more. He expects that he and his colleagues are about to start a new life above the surface.

239.content:
Wakukau Shoal (also: Wakukau-hama): Wakukau Shoal is a shoreline subarea of Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. It has little lore of its own, but in the world quest The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna it is the first place where the Traveler uses the Thunderbird feather on a Mysterious Carving and is drawn into a memory of Kanna Kapatcir.

It is part of the search for the boy Ruu, who is not found here.

Geography: A rocky shoreline with a rock arch, a large camp site and cliffs above. Mysterious Carvings and a Thunder Sakura Bough stand here, and Sea Ganoderma grows along the shore.

Hilichurl camps, including one led by an Electro Samachurl, and Ruin Guards occupy the area. They rearrange themselves over the three days of Tsurumi's cycle: a Thunderhelm Lawachurl, Hydro slimes and Samachurls on day one; Thundercraven Rifthound whelps and a Rifthound with the Ruin Guards nearby on day two; and several Rifthounds, with the Ruin Guards active, on day three.

History: Using the feather here summons two waves of monsters, ending with a Thunderhelm Lawachurl. A voice asks where someone is, and the feather that drops shows the Traveler a vision from the Thunderbird's view of Tsurumi Island under fog. She hears the voices of boars, humans, squirrels, lizards and Wen Kamuy, and then a clear song in the rain, unlike the war songs of the boars and the choruses of the fish.

The feather flies up to Mt. Kanna. Kama and Paimon agree the voice sounded as if the Thunderbird were searching for someone, and the party moves on to Oina Beach.

Quests: The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna (2.2): the first of three feather sites, followed by Oina Beach and the Autake Plains.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Electro Samachurls, Hydro slimes, Ruin Guards and Thundercraven Rifthounds, depending on the day.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no later canon read for this entry changes the shoal.

240.content:
